naics.description: The National Society of Professional Engineers (NSPE) is a U.S. professional membership association representing licensed professional engineers across disciplines and industries. It advocates on licensure, ethics, and public-policy issues affecting the engineering profession, and provides continuing education and credentialing resources to members. NSPE is headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia.
naics.justification: NSPE's core activity is operating a membership association for licensed engineers that advances professional standards and advocacy, matching the Professional Organizations code rather than any engineering-service or manufacturing code.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Considered because the org serves professionals, but NSPE itself does not sell professional services to clients.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all that fits less precisely than the dedicated Professional Organizations code.
NSPE offers continuing education, but training is a secondary activity, not its primary purpose.

naics.category_justification: NSPE is a membership body representing and advocating for professional engineers, the defining trait of a trade/professional association.

naics.description: Arm (Arm Holdings plc) is a British semiconductor and software design company that develops microprocessor architectures and licenses this intellectual property to chipmakers such as Apple, Qualcomm, and Samsung rather than manufacturing chips itself. It earns revenue through upfront licensing fees and per-chip royalties from partners building products on Arm-based designs. Arm's technology underpins the majority of the world's smartphones and a large share of embedded and IoT devices.
naics.justification: Arm's primary activity is designing semiconductor processor architectures and licensing them for use in chips; NAICS groups fabless/design-only semiconductor firms under this manufacturing code even though Arm does not physically fabricate devices, but the fit is imperfect given its pure-licensing model.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Arm's core work is engineering R&D on processor architectures, which this code also captures well.
Arm licenses IP and some software tooling, but its output is chip-architecture IP rather than packaged software products.

alternates.naics_title: Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: Ruled out because Arm does not distribute physical computer hardware or software products through wholesale channels.

naics.category_justification: Arm is a publicly traded, for-profit technology company commenting on its own commercial interests, not a membership or advocacy body.

naics.resolved_name: Medical Imaging & Technology Alliance (a division of the National Electrical Manufacturers Association)
naics.description: The Medical Imaging & Technology Alliance (MITA) is a trade association, historically operated as a division of the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA), representing manufacturers of medical imaging equipment such as MRI, CT, ultrasound, and PET systems. It advocates on regulatory, reimbursement, and standards issues affecting the medical imaging industry and represents companies accounting for the large majority of the global imaging-equipment market. MITA member companies include major device makers like GE HealthCare, Siemens Healthineers, and Philips.
naics.justification: MITA's primary activity is representing and advocating for its member manufacturers on industry-wide regulatory and standards issues, which fits a trade-association code; it was scored just under the associations-specific alternative because MITA specifically represents businesses/manufacturers rather than individual professionals.

alternates.justification: MITA represents manufacturer companies (businesses) rather than individual professionals, which arguably fits this code better.
Ruled out because MITA itself does not manufacture imaging devices; it represents the companies that do.
Ruled out because MITA is not a clinical imaging-service provider.

naics.category_justification: MITA is an industry trade association representing medical-imaging equipment manufacturers' collective interests.

normalized_name: alliance for artificial intelligence in healthcare
display_name: The Alliance for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

refs.raw_name: The Alliance for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

naics.resolved_name: The Alliance for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare (AAIH)
naics.description: The Alliance for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare (AAIH) is a Washington, D.C.-based multi-stakeholder advocacy organization launched in 2019 that promotes scientific, legislative, and regulatory initiatives to support the development and adoption of AI-powered healthcare solutions. Its membership spans biopharma, diagnostics, device manufacturers, AI start-ups, and research institutions, including companies such as Google and Roche. AAIH runs working groups on regulatory and data policy issues affecting health AI.
naics.justification: AAIH's primary activity is coordinating advocacy and policy engagement among its member organizations working on health AI, which best matches a professional/industry-association code, though its cross-sector membership (biopharma, tech, research) makes the fit inexact.

alternates.justification: Its membership is composed largely of businesses, so a business-association code is a close competing fit.
AAIH's regulatory advocacy work has a social-advocacy character, though it centers on member commercial interests rather than public-interest advocacy.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Ruled out because AAIH itself does not conduct R&D; it coordinates policy activity among members who do.

naics.category_justification: AAIH is a membership-based multi-stakeholder coalition advocating for its member organizations' shared interest in health AI policy.

naics.description: The National Information Standards Organization (NISO) is a nonprofit, ANSI-accredited standards development organization that creates and maintains technical standards for managing information in libraries, publishing, and information technology. Founded in 1939 and incorporated as a nonprofit in 1983, NISO's standards are developed through consensus among member organizations and are freely published. NISO also represents U.S. interests on international information-standards committees.
naics.justification: NISO's core activity is developing consensus technical standards through a membership of publishing, library, and IT organizations, which is closest to a professional/standards-association code, though NAICS has no code specific to standards-development bodies.

alternates.justification: NISO's members are largely organizations (publishers, vendors) whose collective interests it serves, resembling a business association.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Considered because standards work resembles technical consulting, but NISO does not provide consulting services for fees.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; NISO is not an information-service provider, it sets standards used by such providers.

naics.category_justification: NISO is organized and operates as a nonprofit standards-development body rather than a for-profit company or government unit, though its consensus, member-driven process also has trade-association characteristics.

naics.description: The Pharmacy Health Information Technology (HIT) Collaborative is a coalition of national pharmacy organizations, formed in 2010, that advocates for integrating pharmacists' patient-care services into interoperable health information technology systems. Its founding members include major pharmacy associations such as APhA, ASHP, and AACP, along with associate members from e-prescribing networks and technology vendors. The Collaborative develops standards and policy positions supporting pharmacist-provided care within electronic health record systems.
naics.justification: The Collaborative's activity is coordinating pharmacy-profession advocacy and standards work among member pharmacy associations, which best fits a professional-association code even though it is itself a coalition of associations rather than individual members.

alternates.justification: Its founding members are professional associations rather than businesses, making this a weaker fit than Professional Organizations.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback considered but less precise than the dedicated professional-organizations code.
Ruled out; the Collaborative sets policy and standards recommendations but does not build software.

naics.category_justification: It is a coalition of pharmacy professional associations advocating collectively for pharmacists' role in health IT, matching the multi-stakeholder coalition definition.

naics.description: The Cyberlaw Clinic is a legal clinic operated jointly by Harvard Law School's Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society, providing law students with hands-on experience representing clients on technology, internet, and intellectual-property law matters, including public-interest amicus and rulemaking comments. Students work under faculty supervision on real cases involving digital rights, privacy, and emerging technology policy. It is part of Harvard University's academic and clinical legal education program.
naics.justification: The Cyberlaw Clinic is a clinical teaching program of Harvard Law School, so its primary activity is part of the university's educational mission, matching the higher-education code used for the parent institution.

alternates.justification: Considered because the clinic provides legal representation, but it operates as a teaching unit of the law school rather than a law firm.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback ruled out because the clinic is clearly a university teaching unit, not a freestanding association.
Ruled out; the clinic's docket work is broader technology-policy litigation support, not a dedicated human-rights mission, and it is not an independent nonprofit.

naics.category_justification: The Clinic is a sub-unit of Harvard Law School, part of Harvard University, an degree-granting institution, and the record refers to the institution's own clinical program.

naics.description: Business Roundtable is a U.S. trade association whose membership consists of chief executive officers of major American companies. It advocates for public policies that its member CEOs believe will foster economic growth and promote a strong U.S. economy, engaging on issues including tax, trade, technology, and regulatory policy. The organization is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
naics.justification: Business Roundtable's defining activity is representing the collective policy interests of its CEO membership, the core definition of a business association.
naics.category_justification: It is explicitly a membership organization of corporate CEOs organized to advocate on shared business-policy interests.

naics.resolved_name: Data Coalition (an initiative of the Data Foundation)
naics.description: The Data Coalition is a membership-based policy initiative, now operated under the nonprofit Data Foundation, that advocates for open, high-quality, and accessible government data and evidence-based public policy. Its members include companies and organizations with a stake in federal data policy, including issues affecting AI and data analytics. The Coalition engages in legislative and regulatory advocacy on data-management and transparency issues.
naics.justification: The Data Coalition's core activity is advocating on data policy on behalf of its member organizations, closest to a business/trade association code, though it operates under a nonprofit parent (Data Foundation) which blurs the trade-vs-nonprofit line.

alternates.justification: Its public-interest framing around open government data has an advocacy-organization character.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Considered given its policy-research activities, but it is not a fee-for-service consultancy.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; despite the 'Data' name, the Coalition does not provide data processing or hosting services itself.

naics.category_justification: It is a membership-based coalition representing organizations' shared interest in data policy, even though it is structurally housed within the nonprofit Data Foundation.

naics.description: The Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA) is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing large and small companies in the computer, internet, information technology, and telecommunications industries. Founded in 1972, it advocates before Congress, regulatory agencies, and courts on issues including antitrust, intellectual property, and technology policy on behalf of its member companies. Members have included major technology firms such as Google, Meta, and Amazon.
naics.justification: CCIA's core activity is representing member technology and telecom companies' collective policy interests, the defining function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: CCIA is explicitly a membership trade association representing the tech and communications industry.

naics.description: Google LLC is a multinational technology company and subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. best known for its internet search engine, and it also operates advertising, cloud computing, consumer hardware, and software services including Android, YouTube, and Google Workspace. Headquartered in Mountain View, California, Google is one of the largest technology companies in the world and has been an active commenter on federal AI and technology policy. Its core revenue remains driven by internet search and digital advertising.
naics.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
naics.justification: Google's flagship and historically primary activity is operating an internet search engine and related information services, matching the search-portal code, though its diversified businesses (cloud, advertising, hardware) mean no single NAICS code fully captures the company.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Google Cloud is a large and growing segment, making this a plausible alternate primary activity.
Digital advertising is Google's dominant revenue source, though it is sold as an ad-placement/search service rather than agency creative work.
Google develops substantial custom software, but this is not its primary revenue-generating activity.

naics.category_justification: Google is a for-profit corporation commenting on technology policy in its own commercial interest.

normalized_name: center for human-compatible ai future of life institute center for long-term cybersecurity and future society
display_name: Center for Human-Compatible AI, Future of Life Institute, Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity, & The Future Society

refs.raw_name: Center for Human-Compatible AI, Future of Life Institute, Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity, & The Future Society

naics.resolved_name: Center for Human-Compatible AI, Future of Life Institute, Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity, & The Future Society (joint comment)
naics.description: This record represents a joint public comment filed together by four separate AI-safety and technology-policy research organizations: the Center for Human-Compatible AI (a UC Berkeley research center), the Future of Life Institute (an independent nonprofit focused on existential and AI risk), the Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity (a UC Berkeley research center), and The Future Society (an independent nonprofit AI governance organization). Each organization separately conducts research and advocacy on AI safety, governance, and long-term risk, and they co-signed shared policy recommendations to federal AI regulators. Because the four are legally distinct entities that only co-filed a comment, no single NAICS code or category can fully represent them.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: The signatories are primarily AI-policy and AI-safety research organizations (two of them university-affiliated research centers, two independent nonprofits), so social-science/policy R&D is the closest single code, but confidence is low because this record actually bundles four distinct organizations with different structures (two are university centers, two are independent nonprofits) rather than one entity.

alternates.justification: The Future of Life Institute and The Future Society function as advocacy-oriented nonprofits on AI governance, fitting this code for those two entities.
The Center for Human-Compatible AI and the Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity are UC Berkeley research centers, which would code as part of the university for those two entities.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Some of the groups' AI-safety research has a technical/engineering character that could fit this R&D code instead of the social-sciences one.

naics.category_justification: The record conflates four legally distinct organizations (two university research centers and two independent nonprofits) into one line, so no single category can be assigned with confidence without splitting the entities.

naics.description: ForHumanity is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization focused on examining and mitigating the risks of AI and autonomous systems in areas including ethics, bias, privacy, trust, and cybersecurity. It develops independent audit and certification criteria for AI systems, drawing on a global community of volunteer contributors, and trains certified auditors through its education programs. ForHumanity engages with regulators such as the Federal Reserve and European authorities to promote independent AI oversight.
naics.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
naics.justification: ForHumanity's core activity is developing and administering independent audit/certification criteria and training for AI systems, a specialized professional-services-like function that does not map to any more specific NAICS code.

alternates.justification: Its mission to promote AI accountability and public trust has a social-advocacy character.
ForHumanity trains and certifies AI auditors, which is itself a training/education activity.
Its audit/certification work resembles third-party testing and certification services, though ForHumanity does not itself perform the audits.

naics.category_justification: ForHumanity is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit pursuing a public-interest mission (independent AI oversight) rather than membership advocacy or a for-profit service.

naics.description: Adobe Inc. is an American multinational software company best known for creative and document software products such as Photoshop, Illustrator, and Acrobat, delivered primarily through subscription-based cloud services. It also provides digital marketing and analytics software through its Experience Cloud business. Adobe is headquartered in San Jose, California, and is a major participant in federal technology and AI policy discussions.
naics.justification: Adobe's primary activity is developing and licensing packaged and cloud-delivered software products, the defining activity of the Software Publishers code.
naics.category_justification: Adobe is a publicly traded for-profit software company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: Amnesty International USA is the U.S. section of Amnesty International, a global nonprofit human-rights movement that researches, documents, and campaigns against human-rights abuses worldwide. It engages in advocacy, public education, and grassroots mobilization on issues including surveillance technology, AI, and civil liberties. Amnesty International USA is headquartered in New York and Washington, D.C.
naics.justification: Amnesty International USA's core mission and activity is human-rights research and advocacy, matching this code exactly.
naics.category_justification: It is a nonprofit human-rights organization pursuing a public-interest advocacy mission rather than representing a paying membership's commercial interests.

naics.description: BSA | The Software Alliance is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing the global software industry, with members including major enterprise software and cloud companies such as Microsoft, Adobe, and IBM. It advocates on policy issues including cybersecurity, data privacy, intellectual property, and AI regulation, and also conducts anti-piracy enforcement on behalf of members. BSA was founded in 1988.
naics.justification: BSA's primary activity is representing member software companies' collective policy interests before governments, the defining function of a business association, though its historical anti-piracy enforcement role adds a secondary function that keeps confidence just under the high-certainty threshold.

alternates.justification: Considered because BSA represents an industry, but its members are companies rather than individual professionals.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; BSA does not sell professional services to clients.
Ruled out; BSA itself does not publish software, it represents companies that do.

naics.category_justification: BSA is explicitly a membership trade association for the software industry.

naics.description: ACT | The App Association is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing thousands of small and mid-size software application development companies. It advocates on policy issues affecting the mobile app economy, including intellectual property, privacy, and AI regulation, and provides resources to help member companies navigate the connected-technology marketplace. The association is affiliated with the industry group CompTIA.
naics.justification: The App Association's core activity is representing app-developer companies' collective policy interests, the defining function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: It is explicitly structured as a membership trade association for app-development businesses.

naics.description: Kaiser Permanente is a large American nonprofit integrated managed-care consortium consisting of the Kaiser Foundation Health Plan, Kaiser Foundation Hospitals, and affiliated Permanente Medical Groups. It provides health insurance coverage and operates hospitals and medical facilities serving over 12 million members, primarily in the western United States. Kaiser Permanente is headquartered in Oakland, California.
naics.justification: Kaiser Permanente operates a system of hospitals and medical facilities as part of its integrated care model, which best characterizes its primary activity, though it is simultaneously a major health insurer, making a single code an imperfect fit for its integrated payer-provider structure.

alternates.naics_title: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers
alternates.justification: Kaiser Foundation Health Plan's core function is underwriting and administering health insurance coverage for its members.
Kaiser's integrated HMO model, combining insurance and directly employed physician groups, closely matches this specific code.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: The affiliated Permanente Medical Groups are physician practices, though this undercounts the hospital and insurance components.

naics.category_justification: Kaiser Foundation Health Plan and Kaiser Foundation Hospitals are structured as nonprofit entities delivering a public-interest healthcare mission, distinguishing it from a standard for-profit insurer or hospital chain.

naics.description: Accenture plc is a multinational professional services company providing management consulting, technology, and outsourcing services to clients across industries and government. Headquartered in Dublin, Ireland (with major U.S. operations), it is one of the largest consulting and IT services firms in the world and has been active in AI strategy and implementation consulting for clients. Accenture is publicly traded and organized around consulting, technology, and operations service lines.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: Accenture's primary activity is providing management and business consulting services to clients, matching this code, though a substantial share of its revenue also comes from technology/systems implementation work covered by a closely related code.

alternates.justification: A large share of Accenture's revenue comes from technology implementation and systems integration, a close competing primary activity.
Considered as a narrower consulting-services alternative to the general management consulting code.
Custom software development is part of Accenture's technology services but is not its overall primary activity.

naics.category_justification: Accenture is a publicly traded, for-profit professional-services firm commenting in its own capacity, not on behalf of unnamed clients.

naics.description: IBM (International Business Machines Corporation) is a multinational technology company providing enterprise hardware, software, and consulting services, including cloud computing, AI (Watson), and IT infrastructure. Headquartered in Armonk, New York, IBM has shifted heavily toward hybrid cloud and software/consulting revenue in recent years while retaining legacy computer-hardware and mainframe businesses. It is a long-time participant in federal technology and AI policy discussions.
naics.justification: IBM's current business mix is dominated by enterprise software, cloud, and IT consulting/systems-integration services rather than hardware manufacturing, making systems-design services the best single-code fit, though its diversified hardware, software, and consulting lines make no single code fully precise.

alternates.justification: IBM's software segment (including Red Hat) is a major and growing revenue source, making software publishing a strong alternate primary activity.
IBM's historical core business was computer/mainframe hardware manufacturing, still a meaningful segment.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: IBM Consulting is a large business line providing management and strategy consulting alongside technology implementation.

naics.category_justification: IBM is a publicly traded, for-profit technology corporation commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: Artis Technologies was an Atlanta-based financial technology company that built a real-time, API-based lending and point-of-sale financing platform, using alternative data and machine-learning-informed decisioning to generate loan offers for consumers at the point of purchase, initially in home-improvement and later healthcare financing. In January 2022 the company rebranded as Momnt. It operated as a technology provider to banks and merchants rather than as a direct lender itself.
naics.justification: Artis Technologies' primary product is a proprietary lending-decisioning software platform licensed to banks and merchants, which best fits a software-publishing code, though its close involvement in loan origination and financial-transaction processing makes a finance-sector code a plausible alternative.

alternates.naics_title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities
alternates.justification: The company's platform processes point-of-sale loan transactions between lenders and merchants, closely matching this financial-processing code.

alternates.naics_title: International, Secondary Market, and All Other Nondepository Credit Intermediation
alternates.justification: Its role in facilitating consumer credit offers gives it characteristics of a nondepository credit intermediary.
The company builds custom decisioning software, though it markets a standardized licensed platform rather than bespoke programming services.

naics.category_justification: Artis Technologies (Momnt) is a for-profit venture-backed fintech company commenting on its own commercial interest in AI-driven lending technology.

naics.description: NCTA - The Internet & Television Association is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing the U.S. cable television and broadband internet industry. Its members include major cable operators and programmers, and it advocates on policy issues including broadband deployment, telecommunications regulation, and technology policy. NCTA was formerly known as the National Cable & Telecommunications Association.
naics.justification: NCTA's core activity is representing cable and broadband companies' collective policy interests, the defining function of a business association.

alternates.justification: Considered because its members are wired telecom/cable carriers, but NCTA itself does not provide telecom service, it represents those that do.
A weaker fit since NCTA represents companies rather than individual professionals.
Ruled out; NCTA does not operate broadcast stations, its members include cable programmers and operators.

naics.category_justification: NCTA is explicitly structured as a membership trade association for the cable and broadband industry.

naics.description: OpenAI is an American artificial intelligence research and product company known for developing large language models and consumer/enterprise AI products such as ChatGPT and the GPT model API. Originally founded as a nonprofit research lab in 2015, it restructured around a capped-profit subsidiary to raise capital while research remains overseen by an affiliated nonprofit entity. OpenAI has been a prominent commenter on federal AI policy and regulation.
naics.justification: OpenAI's primary commercial activity is developing and licensing AI software products (ChatGPT, API access to its models), matching the software-publishing code, though its origins and ongoing work as an AI research organization make a research-focused code a close competitor.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: OpenAI conducts substantial fundamental AI research, which this R&D code also captures well.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: OpenAI's API business involves providing hosted model-inference infrastructure to developers, a plausible alternate primary activity.
Ruled out as a weaker fit; OpenAI sells standardized software/API products rather than bespoke programming services.

naics.category_justification: OpenAI operates commercially through OpenAI Global, LLC, a capped-profit entity that sells AI products and services, though its unusual nonprofit-controlled structure means it does not cleanly fit a standard for-profit company.

naics.description: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce is the largest business federation in the United States, representing millions of businesses of all sizes, sectors, and regions. It advocates before Congress, regulatory agencies, and courts on a broad range of policy issues affecting business interests, including technology and AI regulation. The organization is headquartered in Washington, D.C., across from the White House.
naics.justification: The Chamber's defining activity is representing the collective policy interests of its business membership, the core definition of a business association.
naics.category_justification: It is explicitly organized as a membership federation of businesses advocating on shared policy interests, not a government body despite its name recognition.

naics.description: Equifax Inc. is one of the three major U.S. consumer credit reporting agencies, collecting and maintaining credit and financial data on consumers and providing credit reports, scores, and analytics products to lenders, employers, and other businesses. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Equifax also offers identity verification and workforce data solutions. It is a publicly traded, for-profit company.
naics.justification: Equifax's defining activity is compiling and reporting consumer credit information, the exact activity captured by the Credit Bureaus code.
naics.category_justification: Equifax is a publicly traded, for-profit credit reporting company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: The American College of Cardiology (ACC) is a national professional medical association representing cardiovascular specialists, providing continuing medical education, clinical guidelines, credentialing, and advocacy on healthcare policy issues affecting cardiology. It is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and its membership includes physicians, researchers, and other cardiovascular care professionals. ACC engages in policy discussions on health technology and AI in clinical care.
naics.justification: ACC's core activity is operating a professional membership association for cardiologists that sets clinical guidelines and advocates on their behalf, matching the Professional Organizations code rather than a direct-care or education code.

alternates.justification: The word 'College' suggests an educational institution, but ACC does not grant degrees; this was ruled out as a naming-based false lead.
ACC provides significant continuing medical education, a real but secondary activity relative to its core association function.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback that fits less precisely than the dedicated professional-organizations code.

naics.category_justification: ACC is a membership-based professional medical association representing cardiovascular specialists' collective professional interests, not a degree-granting university despite the word 'College' in its name.

naics.description: The Information Technology Industry Council (ITI) is a Washington, D.C.-based global trade association representing leading technology companies, including major computer hardware, software, and internet firms. It advocates on policy issues such as AI regulation, trade, cybersecurity, and intellectual property before governments worldwide. ITI's membership includes companies like Apple, Google, IBM, and Microsoft.
naics.justification: ITI's core activity is representing member technology companies' collective policy interests globally, the defining function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: ITI is explicitly structured as a membership trade association for the technology industry.

naics.description: The Future Society is an independent nonprofit organization focused on AI governance, conducting research and advocacy to help policymakers and institutions design effective, safe, and inclusive governance frameworks for artificial intelligence. It engages with international bodies, governments, and industry on AI risk and regulatory design. The organization operates as a think tank with a public-interest mission rather than a membership advocacy body.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: The Future Society's core activity is conducting policy research and analysis on AI governance, which fits the social-science/policy R&D code, though this record also appears as one of the four co-signers in a separate joint-comment record elsewhere in this dataset.

alternates.justification: Its policy-advocacy work on AI governance has a social-advocacy character that competes with the R&D framing.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback considered but less precise than the R&D or advocacy codes.
Ruled out; the organization's work is specialized policy research rather than general civic/social activity.

naics.category_justification: The Future Society is structured and operates as an independent nonprofit think tank pursuing a research and public-interest mission rather than representing a paying membership.

naics.description: The Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC) is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit research and advocacy organization focused on protecting privacy, freedom of expression, and civil liberties in the digital age. It conducts policy research, litigation, and public education on issues including consumer privacy, government surveillance, and AI regulation. EPIC was founded in 1994 and frequently files comments and amicus briefs in federal proceedings.
naics.justification: EPIC's core activity is public-interest research and advocacy on digital privacy and civil-liberties policy, matching the social-advocacy code.

alternates.justification: EPIC's privacy and civil-liberties work overlaps with human-rights advocacy, making this a plausible secondary fit.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Considered given EPIC's legal and policy research work, but it does not sell professional services to clients.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback that fits less precisely than the dedicated social-advocacy code.

naics.category_justification: EPIC is a nonprofit research and advocacy organization pursuing a public-interest mission rather than representing paying members' commercial interests.

naics.resolved_name: National Association of Federally-Insured Credit Unions (NAFCU)
naics.description: The National Association of Federally-Insured Credit Unions (NAFCU) is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing federally chartered and federally insured credit unions across the United States. It advocates before Congress and financial regulators on policy issues affecting credit unions, including data privacy, cybersecurity, and financial technology regulation. NAFCU also provides compliance resources and education to member credit unions.
naics.justification: NAFCU's core activity is representing member credit unions' collective policy interests before regulators and Congress, the defining function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: NAFCU is explicitly structured as a membership trade association for federally insured credit unions.

naics.resolved_name: Amazon Web Services, Inc. (a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc.)
naics.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the cloud computing division of Amazon.com, Inc., providing on-demand infrastructure, storage, database, machine learning, and other computing services to businesses, governments, and developers worldwide. AWS is the market-leading cloud infrastructure provider and offers AI/ML services such as Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker. It operates as a distinct business segment and major profit driver within Amazon.
naics.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
naics.justification: AWS's defining activity is providing cloud computing infrastructure, hosting, and data-processing services to customers, matching this code precisely.
naics.category_justification: AWS is a for-profit business segment of Amazon.com, Inc., commenting in its own commercial interest as a technology provider.

naics.resolved_name: Alliance for Nursing Informatics (co-hosted by AMIA and HIMSS)
naics.description: The Alliance for Nursing Informatics (ANI) is a coalition of roughly 30 nursing informatics organizations representing more than 25,000 nurse informaticists, co-hosted and supported by the American Medical Informatics Association (AMIA) and the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS). ANI advances nursing informatics leadership, practice, education, policy, and research through a unified voice across its member organizations. It engages in advocacy on health IT and AI policy issues affecting nursing practice.
naics.justification: ANI's core activity is coordinating advocacy and professional development among nursing-informatics member organizations, closest to a professional-association code, though as a coalition of organizations rather than individuals the fit is inexact.

alternates.justification: Considered because ANI is a coalition of organizations rather than individuals, closer to how business associations are structured.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback considered but less precise than the dedicated professional-organizations code.
Ruled out; despite health-informatics ties, ANI performs no laboratory or clinical services.

naics.category_justification: ANI is a coalition uniting roughly 30 member nursing-informatics organizations to speak with a unified voice, matching the multi-stakeholder coalition definition.

display_name: American Bar Association Antitrust Law Section

refs.raw_name: American Bar Association Antitrust Law Section

naics.resolved_name: American Bar Association's Section of Antitrust Law
naics.description: The Section of Antitrust Law is a specialized practice-area section within the American Bar Association (ABA), the largest voluntary professional association of lawyers and law students in the United States. The Section focuses on antitrust, consumer protection, and competition law, providing continuing legal education, publications, and policy comments on behalf of its member attorneys who practice in those fields. It regularly submits comments to federal agencies on competition-related regulatory matters, including technology and AI issues.
naics.justification: As a section of the ABA, its primary activity shares the parent association's function of representing and serving its member attorneys professionally, matching the Professional Organizations code used for bar associations.

alternates.justification: Considered because it is composed of practicing antitrust lawyers, but the Section itself does not provide legal services to clients.
A weaker fit since the ABA and its sections represent individual professionals (lawyers) rather than businesses.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback that fits less precisely than the dedicated professional-organizations code.

naics.category_justification: It is a specialized practice section of the ABA, a professional membership association of lawyers, and the record refers to that sub-unit's own representative/advocacy function rather than an independent entity.

naics.description: USTelecom - The Broadband Association is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing telecommunications and broadband service providers in the United States. Its members include major telecom carriers and smaller regional broadband providers, and it advocates on policy issues including broadband deployment, telecommunications regulation, and technology policy such as AI. USTelecom was formerly known as the United States Telecom Association.
naics.justification: USTelecom's core activity is representing member telecom and broadband companies' collective policy interests, the defining function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: USTelecom is explicitly structured as a membership trade association for the broadband and telecommunications industry.

naics.resolved_name: IEEE-USA (a unit of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers)
naics.description: IEEE-USA is the U.S.-focused organizational unit of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the world's largest technical professional association. IEEE-USA advances the public policy, career, and professional interests of IEEE's U.S. members, who are engineers and technologists in electrical, electronics, computing, and related fields. It advocates on issues including AI policy, engineering workforce development, and innovation policy.
naics.justification: IEEE-USA's core activity is advancing the professional and policy interests of its engineer and technologist membership, matching the Professional Organizations code that also applies to its parent, IEEE.

alternates.justification: A weaker fit because IEEE-USA represents individual professionals rather than member businesses.
IEEE-USA offers career and professional development resources, a secondary activity relative to its core advocacy function.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback that fits less precisely than the dedicated professional-organizations code.

naics.category_justification: IEEE-USA is a professional membership association unit representing U.S. engineers' and technologists' collective interests.

naics.resolved_name: HMS (Health Management Systems, now part of Gainwell Technologies)
naics.description: Web research for the bare name 'HMS' in this health-AI-policy comment docket could not confidently confirm a single entity: candidates include HMS Holdings/Health Management Systems (a healthcare cost-containment and payment-integrity company later acquired into Gainwell Technologies), Harvard Medical School's HMS abbreviation, and other unrelated organizations using the same initials. Given the surrounding comments in this batch involve health IT/health insurance companies (Kaiser Permanente, Epic Systems, HIMSS), the healthcare cost-management company HMS is the more likely match, but this could not be verified against the specific comment record. Confidence is kept low given this ambiguity.
naics.justification: If this is HMS Holdings/Health Management Systems, its primary historical activity was payment-integrity and cost-containment services for healthcare payers, a specialized business-support activity, but the name is too ambiguous to assign a code with confidence.

alternates.naics_title: Pharmacy Benefit Management and Other Third Party Administration of Insurance and Pension Funds
alternates.justification: If HMS Holdings, its payment-integrity work for health plans resembles third-party insurance administration.
If this instead refers to Harvard Medical School, the university code would apply.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: Considered as a generic healthcare-provider guess, but ruled least likely given no evidence of a clinical-practice entity named simply 'HMS'.

naics.category_justification: The bare initials 'HMS' could not be confidently matched to a specific organization from this comment batch alone, so the category is left unverified rather than guessing between a company (HMS Holdings) and a university unit (Harvard Medical School).

naics.description: The Lincoln Laboratory Supercomputing Center (LLSC) is a high-performance computing facility operated by MIT Lincoln Laboratory, a federally funded research and development center administered by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology primarily for the U.S. Department of Defense. LLSC provides large-scale, on-demand interactive computing resources used by Laboratory researchers for sensor-data processing, simulation, and algorithm development, including machine-learning research, and supports collaboration with MIT campus researchers. It is one of the most powerful university-affiliated supercomputing centers in the world.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: As a facility supporting MIT Lincoln Laboratory's defense-related engineering and scientific research, its primary activity is R&D infrastructure support, matching this code; confidence is moderated because Lincoln Laboratory's FFRDC structure (administered by MIT but funded mainly by DoD) sits between a university research unit and a government-funded R&D center.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The Center's core function is providing large-scale computing infrastructure, a plausible alternate primary-activity code.
Considered given Lincoln Laboratory's government-funded defense/aerospace research portfolio, but this code is narrower (space-specific) than the Center's actual scope.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: Ruled out; the Center's research spans defense, sensing, and AI rather than biotechnology.

naics.category_justification: Lincoln Laboratory is administered by MIT, and the skill's guidance treats a university's sub-unit as sharing the university's category when the record refers to the institution's own research facility, though its status as a DoD-funded FFRDC makes a government or nonprofit-R&D categorization also plausible.

naics.description: The American Medical Informatics Association (AMIA) is a professional membership association representing clinicians, researchers, and other professionals working in biomedical and health informatics. AMIA provides education, credentialing, publications, and policy advocacy on health information technology and AI issues in healthcare, and co-hosts the Alliance for Nursing Informatics along with HIMSS. It is headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland.
naics.justification: AMIA's core activity is operating a professional membership association for health informatics professionals that advances their professional and policy interests, matching this code.

alternates.justification: AMIA offers substantial continuing education and credentialing, a real but secondary activity.
A weaker fit since AMIA represents individual professionals rather than member businesses.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback that fits less precisely than the dedicated professional-organizations code.

naics.category_justification: AMIA is a membership-based professional association representing health-informatics professionals' collective interests.

naics.description: Epic Systems Corporation is a privately held American healthcare software company that develops and sells electronic health record (EHR) software used by major hospital systems and healthcare organizations across the United States. Headquartered in Verona, Wisconsin, Epic's software is used to manage patient records, clinical workflows, and increasingly AI-assisted clinical decision support. Epic is one of the dominant vendors in the U.S. EHR market.
naics.justification: Epic Systems' defining activity is developing and licensing electronic health record software, matching the Software Publishers code.
naics.category_justification: Epic Systems is a privately held, for-profit software company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.resolved_name: Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS)
naics.description: HIMSS (Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society) is a global nonprofit membership organization focused on advancing health information technology, including through education, advocacy, certification, and industry events such as its annual HIMSS Global Health Conference. HIMSS engages with policymakers on health IT and AI regulation and co-hosts initiatives such as the Alliance for Nursing Informatics along with AMIA. It is now operated by Definitive Healthcare after a 2022 acquisition, though it continues to function as a professional and industry membership community.
naics.justification: HIMSS's core activity is operating a professional and industry membership community advancing health IT policy, education, and standards, matching a professional-association code, though its 2022 acquisition by a for-profit company (Definitive Healthcare) complicates a clean nonprofit-association classification.

alternates.justification: HIMSS is widely known for organizing its large annual health IT conference and trade show, a significant share of its activity.
HIMSS's membership includes many vendor organizations, giving it business-association characteristics alongside its individual professional members.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback considered but less precise than the dedicated professional-organizations or trade-show codes.

naics.category_justification: HIMSS functions as a membership organization representing health IT professionals' and vendors' collective interests, though its ownership by a for-profit parent since 2022 introduces some ambiguity versus a purely nonprofit or business classification.

naics.description: The National Association of Manufacturers (NAM) is the largest U.S. trade association representing manufacturers across all industrial sectors, from small businesses to large multinational corporations. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., NAM advocates on policy issues affecting manufacturing, including trade, tax, workforce, and technology regulation such as AI. It is one of the oldest and most prominent industrial trade associations in the country, founded in 1895.
naics.justification: NAM's defining activity is representing manufacturers' collective policy interests across industries, the core function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: NAM is explicitly organized as a membership trade association representing the manufacturing sector's shared policy interests.

naics.description: The Center for Democracy & Technology (CDT) is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit organization that advocates for civil liberties and human rights in the digital age. It works through policy research, litigation, and advocacy on issues such as privacy, free expression, and algorithmic accountability, including AI policy. CDT regularly submits comments to federal agencies such as NIST, OMB, and NTIA on technology regulation.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: CDT's primary activity is policy research and analysis on digital rights issues, which it publishes and uses to inform advocacy, matching R&D in social sciences rather than a narrower civic category.

alternates.justification: CDT could also be seen as a civic advocacy organization given its lobbying and public engagement work.
CDT is not a membership body for a profession, so this is a weaker fit.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all if the research framing is rejected.

naics.category_justification: CDT is a mission-driven 501(c)(3) nonprofit conducting research and advocacy on digital rights, not a membership trade body or government entity.

naics.description: Microsoft Corporation is a multinational technology company headquartered in Redmond, Washington, best known for the Windows operating system, Office productivity suite, Azure cloud computing platform, and a broad portfolio of enterprise and consumer software. It is one of the world's largest software publishers and a major developer of AI systems. Microsoft frequently engages with federal policymakers on technology and AI regulation.
naics.justification: Microsoft's primary business is developing and licensing software products (operating systems, productivity software, cloud platforms), the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: Microsoft is a publicly traded for-profit corporation commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: The Consumer Technology Association is a U.S. trade association representing the consumer technology industry, including manufacturers of electronics, appliances, and connected devices. It is best known for organizing the annual CES trade show and for advocating on behalf of its member companies before Congress and federal agencies. CTA also develops technical standards for the consumer electronics industry.
naics.justification: CTA's primary activity is representing and advocating for its member companies in the consumer technology industry, the defining activity of a business association.
naics.category_justification: CTA is a membership-based trade association representing consumer technology manufacturers' collective interests.

naics.description: TechNet is a national, bipartisan network of technology CEOs and senior executives that advocates on public policy issues affecting the innovation economy, including AI, cybersecurity, and internet policy. It operates as a trade association with state and federal chapters that lobby and submit comments to regulators and legislators. Its membership spans major technology and internet companies.
naics.justification: TechNet's core activity is advocating on behalf of its member technology companies' collective policy interests, matching the business association code.
naics.category_justification: TechNet is explicitly a membership network of tech executives organized to advance shared policy interests.

naics.description: The American College of Radiology is a national professional medical society representing radiologists, radiation oncologists, and medical physicists in the United States. It sets practice guidelines and accreditation standards for medical imaging and advocates on healthcare policy, including the use of AI in radiology. It is a membership organization rather than a degree-granting institution.
naics.justification: ACR's primary activity is representing and setting standards for the radiology profession, the defining activity of a professional membership organization, despite the misleading word 'College' in its name.

alternates.justification: The word 'College' in the name could mislead toward a degree-granting institution, but ACR does not grant degrees.
A generic membership-society fallback, less precise than the professional organization code.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: ACR also produces practice guidelines and accreditation criteria resembling a professional/technical service.

naics.category_justification: Despite its name, ACR is a professional membership association for radiologists, not a degree-granting university.

naics.resolved_name: SAP America, Inc. (subsidiary of SAP SE)
naics.description: SAP America, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of SAP SE, a German multinational that develops enterprise resource planning (ERP) and business management software used by organizations worldwide. It sells and supports SAP's software products, including AI-enabled analytics and business applications, to U.S. customers. SAP frequently comments on technology and AI policy matters affecting enterprise software.
naics.justification: SAP America's primary activity is publishing and licensing enterprise software developed by its parent company SAP SE, matching the software publishers code.
naics.category_justification: SAP America is a for-profit corporate subsidiary commenting on behalf of its own commercial interests.

naics.description: The American Medical Association is the largest professional association of physicians and medical students in the United States. It advocates on healthcare policy, publishes clinical and ethical guidance including on AI in medicine, and represents physicians' interests before government bodies. It is a membership organization, not a hospital or insurer.
naics.justification: The AMA's core activity is representing and advocating for physicians as a professional body, the defining activity of a professional organization.
naics.category_justification: The AMA is a membership-based professional association representing physicians' collective interests.

naics.description: Hitachi, Ltd. is a Japanese multinational conglomerate with businesses spanning information technology, energy, industrial systems, and digital solutions. Its offerings include data infrastructure, IT services, and AI-driven analytics through subsidiaries such as Hitachi Vantara and Hitachi Digital. As a diversified conglomerate, no single NAICS code fully captures its range of activities.
naics.justification: Hitachi's IT and data infrastructure hardware business is a plausible primary activity, but as a broad conglomerate spanning manufacturing, energy, and IT services, no single code is clearly dominant.

alternates.justification: Hitachi Vantara and Hitachi Digital provide significant IT systems design and consulting services.
Hitachi's energy and industrial systems division manufactures power and electrical equipment.
Hitachi Rail is a significant global manufacturer of rail rolling stock and signaling systems.

naics.category_justification: Hitachi is a publicly traded for-profit multinational corporation.

naics.description: The American Academy of Dermatology Association is the advocacy affiliate of the American Academy of Dermatology, the largest professional organization for dermatologists in the United States. It represents dermatologists' interests on healthcare policy and regulatory issues, including the use of AI in skin disease diagnosis. It is a membership society rather than a research institution.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is representing and advocating for the dermatology profession, matching the professional organization code.
naics.category_justification: It is the policy advocacy arm of a professional medical membership society representing dermatologists.

naics.description: The College of American Pathologists is a professional membership organization for board-certified pathologists that also accredits clinical laboratories and administers proficiency testing programs. It advocates on healthcare and laboratory regulatory policy, including AI use in diagnostics. Despite the word 'College' in its name, it is not a degree-granting institution.
naics.justification: CAP's central identity and largest activity is as the professional membership body for pathologists, though it also runs a significant laboratory accreditation and testing program.

alternates.justification: CAP's laboratory accreditation and proficiency testing programs are a major and distinct revenue-generating activity.
The word 'College' in the name could mislead toward an educational institution, but CAP does not grant degrees.
A generic membership-society fallback, less precise than the professional organization code.

naics.category_justification: CAP is fundamentally a professional membership association for pathologists, despite its name resembling an educational institution.
