display_name: Computing Technology Industry Association (CompTIA)Computing Technology Industry Association

refs.raw_name: Computing Technology Industry Association (CompTIA)Computing Technology Industry Association

naics.description: CompTIA is a nonprofit trade association for the information technology industry that develops vendor-neutral IT certifications and advocates on technology policy on behalf of its member companies and IT professionals. It represents a broad cross-section of the IT industry, including AI-related workforce and policy issues. It also provides market research and workforce development programs for the sector.
naics.justification: CompTIA's primary role is representing the IT industry's collective interests through advocacy and standard-setting, the defining activity of a business association, though it also runs a substantial certification business.

alternates.justification: CompTIA's IT certification exams are a major, distinct line of business resembling educational support/testing services.
Its certification and professional-development focus could also fit a professional organization framing.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Listed as a keyword-matched candidate but does not match CompTIA's actual activity of trade advocacy and certification.

naics.category_justification: CompTIA is a membership-based industry trade association representing IT companies and professionals.

naics.description: The Consumer Data Industry Association is a trade association representing consumer reporting agencies, including the major national credit bureaus and background-check companies. It advocates on policy affecting the use of consumer data, credit reporting, and algorithmic decision-making. Its members supply data used in lending, employment, and tenant screening decisions.
naics.justification: The association's primary activity is representing the collective policy interests of consumer reporting companies, matching the business association code.
naics.category_justification: It is a membership trade association representing consumer reporting and data companies.

naics.description: Zest AI (formerly ZestFinance) is a U.S. financial technology company that develops AI-powered credit underwriting and risk-scoring software for lenders. Its platform is designed to help banks and credit unions make more accurate and fair automated lending decisions. The company has been active in policy discussions on fairness and explainability in AI-driven credit decisions.
naics.justification: Zest AI's primary business is developing and licensing proprietary machine-learning software for credit underwriting, matching the software publishers code.

alternates.naics_title: International, Secondary Market, and All Other Nondepository Credit Intermediation
alternates.justification: Zest AI is sometimes associated with lending activity, though it licenses software to lenders rather than lending itself.
Some of its offerings involve bespoke model development for individual lender clients.
Zest AI also provides advisory services on fair-lending model design.

naics.category_justification: Zest AI is a for-profit fintech company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: The Committee for Justice is a Washington, D.C.-based conservative nonprofit legal policy organization focused on judicial nominations, constitutional law, and civil justice reform. It engages in advocacy and public commentary on legal and regulatory policy issues, including technology and AI regulation as they intersect with legal process. It is not a government body or law firm.
naics.justification: The Committee for Justice's primary activity is public-interest legal advocacy and civic commentary, which best fits a civic/social organization rather than a research-heavy think tank.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The organization also produces policy analysis and commentary resembling social-science research.
Its focus on judicial and legal issues could suggest a legal-services fit, though it does not practice law for clients.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback for an advocacy nonprofit that doesn't cleanly fit other categories.

naics.category_justification: It is a mission-driven 501(c) advocacy nonprofit focused on legal and judicial policy, not a membership trade body.

naics.description: The American Action Forum is a center-right nonprofit policy institute in Washington, D.C. that conducts economic and regulatory policy research, including on technology and AI regulation. It publishes analyses intended to inform congressional and executive branch policymaking. It is not affiliated with any political party or government body.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: AAF's primary activity is producing policy and economic research, matching the social-science R&D code used for think tanks.
naics.category_justification: AAF is a nonpartisan 501(c)(3) policy research nonprofit, not a membership trade association or government body.

naics.description: NEMA is a U.S. trade association representing manufacturers of electrical equipment and medical imaging technology. It develops industry standards and advocates on regulatory and technology policy affecting its member manufacturers, including AI used in medical imaging devices. It does not itself manufacture products.
naics.justification: NEMA's core activity is representing and setting standards for its member electrical-equipment manufacturers, the defining activity of a business association.
naics.category_justification: NEMA is a membership-based trade association representing electrical equipment manufacturers.

naics.description: Deloitte & Touche LLP is the U.S. audit and assurance subsidiary of Deloitte, one of the largest professional services networks in the world. It provides financial statement audit and related attestation services to public and private companies, and its broader Deloitte network also offers consulting on AI risk and governance. It is organized as a limited liability partnership of certified public accountants.
naics.justification: Deloitte & Touche LLP is specifically Deloitte's audit and assurance practice, staffed by CPAs, matching the offices of certified public accountants code.
naics.category_justification: Deloitte & Touche LLP is a for-profit professional services partnership commenting in its own or its clients' commercial interest.

naics.resolved_name: IEEE Standards Association (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers)
naics.description: The IEEE Standards Association is the standards-development branch of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the world's largest technical professional organization for engineering and electronics fields. It develops global technical standards, including on AI ethics and autonomous systems, through a consensus process involving engineers and industry stakeholders. It operates as part of IEEE, a nonprofit professional membership association.
naics.justification: As a division of IEEE, a professional engineering membership society, its standards-development work is best captured by the professional organization code that describes its parent.

alternates.justification: Standards development has some overlap with testing and certification services, though IEEE-SA itself does not test products.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback for a standards-setting body if the professional-organization framing is rejected.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Standards writing could loosely be seen as a professional technical service.

naics.category_justification: IEEE-SA is a sub-unit of IEEE, a professional/technical membership society, whose standards work represents its engineering membership's collective interests.

naics.description: Olive AI was a U.S. healthcare technology company that developed AI-powered automation software to help hospitals and health systems streamline administrative and revenue-cycle processes. The company was headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, and was venture-backed before winding down parts of its operations in 2023. Its core product was cloud-based automation software sold to healthcare providers.
naics.justification: Olive AI's primary activity was developing and licensing proprietary healthcare automation software, matching the software publishers code.

alternates.justification: Some of Olive's implementations involved bespoke configuration for individual health-system clients.
Olive also provided revenue-cycle process advisory alongside its software.
Its close integration with hospital operations gives a weak health-services angle, though Olive did not deliver clinical care.

naics.category_justification: Olive AI was a venture-backed for-profit software company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.resolved_name: NEC Corporation of America (subsidiary of NEC Corporation, Japan)
naics.description: NEC Corporation of America is the U.S. subsidiary of NEC Corporation, a Japanese multinational IT and electronics company. It provides information technology integration, communications infrastructure, public safety, and biometric identification solutions, including facial recognition and other AI-driven technologies, to U.S. government and commercial customers. It functions primarily as a systems integrator and solutions provider rather than a hardware manufacturer.
naics.justification: NEC Corporation of America's primary U.S. activity is designing and integrating IT and communications systems (including biometrics and public-safety solutions) for customers, rather than manufacturing hardware directly.

alternates.justification: NEC's parent company is historically a computer and electronics hardware manufacturer.
NEC also provides telecommunications infrastructure, though it is not itself a carrier.

alternates.naics_title: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: NEC manufactures some communications equipment, a secondary line of business.

naics.category_justification: NEC Corporation of America is a for-profit corporate subsidiary commenting on behalf of its own commercial interests.

naics.description: Color Of Change is a U.S. nonprofit racial justice advocacy organization that mobilizes its members to campaign against racial discrimination in areas including criminal justice, media, corporate accountability, and technology, such as algorithmic bias and facial recognition. It conducts online organizing campaigns and issues policy comments to government agencies. It does not provide direct social services.
naics.justification: Color Of Change's core activity is civic advocacy and grassroots organizing around racial justice issues, matching the civic and social organizations code.

alternates.justification: Its campaign-style organizing and lobbying could suggest a political organization framing, though it is not a party or PAC.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Some of its output includes issue research and reports, a weaker secondary activity.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback for an advocacy nonprofit not cleanly fitting other categories.

naics.category_justification: It is a mission-driven 501(c)(4)/(c)(3)-affiliated racial justice advocacy nonprofit, not a membership trade or professional body.

naics.description: The MITRE Corporation is a U.S. nonprofit organization that operates several federally funded research and development centers (FFRDCs) on behalf of U.S. government agencies, conducting systems engineering and research in areas including cybersecurity, aviation, healthcare, and artificial intelligence. It works exclusively in the public interest and does not manufacture or sell products commercially. MITRE is frequently consulted by federal agencies on technical standards and policy.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: MITRE's primary activity is engineering and scientific research and development performed for federal agencies through its FFRDCs, matching this R&D code.
naics.category_justification: MITRE is a nonprofit corporation that operates FFRDCs in the public interest, distinct from a government agency itself.

naics.resolved_name: Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA, Republic of Korea)
naics.description: The Telecommunications Technology Association is a South Korean information and communications technology standardization body that develops ICT standards and provides testing and certification services, including through its Center for Trustworthy AI, which focuses on AI testing and certification frameworks. It is organized as a private, autonomous standards and testing organization rather than a telecommunications carrier. TTA has submitted comments to U.S. agencies such as NIST on AI risk management guidance.
naics.justification: TTA's core activities are ICT standards development and product testing/certification, which most closely matches testing laboratories and services rather than telecommunications carriage.

alternates.justification: TTA also functions as a standards-setting membership body akin to a professional/technical association.
The 'Telecommunications' in its name could mislead toward a carrier classification, but TTA does not operate telecom networks.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its research and policy advisory work on AI trustworthiness could also fit general technical consulting.

naics.category_justification: TTA functions as a Korean industry standards and certification body with quasi-governmental ties; it most resembles a trade/standards association rather than a private company, though its exact legal status is not fully confirmed.

naics.description: Queer in AI is a volunteer-run grassroots affinity organization and community for LGBTQ+ individuals working or studying in artificial intelligence and machine learning. It organizes events, mentorship, and advocacy at major AI/ML conferences and has submitted comments on AI policy affecting marginalized communities. It is not a formally staffed institution but operates as an all-volunteer collective.
naics.justification: Queer in AI functions as a community/affinity advocacy group organizing members around shared identity and interests within the AI field, matching civic and social organizations.

alternates.justification: It also functions somewhat like a professional affinity group for AI/ML practitioners.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)

naics.resolved_name: Graduates for Engaged and Extended Scholarship in Computing and Engineering (GEESE), University of California, Berkeley
naics.description: GEESE (Graduates for Engaged and Extended Scholarship in Computing and Engineering) is a graduate student group at the University of California, Berkeley that provides a space for computing and engineering graduate students to engage with the societal implications of technology. The group organizes and supports related coursework, seminars, and discussions on topics such as fairness, privacy, and technology ethics, operating within Berkeley's computing and engineering graduate community.
naics.justification: GEESE is a graduate student organization operating within UC Berkeley, so per guidance for university sub-units it is classified under higher education.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Its activities touch on socially oriented research topics, though it primarily functions as a student group rather than an R&D unit.
As a student club/interest group, it could alternatively be seen as a civic/social organization rather than a formal academic unit.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Some engineering-related seminar topics touch on technical R&D themes.

naics.category_justification: GEESE is a graduate student group operating within and affiliated with UC Berkeley.

naics.description: The Institute for Workplace Equality (formerly The OFCCP Institute) is a Washington, D.C.-based national nonprofit employer association that trains and educates federal contractors on affirmative action and equal employment opportunity compliance. It supports employers navigating obligations enforced by the Department of Labor's OFCCP, EEOC, and related regulations, and has developed tools such as a Pay Equity Index. The organization changed its name in 2017 to reflect an expanded scope of training and advocacy.
naics.justification: The Institute functions as a membership-based employer association providing training, tools, and advocacy for federal contractors, matching a business association.

alternates.justification: Could alternatively be seen as a professional organization for compliance practitioners rather than a general business association.
The Institute provides HR compliance tools and consulting-style guidance to member employers.
A significant part of its activity is delivering training programs to employer members.

naics.category_justification: It is a membership-based employer association representing and training federal contractors on compliance issues.

naics.description: The Center for American Entrepreneurship (CAE) is a nonpartisan Washington, D.C.-area 501(c)(3) research, policy, and advocacy organization founded by John Dearie. It engages and educates policymakers at the federal, state, and local levels on the importance of entrepreneurship and startups to innovation, economic growth, and job creation, and pursues a policy agenda to support new business formation and growth.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: CAE's core activity is producing economic and policy research to inform its advocacy on entrepreneurship policy, matching R&D in the social sciences, though it is also heavily focused on direct advocacy.

alternates.justification: Much of CAE's day-to-day work is direct policy advocacy and lobbying-adjacent engagement with policymakers.
It functions somewhat like a business-interest association, though it is not a dues-based membership body.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Appeared in candidate shortlist context but does not match its actual nonprofit research/advocacy mission.

naics.category_justification: CAE is a 501(c)(3) nonpartisan policy research and advocacy organization, not a dues-based membership trade group.

naics.description: Consumer Reports is an American nonprofit organization, founded in 1936, dedicated to independent product testing, ratings, investigative journalism, and consumer advocacy. It publishes Consumer Reports magazine and online content based on its own laboratory testing and surveys, and does not accept advertising from manufacturers or retailers. The organization also advocates for consumer protections on issues including product safety, digital rights, and financial fairness.
naics.justification: A core, defining activity of Consumer Reports is independent laboratory testing of consumer products, matching this code, though it also has substantial publishing and advocacy operations.

alternates.justification: Consumer Reports also publishes a well-known magazine and extensive online content based on its testing results.
Its consumer-advocacy work is a major and growing part of its overall mission.
Appeared in the candidate shortlist due to keyword overlap with 'consumer' but does not match its actual activities.

naics.category_justification: Consumer Reports is an explicitly nonprofit organization dedicated to independent testing and public-interest consumer advocacy.

naics.resolved_name: American Council for Technology and Industry Advisory Council (ACT-IAC)
naics.description: ACT-IAC (American Council for Technology-Industry Advisory Council) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit membership organization that brings together government and industry professionals to improve government through the effective use of technology. It combines the American Council for Technology, composed of government employees, and the Industry Advisory Council, comprising roughly 500 member companies, to provide a forum for collaboration, education, and thought leadership on federal IT topics.
naics.justification: ACT-IAC is a dues-based membership organization connecting government and industry members around shared technology-modernization interests, matching a business association.

alternates.justification: Could alternatively be viewed as a professional organization for government-technology practitioners.
ACT-IAC provides significant education and training programming to its members.
Appeared in the candidate shortlist context but does not match its actual membership-association activity.

naics.category_justification: ACT-IAC is a membership-based public-private council representing government and industry members' shared interest in government technology modernization.

naics.description: SaferAI is a French nonprofit organization founded in 2023 that works to advance AI risk management in policy and industry. It develops quantitative risk models for advanced AI systems, independently rates how well AI companies manage risk, and contributes to international AI safety standards, including work with the EU and OECD. SaferAI advises AI Safety Institutes and policymakers globally.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: SaferAI's primary activity is technical research to model and quantify AI risks, closest to engineering/technical R&D, though it also engages heavily in policy and standards advocacy.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Much of its standards and policy work has a social-science/governance character.
Its advisory and standards-setting work with policymakers resembles advocacy activity.
SaferAI rates and advises companies on risk management practices, resembling consulting.

naics.category_justification: SaferAI is described as a nonprofit organization conducting research and advising on AI risk-management standards.

naics.description: Scale AI is a San Francisco-based technology company, founded in 2016, that provides data labeling and annotation services and AI training-data infrastructure for machine learning models, including computer vision, autonomous vehicles, and large language models. The company combines machine learning tools with human-in-the-loop annotation workforces via subsidiaries such as Remotasks and Outlier. Meta made a major investment in Scale AI, acquiring a significant minority stake.
naics.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
naics.justification: Scale AI's core offering is a data-processing platform (annotation and data-pipeline services) for AI training data, the closest fit among available codes, though this code is intended more for infrastructure/hosting than human-in-the-loop annotation services.

alternates.justification: Much of Scale AI's work involves managing large annotation workforces, which functions as a business support service.
Scale AI also builds custom ML tooling and software for clients.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: General fallback given the company's hybrid data-services and software business model.

naics.category_justification: Scale AI is a venture-backed, for-profit technology company.

naics.description: The Blue Cross Blue Shield Association (BCBSA) is a national federation of 33 independent, community-based health insurance companies that together provide coverage to more than 100 million people across the United States. Headquartered in Chicago, BCBSA licenses the Blue Cross and Blue Shield trademarks to its member companies and administers Medicare programs in many regions. It also coordinates policy advocacy on behalf of its member health plans.
naics.justification: BCBSA's core role is coordinating and representing the shared interests, trademark licensing, and standards of its member health-insurance companies, matching a business association, though its licensing and administrative functions also resemble an insurance-related entity.

alternates.naics_title: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers
alternates.justification: BCBSA is closely associated with health-insurance provision through its licensed member plans, even though the association itself does not directly underwrite policies.

alternates.naics_title: Pharmacy Benefit Management and Other Third Party Administration of Insurance and Pension Funds
alternates.justification: BCBSA administers certain national programs, such as coordinating Medicare administration, on behalf of members.
Could alternatively be seen as a professional/industry organization for its member health plans.

naics.category_justification: BCBSA functions as a federation/association representing and coordinating its independent member health-insurance companies.

naics.description: The AI Risk and Vulnerability Alliance (ARVA) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization whose mission is to help communities recognize, diagnose, and manage vulnerabilities and risks in AI systems. Its flagship project is the AI Vulnerability Database (AVID), an open-source taxonomy and knowledge base of AI system flaws and mitigation techniques modeled on cybersecurity best practices. ARVA collaborates with researchers and civil society organizations on AI red-teaming and risk documentation.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: ARVA's core activity is technical research and tool-building to document and evaluate AI system risks, closest to engineering-oriented R&D, though it functions largely as an open-source, community-driven database project.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: AVID functions partly as an open, searchable knowledge database and information service.
Its advocacy for AI safety standards alongside other civil-society groups resembles social-advocacy work.
It builds and maintains open-source software tools as part of its database project.

naics.category_justification: ARVA is explicitly identified as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

naics.description: Cision US Inc. is a Chicago-headquartered provider of cloud-based software for public relations and communications professionals, offering media monitoring, analytics, and newswire distribution services such as PR Newswire and PRWeb. The company, a subsidiary of Platinum Equity, serves marketing and communications teams worldwide with tools for tracking media coverage and measuring communications impact. It operates across dozens of locations globally.
naics.justification: Cision's core offering is proprietary cloud software (media-monitoring and PR platforms) licensed to customers, matching software publishing, though it also runs newswire distribution services that resemble other information-sector activities.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Its media-monitoring and newswire distribution services function partly as an information service.
Cision serves the PR industry closely, though it provides software tools rather than acting as a PR agency itself.

alternates.naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
alternates.justification: Its analytics products include some media/sentiment measurement resembling market research.

naics.category_justification: Cision is a for-profit, private-equity-owned software and media services company.

naics.description: Johnson & Johnson is an American multinational corporation headquartered in New Brunswick, New Jersey, that develops, manufactures, and markets pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and consumer health products. Incorporated in 1887, it operates through more than 265 subsidiary companies worldwide and is one of the largest healthcare companies globally. J&J holds a AAA credit rating and is ranked among the largest U.S. corporations by revenue.
naics.justification: Pharmaceuticals represent J&J's largest and primary business segment, matching this code, though the company is a diversified conglomerate that also manufactures medical devices and consumer health products.

alternates.justification: J&J's MedTech segment manufactures a large range of surgical and medical devices.
J&J's consumer health segment produces personal-care and toiletry products.
J&J operates as a holding company over more than 265 operating subsidiaries, which could alternatively support classification as a holding company.

naics.category_justification: Johnson & Johnson is an unambiguous, publicly traded for-profit multinational corporation.

naics.resolved_name: Investor Alliance for Human Rights (an initiative of the Interfaith Center on Corporate Responsibility)
naics.description: The Investor Alliance for Human Rights is a collective action platform established by the Interfaith Center on Corporate Responsibility to facilitate investor advocacy on human rights and labor issues. Its roughly 150 institutional investor members, representing trillions of dollars in assets under management across some 21 countries, engage companies on responsible business conduct and have published tools such as an Investor Toolkit on Human Rights. It promotes investor practices consistent with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights.
naics.justification: The Alliance's core mission is coordinating investor advocacy specifically around human rights, matching this code, though its investor-membership structure also resembles a finance-sector coalition.

alternates.justification: Its broader corporate-accountability advocacy extends beyond a narrow human-rights framing.
Its membership and toolkit are oriented toward institutional investors' asset-management practices.
It functions as a coalition of investor-member organizations coordinating shared advocacy positions.

naics.category_justification: It is a membership coalition of institutional investors organized to advance shared advocacy goals on human rights.

naics.description: Accenture Federal Services (operating as Accenture National Security Services) is the U.S. federal-government-focused subsidiary of the global professional services firm Accenture. Based in Arlington, Virginia, it provides technology consulting, digital transformation, cybersecurity, cloud, data analytics, and IT modernization services to federal civilian, defense, and intelligence agencies. The company employs more than 13,000 people and has grown through acquisitions such as Cognosante.
naics.justification: Accenture Federal Services' primary offerings are IT modernization, cloud, and systems consulting for federal clients, closest to computer systems design services, though it also provides broad management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The firm also provides broad management and digital-transformation consulting beyond pure systems design.
Some of its offerings, such as cybersecurity services, fall under general computer-related services.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: General fallback for its highly diversified federal consulting portfolio.

naics.category_justification: Accenture Federal Services is a for-profit subsidiary of a publicly traded professional-services corporation.

naics.description: WITNESS is a New York City-based international nonprofit organization, founded in 1992, that trains and supports human-rights defenders and activists in using video and technology to document and expose human-rights abuses. It provides training, practical guidance, and advocacy tools, and operates in more than 100 countries. Its WITNESS Media Lab addresses challenges of sourcing, verifying, and contextualizing eyewitness video, including issues raised by AI-generated media.
naics.justification: WITNESS's defining mission and activity is supporting human-rights documentation, training, and advocacy, directly matching this code.

alternates.justification: Its work spans broader social-justice advocacy in addition to a narrower human-rights focus.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction
alternates.justification: A significant part of its activity is training activists and community members, resembling instructional services.
Video documentation and media production are central tools of its work, though not its defining organizational activity.

naics.category_justification: WITNESS is an established international nonprofit human-rights organization.

naics.description: Hugging Face, Inc. is a New York City-based company that develops open-source tools and a collaborative hosting platform for machine learning, often described as the 'GitHub of machine learning.' Founded in 2016, it maintains the widely used Transformers library and the Hugging Face Hub, which hosts over a million publicly shared models, datasets, and applications. The company is backed by major technology investors including Google, Amazon, Nvidia, and Salesforce.
naics.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
naics.justification: Hugging Face's primary business is hosting a large-scale platform (the Hugging Face Hub) for sharing ML models, datasets, and applications, matching data processing/web hosting, though it also develops and publishes open-source software.

alternates.justification: Hugging Face develops and distributes open-source and proprietary machine-learning software libraries.
The company offers enterprise support and custom deployment services for its platform.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: The Hub also functions as a searchable directory/information service for ML resources.

naics.category_justification: Hugging Face is a venture-backed, for-profit technology company.

normalized_name: center for responsible ai at new york university
display_name: Center for Responsible AI at New York University

refs.raw_name: Center for Responsible AI at New York University

naics.resolved_name: Center for Responsible AI at New York University
naics.description: The Center for Responsible AI (R/AI) at New York University is a research center, founded by Professor Julia Stoyanovich, dedicated to ensuring AI systems are designed and deployed responsibly. It conducts interdisciplinary research on the societal impacts of AI, develops tools and frameworks for responsible AI, and runs educational and public-engagement programs, including the New York AI Exchange in partnership with CUNY. The center is housed at NYU.
naics.justification: The Center for Responsible AI is a research center housed within and operated by New York University, so per guidance for university sub-units it is classified under higher education.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The center's day-to-day work is interdisciplinary research on AI's societal impact, distinct from formal instruction.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Some of its research and tool development is technical/engineering-oriented.
Some of the center's output includes building open-source software tools for responsible AI, a minor part of its overall research mission.

naics.category_justification: It is a research center formally established within and operated by New York University.

naics.description: DLA Piper is a global law firm formed in 2005 through the merger of three firms, with offices in more than 40 countries. It is among the largest law firms in the world by headcount and provides legal services across practice areas including corporate law, litigation, intellectual property and technology, government affairs, and tax. The firm advises clients on regulatory and policy matters, including technology and AI regulation.
naics.justification: DLA Piper's primary activity is providing legal services to clients, the defining activity of this code.

alternates.justification: The firm's government-affairs practice provides consulting-adjacent advisory services.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: General fallback given the firm's broad range of professional services beyond core legal practice.
The firm's employment practice touches HR-related advisory work, though this is a minor part of its business.

naics.category_justification: DLA Piper is a for-profit law firm/partnership serving corporate and government clients in its own professional capacity.

naics.description: The Integrity Institute is a nonprofit organization run by a community of trust-and-safety ('integrity') professionals working to advance the theory and practice of protecting the social internet. Its research draws on the experience of more than 600 trust-and-safety professionals from over 80 technology companies across 23 countries, and it produces public research, webinars, and a podcast on platform governance, digital safety, and technical policy design. It partners with corporate teams, regulators, and civil society organizations.
naics.justification: The Institute organizes and represents a community of trust-and-safety professionals who pool expertise and produce shared research, matching a professional organization, though it also functions like a policy research nonprofit.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It produces substantial original research on platform governance and digital safety.
Its public-facing advocacy on platform governance issues resembles social-advocacy activity.
Could alternatively be seen as an industry-linked association given its ties to member companies' staff.

naics.category_justification: It functions as a membership community of integrity/trust-and-safety professionals producing shared research and advocacy, similar to a professional association.

naics.resolved_name: Centre for Information Policy Leadership at Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP
naics.description: The Centre for Information Policy Leadership (CIPL) is a global privacy and data-policy think tank operating within the law firm Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP. Founded in 2001, it develops research, white papers, and policy recommendations on privacy, data governance, and cybersecurity, working with more than 85 member companies as well as regulators and policymakers worldwide. It is financially supported jointly by its member companies and the law firm.
naics.justification: CIPL functions as an industry-funded coalition representing and advancing its member companies' shared interests in privacy and data policy, closest to a business association, though it is legally organized within a law firm rather than as an independent membership entity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Much of CIPL's output is formal policy research and white papers on data governance.
It is housed and financially supported within, and shares infrastructure with, a law firm.
Its public-policy advocacy work also resembles broader social-advocacy activity.

naics.category_justification: CIPL is member-funded by more than 85 companies who participate to advance shared data-policy positions, characteristic of an industry coalition, albeit hosted inside a law firm.

naics.description: Lumeris is a St. Louis-based healthcare technology and services company that partners with health systems and physician groups to deliver value-based, AI-enabled primary care management. Its offerings include the 'Tom' AI-powered platform, built on Google Cloud, which supports predictive analytics, administrative automation, and clinical decision support for population health management. The company reports managing billions of dollars in medical expenses across more than a million patient lives.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: Lumeris provides care-management consulting, technology, and administrative support services to healthcare organizations rather than delivering direct patient care or purely licensing standalone software, making general management consulting the closest available fit, though this only partially captures its technology-platform business.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its 'Tom' platform functions as a cloud-based data and analytics service for healthcare clients.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
alternates.justification: Lumeris works closely with primary-care delivery, though it does not itself provide direct patient care.

alternates.naics_title: Pharmacy Benefit Management and Other Third Party Administration of Insurance and Pension Funds
alternates.justification: Some of its value-based care administration work resembles third-party administration for payers.

naics.category_justification: Lumeris is a for-profit healthcare technology and services company.

naics.description: ReadWriteReality, Inc. is a small technology company that develops AI-powered tools for generating immersive visual content, including 'Panorama Pro,' a generative AI application that creates 360-degree panoramic scenes from text descriptions. The company appears to be founder-led, with limited public information available beyond its product offerings. It operates in the generative AI content-creation space.
naics.justification: The company's primary identifiable activity is developing and distributing an AI-powered generative software application, closest to software publishing, though very limited independent information is available to confirm its full business model.

alternates.justification: The company may operate more as a small custom-development shop than a packaged-software publisher.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its generative-AI tool may be delivered as a hosted service rather than licensed software.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: General fallback given minimal available information on the company's actual business structure.

naics.category_justification: Available evidence points to a small for-profit technology company, though limited public information leaves some uncertainty.

naics.description: Knowledge Ecology International (KEI) is a Washington, D.C. and Geneva-based nonprofit, non-governmental organization founded in 2006 (evolving from the earlier Consumer Project on Technology, founded by Ralph Nader in 1995). KEI researches and advocates on the management of knowledge resources, focusing on the intersection of intellectual property, public health, competition policy, and access to knowledge for vulnerable and low-income populations. It engages in research, advocacy, and technical advice to governments and NGOs.
naics.justification: KEI's core activity is public-interest research and advocacy on intellectual-property and knowledge-access policy, matching a social advocacy organization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: KEI produces substantial original policy research alongside its advocacy work.
It engages with industry and government stakeholders on policy, though it is not a dues-based membership body.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: General fallback given its mixed research/advisory/advocacy activities.

naics.category_justification: KEI is an established nonprofit NGO engaged in public-interest research and advocacy rather than representing dues-paying members.

naics.resolved_name: Computing Research Association's Computing Community Consortium
naics.description: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) is a programmatic committee of the Computing Research Association (CRA), established in 2006 through a cooperative agreement with the National Science Foundation. It catalyzes and organizes the U.S. computing research community, running visioning workshops and producing reports that articulate high-impact research directions for policymakers, government, and industry. It is based at CRA headquarters in Washington, D.C.
naics.justification: CCC's primary activity is coordinating and representing the interests of the computing research community (academic departments, labs, and researchers) rather than performing research itself, which fits a professional organization that serves a field's practitioners.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: CCC funds visioning and workshops adjacent to research, but it does not itself conduct R&D.
Similar membership-representation structure, but CCC represents an academic/research field rather than businesses.
CCC is closely tied to academic computer science departments but is not itself a degree-granting institution.

naics.category_justification: CCC is a committee of the nonprofit Computing Research Association that coordinates and advocates for the academic computing research community, though its role also resembles a professional/trade body.

naics.description: Chegg, Inc. is a publicly traded education technology company based in Santa Clara, California. It provides online homework help, textbook rentals, tutoring, and other student support subscription services. Chegg targets primarily college and high school students in the United States.
naics.justification: Chegg's primary business is providing supplementary academic support services (homework help, tutoring, study materials) to students, which matches educational support services rather than a degree-granting institution.

alternates.justification: Chegg's homework-help and study tools are delivered as a subscription software/app platform.
Broad catch-all for its bundled support services if education-specific code were deemed inapplicable.
Chegg develops proprietary software and AI tools in-house to deliver its services.

naics.category_justification: Chegg is a for-profit, publicly traded corporation commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: Unlearn.AI is a San Francisco-based biotechnology/AI company that develops AI-generated 'digital twins' of clinical trial participants to reduce the size and duration of control groups in clinical trials. Its platform is trained on large volumes of historical patient data and is used by pharmaceutical sponsors to accelerate drug development. The company's methodology has been reviewed by regulators including the EMA and FDA.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
naics.justification: Unlearn.AI's core activity is developing and applying novel biomedical/clinical-trial modeling methods, which is closest to biotechnology R&D even though the product is delivered as software.

alternates.justification: The digital twin platform is fundamentally a software product built and licensed to pharma clients.
The platform could alternately be viewed as licensed software rather than custom development.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
alternates.justification: The work supports clinical trials but Unlearn.AI does not directly deliver patient care.

naics.category_justification: Unlearn.AI is a venture-backed, for-profit company selling its digital twin platform to pharmaceutical clients.

naics.resolved_name: Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association
naics.description: The Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) is a trade association representing securities firms, banks, and asset managers active in the U.S. capital markets. It advocates on securities regulation, market structure, and financial policy on behalf of its member firms. SIFMA is headquartered in New York and Washington, D.C.
naics.justification: SIFMA's defining activity is representing and advocating for its member firms in the securities industry, the core function of a business association.
naics.category_justification: SIFMA is a membership-based trade association representing the collective interests of securities and financial firms.

naics.description: The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is a San Francisco-based nonprofit organization founded in 1990 that advocates for civil liberties in the digital world, including free speech, privacy, and consumer rights online. It engages in impact litigation, policy advocacy, and technology development to protect digital rights. EFF frequently comments on technology and AI policy proceedings.
naics.justification: EFF's primary activity is advocacy and litigation to protect civil liberties and digital rights, which most closely matches human rights/civil liberties organizations.

alternates.justification: EFF's broader digital-rights advocacy could also fit general social advocacy.
EFF conducts significant impact litigation, though this is a means to its advocacy mission rather than a commercial legal practice.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: Catch-all category for nonprofit advocacy organizations not elsewhere classified.

naics.category_justification: EFF is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit civil liberties organization, not a membership trade body representing an industry's business interests.

naics.description: HR Policy Association is a Washington, D.C.-based trade association representing chief human resources officers of major U.S. corporations. It advocates on federal labor, employment, and human capital policy on behalf of its member companies. It also operates affiliated entities focused on health care and global HR policy.
naics.justification: The association's core function is representing the collective policy interests of corporate HR executives, the defining activity of a business association.

alternates.justification: Could alternately be viewed as a professional body for HR executives as individual practitioners.
Its federal policy advocacy work overlaps with general social/industry advocacy.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: General catch-all category for member organizations.

naics.category_justification: HR Policy Association is a membership organization representing corporate HR leaders' collective interests in policy debates.

naics.description: The Center for American Progress (CAP) is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit public policy research and advocacy organization associated with progressive politics. It produces policy research and analysis across economic, social, and technology issues and advocates for policy change. CAP was founded in 2003.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: CAP's primary activity is conducting policy research and analysis across social, economic, and political topics, matching R&D in the social sciences and humanities.

alternates.justification: CAP also engages heavily in direct policy advocacy and campaigning beyond pure research.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: General catch-all for nonprofit policy organizations.
CAP has a close affiliation with progressive political causes, though it is not itself a party or campaign committee.

naics.category_justification: CAP is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit think tank conducting research and advocacy rather than representing a defined membership base.

naics.description: TIC Council Americas is the regional arm of the TIC Council, a global trade association representing independent testing, inspection, and certification (TIC) companies. It advocates for members' interests in quality infrastructure, standards, and conformity assessment policy in North, Central, and South America. The global TIC Council is headquartered in Brussels.

naics.description: Chamber of Progress is a tech industry trade coalition that advocates for policies favorable to the technology sector, funded primarily by large technology companies. It publishes policy analysis and engages with lawmakers and regulators on issues including AI, antitrust, and platform regulation. It positions itself as a center-left-leaning industry association representing the tech sector's collective policy interests.
naics.justification: Chamber of Progress's primary activity is representing the collective policy interests of its technology-company funders/members before government, matching a business association's function.

alternates.justification: Its public-facing policy campaigns and framing also fit a general social advocacy classification.
Its industry-focused advocacy has some overlap with a professional/industry organization classification.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its policy-advisory activities have some resemblance to consulting, though it operates as an advocacy coalition rather than a fee-for-service consultancy.

naics.category_justification: Chamber of Progress functions as an industry-funded coalition advocating on behalf of technology companies' collective policy interests.

naics.description: The Confidential Computing Consortium is a Linux Foundation-hosted project that brings together hardware vendors, cloud providers, and software companies to advance confidential computing technology, which protects data in use through hardware-based trusted execution environments. It develops open-source tools, technical standards, and educational resources, and its members include major technology companies. It functions as an industry consortium rather than a single commercial entity.
naics.justification: The Consortium's primary activity is coordinating member companies' collaborative technical and standards work on confidential computing, matching a business-association-style function.

alternates.justification: Its development of open-source confidential computing tools has a software-development character.
Its technical standards-setting role among industry experts also resembles a professional/standards organization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Its collaborative technical development work has an engineering R&D character.

naics.category_justification: The Confidential Computing Consortium is explicitly an industry consortium of member companies collaborating on shared technical standards, hosted by the Linux Foundation.

naics.description: Friends of the Earth is an environmental advocacy nonprofit and part of the international Friends of the Earth federation, campaigning on climate change, environmental justice, and the ecological impacts of corporate and government activity, including the energy demands of AI and data centers. It engages in public campaigns, litigation, and policy advocacy in the United States. It is a longstanding environmental and environmental-justice organization.
naics.justification: Friends of the Earth's defining activity is environmental advocacy and campaigning, the core activity of this environmental organization code.

alternates.justification: Its broader environmental-justice and social-equity campaigning also fits a general social advocacy classification.
As a broad-based civic advocacy nonprofit, this general civic organization code is a distant alternative.
Some of its technical environmental analysis work has minor overlap with environmental consulting, though its primary mode is advocacy, not client-based consulting.

naics.category_justification: Friends of the Earth is a mission-driven environmental advocacy nonprofit, not a membership trade body representing industry interests.

naics.description: Compsim LLC is a small, women-owned technology company based in Brookfield, Wisconsin, that develops and licenses Knowledge Enhanced Electronic Logic (KEEL) technology, a software framework for building explainable, human-like reasoning into devices and applications. Founded in 1999, it targets licensing partnerships across sectors such as military, medical, finance, and industrial automation rather than selling products directly to end users. The company positions itself around explainable and adaptive AI technology.
naics.justification: Compsim's primary business model is developing and licensing its proprietary KEEL software technology to partner organizations, matching the software-publishing activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Given its small size and technology-licensing model, much of its work may be closer to applied R&D than mass software distribution.
Its partnership-based, customized technology integration work has a custom-programming character.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Some of its partner-facing technology guidance resembles specialized technical consulting.

naics.category_justification: Compsim LLC is a small, privately held, for-profit technology licensing company.

naics.description: ControlAI is a nonprofit organization, founded in 2023 by Andrea Miotti, that advocates for international prohibition of artificial superintelligence development while supporting continued narrower AI applications. It runs public policy campaigns targeting lawmakers in the UK, US, Canada, and Germany, including efforts against AI-generated deepfakes and for AI extinction-risk-focused legislation. ControlAI is a prominent voice in the AI safety advocacy movement.
naics.justification: ControlAI's defining activity is public advocacy and lobbying campaigns aimed at restricting advanced AI development due to safety/extinction-risk concerns, matching the social advocacy organization activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Some of its policy analysis (e.g., 'A Narrow Path') has a research/policy-development character.
Unlikely, but considered since it engages industry and policymakers; it is not a membership business association.
As a broad civic advocacy campaign organization, this general code is a distant alternative.

naics.category_justification: ControlAI is described as a non-profit dedicated to AI safety advocacy, not a membership trade body, university, or government unit.

naics.description: The Health IT End-Users Alliance is a coalition of health information professionals, physicians, hospitals, and other front-line healthcare provider organizations that use health IT systems in patient care. It advances end-user perspectives in health IT policy and standards development, including issuing consensus statements on topics such as AI in healthcare and social determinants of health data. There is no cost to participate, and it functions as a collective advocacy voice for health IT end users rather than a vendor or care provider itself.
naics.justification: The Alliance's core activity is representing its member healthcare provider organizations' collective policy positions on health IT standards and regulation, matching a business-association-style function.

alternates.justification: Its consensus-statement advocacy on health IT and health equity policy also fits a general social advocacy classification.
Its membership of health IT and clinical professionals has some overlap with a professional organization classification.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
alternates.justification: The candidate shortlist reflected its healthcare-provider membership base, though the Alliance itself does not deliver patient care.

naics.category_justification: The Health IT End-Users Alliance is explicitly a coalition of healthcare provider organizations coordinating a collective policy voice, matching the trade/coalition category.

naics.description: Plan International USA is the U.S. member of Plan International, a global children's rights and humanitarian development organization that runs programs on child sponsorship, education, health, and protection, particularly for girls, in developing countries. It engages in advocacy and program delivery, including on the responsible use of technology and AI affecting children's rights. It is a longstanding international development and humanitarian nonprofit.
naics.justification: Plan International USA's primary activity is delivering humanitarian and child-development relief programs (education, health, protection) internationally, matching emergency/relief services.

alternates.justification: Its focus on children's rights advocacy also fits a human rights organization classification.
Its broader advocacy work on children's welfare and technology policy fits general social advocacy.
Some program elements touching community services have minor overlap with this code, though it is a weaker fit than relief services.

naics.category_justification: Plan International USA is a mission-driven international humanitarian and children's development nonprofit.

naics.description: Wiley (John Wiley & Sons, Inc.) is a global publishing company known for academic journals, scholarly research publishing, textbooks, and professional/educational content. It also provides research analytics and AI-related publishing tools and has commented on federal AI policy regarding text-and-data mining, copyright, and research integrity. Wiley is a publicly traded company with a long history in scientific, technical, and educational publishing.
naics.justification: Wiley's core, longstanding business is publishing books, academic journals, and educational content, matching the book-publishing activity.

alternates.justification: A very large share of Wiley's revenue comes from academic journal (periodical) publishing rather than books specifically.
Wiley also offers digital research tools and platforms, which have a software-publishing character.
Wiley's educational content and training materials have some overlap with educational support services.

naics.category_justification: Wiley is a publicly traded, for-profit publishing corporation.

naics.description: PRISMAGuard LLC is a small Austin, Texas-based advisory firm founded by cybersecurity expert Mano Paul, offering fractional CTO/CISO services and AI and cybersecurity strategy, compliance, and educational programs for organizations. It develops AI cybersecurity training content and workshops for both management and operational staff. The company operates as a technology and cybersecurity consultancy rather than a product vendor.
naics.justification: PRISMAGuard's primary activity is providing fractional CISO/CTO advisory and AI/cybersecurity strategy services to client organizations, which fits computer systems design and related consulting services.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its fractional executive (CTO/CISO) advisory role has strong overlap with general management consulting.
Its AI cybersecurity workshops and educational programs for staff fit professional training services.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its broader technology/cybersecurity advisory work also fits general scientific/technical consulting.

naics.category_justification: PRISMAGuard LLC is a small, privately held, for-profit advisory and consulting firm.

naics.description: Digimarc Corporation is a publicly traded technology company based in Beaverton, Oregon, that develops digital watermarking and content authentication software used to identify and trace digital and physical media. Its products embed imperceptible signals into images, packaging, and video to support recycling sorting, brand protection, and content provenance. Digimarc has engaged with federal AI policy discussions around content authenticity and synthetic media detection.
naics.justification: Digimarc's primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary watermarking and content-verification software, which is the core business of a software publisher rather than a services or hardware firm.

alternates.justification: The company writes software, but it sells standardized licensed products rather than custom-built client software.

alternates.naics_title: Computer Terminal and Other Computer Peripheral Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Digimarc has historical ties to imaging hardware, but its current business is software and licensing, not manufacturing.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Digimarc does not primarily operate as a consulting firm.

naics.category_justification: Digimarc is a for-profit, publicly traded corporation commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: The Center for AI Policy is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit organization focused on advocating for federal legislation and regulatory measures to reduce catastrophic risks from advanced artificial intelligence. It engages with congressional staff and federal agencies to promote AI safety-oriented policy proposals. The organization positions itself as a policy advocacy group rather than a technical research lab.
naics.justification: The organization's core activity is advocating for specific AI safety policy outcomes with government, which fits the social advocacy classification rather than membership representation or direct research delivery.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The organization also produces policy research and draft legislation, which could be classified as R&D.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: As a niche policy nonprofit, it could fall into this catch-all category.
Less likely, as its focus is narrowly policy advocacy rather than general civic engagement.

naics.category_justification: It operates as a mission-driven policy advocacy nonprofit rather than a membership trade body, government unit, or university.
