naics.description: The Center for Health Security is a research and policy center within the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health that studies biosecurity, pandemic preparedness, and emerging technology risks, including AI's role in biological threats. It conducts research, publishes analyses, and advises policymakers on health security issues. As a university-based center, its work and staffing are integrated into Johns Hopkins University.
naics.justification: The center is an academic research unit of Johns Hopkins University; per NAICS practice for university sub-units, its primary activity is coded under the parent institution's higher-education classification.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Viewed as a standalone research center, its output is policy and social-science-oriented research and analysis.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: Some of its biosecurity work touches biotechnology research, though it is not a lab-bench biotech R&D operation.
The center engages in policy advocacy on health security, but this is secondary to its academic research role.

naics.category_justification: It is a center embedded within a degree-granting university's school of public health, so the record reflects the institution rather than an independent nonprofit.

naics.description: The University of Colorado Boulder is a public research university and the flagship campus of the University of Colorado system, offering undergraduate and graduate degrees across the sciences, engineering, humanities, and business. It conducts extensive federally funded research, including work in aerospace, computer science, and environmental science. The university regularly participates in federal policy comment processes related to research and technology.
naics.justification: The university's primary activity is degree-granting higher education, which is the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: It is unambiguously a public degree-granting university.

naics.description: Cleveland Clinic is a nonprofit multispecialty academic medical center headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, operating hospitals and outpatient clinics that provide patient care alongside medical research and physician training. It is one of the largest nonprofit hospital systems in the United States and is affiliated with a medical school. Cleveland Clinic engages in federal health and technology policy discussions relevant to clinical AI applications.
naics.justification: Cleveland Clinic's primary activity is operating hospitals delivering inpatient and outpatient medical and surgical care, matching this hospital code even though it also conducts research and education.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: Cleveland Clinic includes large physician practice groups, but its core identity is hospital-based care.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It conducts medical research, but this is not the correct R&D code and is secondary to patient care.
It has an affiliated medical school (Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine), but Cleveland Clinic itself is primarily a hospital system, not the degree-granting institution.

naics.category_justification: It is organized as a nonprofit hospital system rather than a government, university, or trade body, though it holds academic affiliations.

naics.description: BABL AI is a private company founded in 2018 that provides third-party algorithmic auditing and certification services, helping organizations assess AI systems for bias and compliance with regulations such as NYC Local Law 144 and the EU AI Act. It also offers consulting and training on responsible AI governance. BABL AI positions itself as an independent auditor using assurance methodologies similar to financial auditing.
naics.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
naics.justification: BABL AI's core service is independent technical assessment and auditing of AI systems, which is a specialized consulting activity not tied to a more specific NAICS code.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its AI governance advisory work resembles general management consulting.
BABL AI explicitly models its audits on financial-auditing assurance standards, though it is not an accounting firm.
It offers online education and certification on responsible AI, a smaller part of its business.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit firm selling auditing and consulting services in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: Truepic is a San Diego-based technology company that provides software and APIs for verifying the authenticity and provenance of photos and videos, aiming to combat deepfakes and digital fraud. Its tools are used by enterprises, marketplaces, and content platforms to establish content credentials. Truepic is a founding member of the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA).
naics.justification: Truepic's primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary content-verification software and APIs, characteristic of a software publisher.

alternates.justification: It also provides API integration services, which borders on custom programming work.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its verification service involves cloud-based processing, though this is not its primary identity.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Less likely, as Truepic sells a software product rather than consulting services.

naics.category_justification: Truepic is a privately held, for-profit technology company commenting on its own behalf.

naics.description: Panorama Global is a Seattle-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit, founded in 2015, that convenes funders, governments, nonprofits, and companies to collaborate on global health and social-impact challenges such as pandemic preparedness and violence against children. It operates as part of the broader Panorama Group alongside Panorama Action and Panorama Strategy. It receives significant funding from philanthropic sources, including the Gates Foundation.
naics.justification: Panorama Global's core activity is convening and advocacy work around global social-impact issues rather than direct service delivery, research, or membership representation, best matching a social advocacy organization code.

alternates.justification: Its role convening diverse stakeholders around social causes resembles a civic organization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It funds and coordinates research-driven initiatives, though it is not primarily a research producer itself.
It channels philanthropic funding to initiatives, though it functions more as a convening platform than a traditional grantmaking foundation.

naics.category_justification: It is registered as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that facilitates philanthropic and multi-stakeholder collaboration rather than representing a dues-paying membership.

naics.description: Cranium AI is a private technology company that provides an AI security and governance platform helping enterprises assess, monitor, and manage risks in their AI and machine learning systems. Its software addresses AI model vulnerabilities, compliance, and third-party AI risk management. The company markets itself to enterprises deploying AI at scale.
naics.justification: Cranium AI's primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary AI risk-management software platform, matching the software publisher classification.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It also provides advisory services on AI risk, bordering on technical consulting.
Its platform integrates with client AI systems, resembling systems design/integration work.
It addresses AI 'security,' but this code covers physical/electronic security systems, not software security platforms.

naics.category_justification: Cranium AI is a privately held, for-profit software company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: Synergist Technology (doing business as Synergist Technologies) is a private software company offering the AFFIRM platform, an AI Management System designed to help organizations govern AI risk and comply with frameworks such as NIST AI RMF, ISO 27001, and the EU AI Act. It also markets zero-trust cybersecurity compliance capabilities, often to government and enterprise clients. The company submitted comments to NIST on AI risk management.
naics.justification: The company's primary activity is developing and licensing a proprietary AI governance and compliance software platform, matching the software publisher classification.

alternates.justification: It works closely with government and enterprise clients on system integration for compliance, bordering on systems design services.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: It offers compliance consulting alongside its software product.
Some engagements may involve custom development work for government clients.

naics.category_justification: It is a privately held, for-profit software vendor commenting on its own behalf.

naics.description: America's Credit Unions is a national trade association formed in 2024 through the merger of the Credit Union National Association (CUNA) and the National Association of Federally-Insured Credit Unions (NAFCU). It represents credit unions before Congress and federal regulators, advocating on issues including data privacy, cybersecurity, and financial technology policy. The organization provides advocacy, compliance resources, and education to its member credit unions.
naics.justification: The organization's core activity is representing and advocating for its member credit unions' collective interests, which is the defining activity of a business association.

alternates.justification: This code applies to actual credit unions providing financial services, not the association representing them.

alternates.naics_title: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
alternates.justification: Despite 'union' in some member names, this is a trade/business association, not a labor union.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A general catch-all, less fitting than the specific business association code.

naics.category_justification: It is explicitly a membership trade association representing the credit union industry, formed from the merger of two prior trade associations.

naics.description: RAND Corporation is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research institute headquartered in Santa Monica, California, that conducts policy analysis and research for U.S. and international government agencies, militaries, and other clients across national security, health, economics, and technology. It operates several federally funded research and development centers (FFRDCs) and publishes extensively on public policy issues, including AI governance. RAND funds a graduate school, the Pardee RAND Graduate School, as part of its research mission.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: RAND's primary activity is conducting contract research and policy analysis across social science, economic, and policy domains, matching this R&D code even though it also touches technical and security topics.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: RAND also conducts substantial technical, engineering, and national-security research that spans beyond social sciences.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Some RAND engagements resemble policy consulting, though its core identity is research rather than consulting.
RAND operates a graduate school, but that is a subsidiary activity of the larger research institute.

naics.category_justification: RAND is organized as a nonprofit research institute rather than a government agency, university, or membership association, though it operates federally funded research centers.

naics.description: NetChoice is a trade association representing e-commerce and internet companies, advocating for free-market principles and against regulation it views as burdensome to online businesses, including in areas of content moderation, data privacy, and child online safety. It frequently engages in litigation challenging state and federal technology laws. Its members include major internet and technology companies.
naics.justification: NetChoice's core activity is representing and advocating for its member internet and e-commerce companies' shared policy interests, matching the business association code.

alternates.justification: Much of its activity is policy advocacy and litigation rather than traditional trade-association services to members.
It frequently engages in litigation, though it is not itself a law firm.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A general catch-all, less fitting than the specific business association code.

naics.category_justification: It is a membership-based trade association advocating for internet and e-commerce companies.

naics.description: Lambda (also known as Lambda Labs) is a private company that provides GPU cloud computing infrastructure and hardware optimized for AI and machine learning workloads, including training and inference services for AI developers. It sells cloud compute instances as well as on-premises GPU servers and workstations. Lambda has commented on federal AI and computing infrastructure policy.
naics.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
naics.justification: Lambda's primary activity is providing cloud-based GPU computing infrastructure for AI workloads, matching this code's coverage of computing infrastructure providers.

alternates.justification: Lambda also designs and sells GPU servers and workstations as hardware products.

alternates.naics_title: Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: A minor part of its business involves reselling hardware, though this is not its primary activity.
It offers some systems integration work for enterprise AI infrastructure, though cloud infrastructure provision is primary.

naics.category_justification: Lambda is a privately held, for-profit company commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: The Technology Trade Regulation Alliance (TTRA) is a trade association of small, medium, and large technology companies—spanning software, hardware, semiconductors, and medical devices—focused on global trade regulation and compliance. It maintains Customs and Export Controls committees with over 350 trade compliance and policy professionals from member companies. TTRA engages in advocacy on customs classification, export controls, and trade agreement issues affecting the technology sector.
naics.justification: TTRA's core activity is representing member technology companies on shared trade-regulation and customs-compliance advocacy, matching the business association classification.

alternates.naics_title: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Some of its committee work resembles trade-compliance consulting, though it is member-driven advocacy rather than a fee-for-service consultancy.
Its regulatory advocacy work has an advocacy component, though it is primarily organized around business/trade interests.
Less fitting, as TTRA is member-governed rather than a fee-based business services vendor.

naics.category_justification: It is explicitly structured as a membership-based industry alliance representing technology companies on trade policy.

naics.description: The Payments Leadership Council is a CEO-led coalition of major U.S. payments companies, including American Express, Discover, FIS, Fiserv, Global Payments, Mastercard, and Visa, formed to promote public policies supporting innovation, competition, and consumer protection in the payments industry. It engages with policymakers on issues such as data security, financial technology regulation, and payments infrastructure. The council issues public comments and statements on relevant federal legislation and regulation.
naics.justification: The council's core function is coordinating shared policy advocacy among competing payments companies, matching the business association classification even though it is structured as a CEO council rather than a traditional dues-based association.

alternates.naics_title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities
alternates.justification: Its member companies operate in payments processing, but the council itself does not process transactions.
Its activity is largely policy advocacy rather than traditional member services.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A general catch-all for organizations that do not fit cleanly elsewhere.

naics.category_justification: It is an industry coalition of company CEOs organized specifically to advance shared policy positions for the payments sector.

alternates.naics_title: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities
alternates.justification: If this were a government advisory board rather than an industry group, this public-administration code could apply instead.

naics.description: The Internet Infrastructure Coalition (i2Coalition) is a trade association representing companies that build and operate the internet's foundational infrastructure, including web hosting, cloud computing, and data center providers. It advocates before Congress and federal agencies on policy issues such as data privacy, cybersecurity, and internet governance affecting its member companies. Its membership includes hosting providers, domain registrars, and cloud service companies.
naics.justification: The coalition's core activity is representing and advocating for its member internet infrastructure companies, matching the business association classification.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: This code describes its members' industry, but the coalition itself provides advocacy rather than hosting services directly.
Its policy advocacy work has an advocacy component, though it is member-representation focused.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A general catch-all, less fitting than the specific business association code.

naics.category_justification: It is explicitly organized as a membership trade association for internet infrastructure companies.

naics.description: The Global Anti-Scam Alliance (GASA) is an international nonprofit coalition based in the Netherlands that brings together governments, consumer protection organizations, law enforcement, and companies to combat online fraud and scams. It publishes global research on scam trends, provides victim support resources, and coordinates cross-border anti-scam initiatives. GASA engages with U.S. and international regulators on consumer protection and online safety policy.
naics.justification: GASA's core activity is coordinating advocacy, research, and awareness efforts against online scams across a multi-stakeholder membership, best matching a social advocacy organization.

alternates.justification: Its broad public-awareness and consumer-protection mission resembles a civic organization.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: GASA publishes research reports on scam trends, though this is not its primary activity.

naics.category_justification: It functions as a multi-stakeholder coalition of governments, companies, and consumer groups united around a shared anti-scam mission, fitting the coalition category even though it also carries nonprofit traits.

Cloudflare regularly participates in federal technology, privacy, and AI policy discussions.

naics.justification: GitHub's primary activity is developing and licensing software products and platforms (including Copilot and Enterprise offerings) to developers and organizations, matching the software publishing code.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Very close alternate given GitHub's core function as a hosted code-repository and infrastructure service.
Ruled out as secondary; GitHub provides a standardized platform product rather than custom programming services.
Discarded; not a meaningful fit for GitHub's software-hosting business model, included only as a low-confidence third alternate.

naics.category_justification: GitHub is a for-profit software company operating as a wholly owned subsidiary of Microsoft, commenting in its own or its parent's commercial interest.

naics.resolved_name: AH Capital Management, L.L.C. (Andreessen Horowitz / a16z)
naics.description: AH Capital Management, L.L.C., known as Andreessen Horowitz or 'a16z,' is a Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. The firm invests in technology companies across sectors including software, fintech, crypto, biotech, and artificial intelligence, and manages tens of billions of dollars in assets across numerous funds. a16z is an active participant in AI policy discussions, often advocating for lighter-touch regulation of AI development.
naics.justification: a16z's primary activity is raising and deploying venture capital funds into portfolio companies, which NAICS classifies under intermediation activity for firms of this type.

alternates.justification: Very close alternate given a16z's core function as an investment management firm.
Plausible alternate given the firm's active portfolio management role for its funds' investors.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; a16z's primary business is capital deployment, not fee-based management consulting.

naics.category_justification: a16z is a for-profit venture capital firm advocating on AI policy in its own commercial and portfolio interest.

naics.description: AE Studio is a bootstrapped product development, design, and data science agency that builds custom software and AI applications for startups and enterprises. It has also expanded into AI alignment and safety research, working on interpretability and deception-reduction techniques for language models. Profits from client consulting work are reinvested into internal research projects, including a brain-computer interface initiative.
naics.justification: AE Studio's core, revenue-generating activity is custom software and product development for client startups and enterprises, which is the defining activity of this code, even though it also conducts AI alignment research.

alternates.justification: The firm also designs and integrates technology systems for clients as part of its consulting engagements.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A meaningful share of its work is dedicated AI alignment/safety research rather than client delivery.
Some offerings resemble licensed software products rather than bespoke client programming.

naics.category_justification: AE Studio is a privately held, for-profit consulting and technology agency serving corporate clients.

naics.resolved_name: Brookhaven National Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy)
naics.description: Brookhaven National Laboratory is a U.S. Department of Energy multiprogram national laboratory in Upton, New York, managed under contract by Brookhaven Science Associates. It conducts basic and applied research in nuclear and high-energy physics, energy technology, and environmental and national-security science, operating major user facilities such as particle accelerators. As a DOE national lab, it serves the federal government's science and energy research mission.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: Brookhaven's primary activity is conducting physical and engineering science research for the Department of Energy, which plainly matches this R&D code.
naics.category_justification: It is a federally owned Department of Energy national laboratory (a contractor-operated federal facility), consistent with the Government category.

naics.description: NERC is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority designated by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission as the Electric Reliability Organization for North America. It develops and enforces mandatory reliability standards for the bulk power system across the United States, Canada, and part of Mexico, and monitors and assesses grid reliability. NERC also trains and certifies industry personnel involved in grid operations.
naics.naics_title: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities
naics.justification: NERC's core function is developing and enforcing reliability regulations for the electric utility industry, which matches this public-administration-style regulatory code even though NERC is legally a private nonprofit rather than a government agency.

alternates.justification: NERC could alternatively be viewed as an industry self-governance body representing electric utilities.

alternates.naics_title: Electric Bulk Power Transmission and Control
alternates.justification: NERC does not itself operate transmission assets, making this a weaker fit despite its grid focus.
NERC also certifies and trains grid-reliability professionals, though this is not its primary activity.

naics.category_justification: NERC is structured as a private nonprofit corporation performing a delegated regulatory function under FERC oversight, rather than being itself a government body.

naics.resolved_name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy)
naics.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory is the largest U.S. Department of Energy science and energy national laboratory, located in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and managed under contract by UT-Battelle. It conducts research in neutron science, nuclear science, advanced materials, high-performance computing, and energy technologies, operating major user facilities such as the Spallation Neutron Source. ORNL supports both civilian science and national security missions for the federal government.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: ORNL's primary activity is physical and engineering science research conducted for the Department of Energy, which is a direct match for this R&D code.
naics.category_justification: It is a federally owned Department of Energy national laboratory (contractor-operated federal facility), consistent with the Government category.

naics.description: Leidos is a publicly traded Fortune 500 science and technology company headquartered in Reston, Virginia, that provides systems integration, IT services, engineering, and research and development primarily to U.S. defense, intelligence, civil, and health government agencies. Its work spans cybersecurity, systems engineering, logistics, and advanced analytics. It is one of the largest government-focused technology contractors in the United States.
naics.justification: Leidos' largest business lines involve designing, integrating, and managing IT and systems solutions for government clients, which best characterizes its primary activity despite a diversified portfolio.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A substantial share of Leidos' defense and intelligence work is R&D-oriented engineering and scientific research.
Leidos is also commonly classified under engineering services given its origins and government engineering contracts.
Leidos performs some operations and facilities-support contracts for government sites, though this is a minor share of revenue.

naics.category_justification: Leidos is a publicly traded, for-profit government-services corporation acting in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: Planet Labs PBC is a publicly traded (NYSE: PL) public benefit corporation that operates the world's largest constellation of Earth-observation satellites. It captures and sells daily satellite imagery and geospatial analytics used for agriculture, defense and intelligence, environmental monitoring, and civil government applications. The company markets its data primarily as a subscription-based geospatial analytics service rather than as a telecommunications carrier.
naics.justification: Planet Labs' primary commercial activity is producing and selling geospatial imagery and mapping analytics derived from its satellites, which aligns with mapping/surveying services more than satellite communications carriage.

alternates.justification: Planet Labs owns and operates the satellites that generate its data, which could also be viewed as a satellite operations business.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: The company delivers its imagery through a cloud-based data platform.
Not a strong fit, but included as a low-confidence alternate given the technical/analytical nature of the business.

naics.category_justification: Planet Labs is a publicly traded, for-profit corporation, notwithstanding its public benefit corporation legal structure.

naics.description: Utilidata is a Rhode Island-based technology company that develops distributed artificial intelligence software and hardware, branded Karman, for the electric grid edge, embedding AI compute into smart meters and grid devices. Its platform, built on NVIDIA hardware, analyzes grid data in real time to improve reliability and integrate distributed energy resources. The company began as a provider of grid substation optimization software before expanding into AI-enabled grid-edge products.
naics.justification: Utilidata's core product is a licensed AI software platform (Karman) for grid devices, which is best captured by software publishing even though it is delivered alongside partner hardware.

alternates.naics_title: Instruments and Related Products Manufacturing for Measuring, Displaying, and Controlling Industrial Process Variables
alternates.justification: Utilidata's technology is embedded in physical grid-monitoring and control hardware modules.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The company performs significant applied R&D in grid AI technology.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Utilidata's origins included grid optimization consulting/software services for utilities.

naics.category_justification: Utilidata is a privately held, for-profit technology company.

It collaborates closely with the University of Utah's NSF-funded WIRED Global Center, a hub for research on power grid resilience against climate-driven disturbances such as wildfires and extreme weather. Both units operate as research programs within the University of Utah.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)

naics.description: Symbium is a San Francisco-based technology company that builds software to streamline citizen and contractor interactions with government permitting, focused initially on residential decarbonization projects such as solar, storage, and heat pumps. Its proprietary Complaw technology, originating from Stanford's AI Lab, automates regulatory compliance analysis so users can instantly determine what permits a property needs. Symbium's instant permitting service has been implemented in more than 50 U.S. jurisdictions.
naics.justification: Symbium's primary business is licensing a proprietary software platform (Complaw) that automates permitting and compliance analysis, matching software publishing.

alternates.justification: The company also integrates its software directly with municipal permitting systems, resembling systems design work.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Symbium's regulatory-analysis service does not fit neatly into a single professional-services code.
Not a fit; included only because the company operates adjacent to government permitting functions it does not itself administer.

naics.category_justification: Symbium is a privately held, for-profit software company.

naics.description: Rhizome Data, founded in 2023, is a Washington, D.C.-based startup that builds an AI-powered climate resilience platform for electric utilities. Its software combines historical utility equipment performance data with global climate models to predict grid failures from extreme weather events such as snowstorms and wildfires. Rhizome markets its platform to help utilities prioritize grid-hardening investments.
naics.justification: Rhizome's primary offering is a licensed SaaS analytics platform for utilities, matching the software publishing code.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)

naics.category_justification: Rhizome Data is a privately held, venture-backed for-profit startup.

naics.description: Edison Electric Institute (EEI) is the trade association representing all U.S. investor-owned electric companies. It advocates on behalf of its member utilities before Congress, regulators, and other policymakers on energy, environmental, and grid policy issues, and provides industry research, benchmarking, and standards support. EEI's international members also include electric utilities outside the United States.
naics.justification: EEI's defining activity is representing and advocating for its investor-owned electric utility members, the core activity of a business association code.

naics.category_justification: EEI is explicitly a membership trade association representing investor-owned electric utility companies.

naics.description: RoarTech Inc. is a Washington, D.C.-area minority- and women-owned small business that provides cloud architecture, cloud migration, DevSecOps, and enterprise governance consulting, largely to U.S. Department of Defense and federal government clients. It supports digital transformation initiatives across people, process, and technology for government customers.
naics.justification: RoarTech's core business is designing and implementing cloud, IT, and data systems for government clients, matching computer systems design services.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services

naics.category_justification: RoarTech is a privately held, for-profit government IT consulting firm.

naics.description: Hortus AI is a small, bootstrapped technology company that operates Trellis, a marketplace and evaluation platform intended to help businesses, governments, and nonprofits choose AI tools that serve the public interest across sectors such as housing, finance, education, and healthcare. naics.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
naics.justification: Hortus AI's core product is an online marketplace/directory and evaluation service for AI tools, which most closely matches an information/portal service rather than software development itself.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services

naics.category_justification: Hortus AI is described as a revenue-generating company rather than a registered nonprofit, though its public-interest mission introduces some ambiguity.

naics.description: The American Statistical Association (ASA) is the leading professional membership association for statisticians and data scientists in the United States. It promotes statistical practice, research, and education, publishes journals, sets professional and ethical standards, and advocates on public policy issues involving statistics and data. Founded in 1839, it is one of the oldest professional societies in the country.
naics.justification: ASA's primary activity is operating as a professional membership society for statisticians, directly matching this code.

alternates.justification: ASA offers professional education and training, but it is not a degree-granting institution.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services

naics.description: The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) is a professional membership organization of pediatricians dedicated to child health, with roughly 67,000 members. It publishes clinical guidelines and policy statements, provides continuing medical education, and advocates before Congress and federal agencies on child health, safety, and technology policy issues, including AI in pediatric care. AAP is headquartered in Itasca, Illinois.

naics.resolved_name: Carnegie Mellon University and University of Pittsburgh
naics.description: Carnegie Mellon University and the University of Pittsburgh are two private and public research universities, respectively, located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, that jointly submitted comments on federal AI policy. Both are major research institutions with significant computer science, robotics, and AI research programs, and frequently collaborate on regional technology initiatives. Each institution offers undergraduate, graduate, and professional degree programs.
naics.justification: Both organizations are degree-granting universities, which is an unambiguous match for this code.
naics.category_justification: Both named entities are the universities themselves, not sub-units or affiliated nonprofits.

naics.description: GitLab is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: GTLB) software company that develops and sells a DevSecOps platform used by software teams to plan, build, secure, and deploy code. It offers both open-source and paid enterprise editions of its software, along with cloud-hosted and self-managed deployment options. GitLab is headquartered in San Francisco and operates as an all-remote company.
naics.justification: GitLab's core business is developing and licensing its DevSecOps software platform, a clear match for software publishing.
naics.category_justification: GitLab is a publicly traded, for-profit software company acting in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: Human AI Labs, Inc., doing business as Personal AI, is a San Francisco-based startup founded in 2020 that develops AI products for personal productivity and communication. Its core technology, the Generative Grounded Transformer, trains personalized language models on an individual's own data rather than broad internet data, aiming to create privacy-centric AI personas. The company has raised venture seed funding to develop this proprietary model.
naics.justification: Personal AI's primary offering is a licensed AI software application/platform, matching software publishing.

alternates.justification: The company conducts applied AI model research, though this NAICS code is intended for physical/engineering sciences rather than software AI research.

naics.category_justification: Personal AI (Human AI Labs, Inc.) is a privately held, venture-funded for-profit startup.

naics.resolved_name: Advanced Medical Technology Association (AdvaMed) - Medical Imaging Division

The division specifically represents manufacturers of imaging equipment such as MRI, CT, and ultrasound systems.

naics.description: Noblis is a not-for-profit science, technology, and strategy organization headquartered in Reston, Virginia, that provides research, engineering, and advisory services to U.S. federal government clients across defense, homeland security, intelligence, and civil agencies. It was originally formed in 1996 as Mitretek Systems, a spin-off from the MITRE Corporation, before being renamed Noblis. Noblis employs nearly 2,000 people combining scientific research, digital engineering, and emerging technology to solve complex federal challenges.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: Noblis' primary activity is applied scientific and engineering research and advisory work for federal government clients, matching this R&D code.

alternates.justification: A substantial portion of Noblis' government work involves IT systems design and integration.
Noblis' origins and much of its work are engineering-services oriented.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Noblis also provides strategic advisory services to federal agencies.

naics.category_justification: Noblis is explicitly organized as a not-for-profit corporation, distinct from a for-profit government contractor.

naics.resolved_name: Brennan Center for Justice (NYU School of Law) and Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), joint filing with other organizations
naics.description: This record represents a joint comment filed by the Brennan Center for Justice, a nonpartisan law and policy institute affiliated with New York University School of Law, together with the Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), a nonprofit research and advocacy organization focused on privacy and civil liberties, and other unnamed co-signing organizations. Both named organizations conduct legal research, litigation, and advocacy on government accountability, privacy, and technology policy issues, including AI. The 'et al.' indicates additional civil-society co-signers not individually listed.
naics.justification: The named organizations primarily conduct policy research and advocacy on civil liberties and government accountability issues, which best fits this social-advocacy code rather than a narrower human-rights or academic code.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Both organizations produce substantial legal and policy research, which could alternatively be classified as social-science R&D.
EPIC and the Brennan Center touch on civil-liberties/human-rights themes, though their focus is broader policy and legal advocacy.
The Brennan Center is affiliated with NYU Law School, but operates as an independent nonprofit rather than as the university itself.

naics.category_justification: This is an ad hoc, multi-organization joint policy comment ('et al.') from civil-society nonprofits acting together, matching the coalition definition even though it is not a permanent membership body.

naics.description: Datavant is a health information technology company, headquartered in New York, that operates a data-exchange platform connecting more than 80,000 hospitals and clinics, the majority of large U.S. health systems, and all major U.S. payers. It enables healthcare organizations to securely link, de-identify, and exchange patient data for uses including clinical research, analytics, and AI-ready applications. Datavant merged with Ciox Health in 2021, becoming the largest medical record retrieval company in the U.S.
naics.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
naics.justification: Datavant's core business is operating a data-processing and exchange platform for healthcare data, matching this code.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
alternates.justification: Datavant's record-retrieval business touches health-services administration, though it does not deliver clinical care itself.
Datavant develops significant proprietary software to power its data platform.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Not a strong fit; included as a low-confidence catch-all given the specialized nature of health-data intermediary services.

naics.category_justification: Datavant is a privately held, for-profit health technology company.

naics.description: The Alliance for Digital Innovation (ADI) is a nonprofit trade association representing commercial technology companies that sell IT products and services to the U.S. public sector. It advocates for modernizing government technology acquisition, developing a skilled government IT workforce, and encouraging adoption of innovative technologies to address federal IT challenges. ADI has been led by Matthew Cornelius since 2019 and engages in federal advocacy including comments on technology regulations.
naics.justification: ADI's defining activity is representing and advocating for its member commercial technology companies' collective interests in government IT policy, matching this business association code.

alternates.justification: A weaker fit given ADI's membership is companies rather than individual professionals.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Not a fit; ADI does not provide direct consulting services itself.
Not applicable; ADI is a private association, not a government body.

naics.category_justification: ADI is explicitly described as a trade body/unified voice for its member commercial technology companies.

naics.resolved_name: The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights - Center for Civil Rights and Technology
naics.description: The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights is a coalition of more than 200 national civil rights, labor, and human rights organizations that advocates for federal civil rights policy. Its Center for Civil Rights and Technology focuses specifically on how technologies such as artificial intelligence affect civil rights, working to ensure technology policy accounts for equity and nondiscrimination. The Leadership Conference coordinates joint advocacy positions across its member organizations on behalf of the broader civil rights community.
naics.justification: The Leadership Conference's core mission is civil and human rights advocacy, and its technology-focused center applies that mission to AI policy, matching this code.

alternates.justification: The Conference's broad social-justice advocacy work could also fit this more general social-advocacy code.
Not a strong fit; the Conference is a coalition of civil-society organizations, not businesses.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The Center for Civil Rights and Technology conducts some policy research, though advocacy is its dominant activity.

naics.category_justification: The Leadership Conference is explicitly organized as a coalition of over 200 member civil rights and human rights organizations coordinating joint advocacy.

refs.raw_name: Association of University Technology Managers, Inc. (AUTM)

naics.resolved_name: Association of University Technology Managers, Inc. (AUTM)
naics.description: AUTM is a professional membership association for individuals involved in managing intellectual property and technology transfer at universities, research institutions, hospitals, and government agencies. It provides training, certification, networking, and advocacy on policy issues affecting academic technology transfer and commercialization, such as patent policy. AUTM's members work at the intersection of research institutions and industry to move discoveries from the lab to the marketplace.
naics.justification: AUTM's core activity is operating as a professional membership society for technology-transfer managers, matching this code.

alternates.justification: AUTM provides substantial certification and training programs for its members.
A weaker fit since AUTM's membership consists of individual professionals rather than companies.
Not a fit; AUTM is not itself a degree-granting institution despite its university-affiliated membership.

naics.category_justification: AUTM is a professional membership association representing technology-transfer managers' collective professional interests.

naics.description: Exhaustless Inc. is an Ann Arbor, Michigan-based company, led by CEO Steven P. Endres, that designs and conducts market-based auctions to allocate scarce airport, highway, and waterway capacity, such as takeoff and landing slots at congested airports. It holds patents related to airport capacity and thrust-assist aircraft technology, and has run slot auctions at major airports including JFK, LaGuardia, Newark, and Amsterdam. Exhaustless advocates before federal agencies such as the DOT for market-based congestion-management policy.
naics.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
naics.justification: Exhaustless provides a specialized market-design and auction-administration service for allocating transportation capacity, which does not map to a more specific NAICS code and is best captured by this catch-all professional-services code.

alternates.justification: Exhaustless' core function is running competitive market-clearing auctions, conceptually similar to an exchange, though for airport slots rather than securities.
The company's advisory and policy work with transportation agencies resembles management consulting.
Exhaustless is involved in airport slot allocation, though it does not operate airport facilities itself.

naics.category_justification: Exhaustless is a privately held, for-profit company commenting in its own commercial capacity as a market-mechanism provider.

display_name: PhRMA (Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America)

refs.raw_name: PhRMA (Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America)

naics.resolved_name: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA)
naics.description: PhRMA is the trade association representing the leading U.S. biopharmaceutical research and manufacturing companies. It advocates on behalf of member companies before Congress, federal agencies, and the courts on issues including drug pricing, intellectual property, regulatory policy, and the use of AI in drug discovery and development. PhRMA also funds policy research and public education campaigns related to the pharmaceutical industry.
naics.justification: PhRMA's defining activity is representing and advocating for its member pharmaceutical manufacturing companies, matching this business association code.

alternates.justification: Not a fit; PhRMA's members manufacture pharmaceuticals, but the association itself does not manufacture drugs.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: PhRMA funds some policy research, though advocacy for members is its dominant activity.
A weaker fit since PhRMA's membership consists of companies rather than individual professionals.

naics.category_justification: PhRMA is explicitly a trade association representing pharmaceutical manufacturing companies' collective interests.

naics.resolved_name: Askeladden L.L.C. (The Clearing House Payments Company's Patent Quality Initiative)
naics.description: Askeladden L.L.C. is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Clearing House Payments Company L.L.C., a banking association and payments company owned by major U.S. commercial banks. Askeladden operates the Patent Quality Initiative (PQI), which advocates for improving patent examination quality and reforming patent litigation, particularly as it affects the financial services industry. It engages with the USPTO, courts, and Congress on patent policy issues, including those touching AI-related inventions.
naics.justification: As the patent-policy advocacy arm of a bank-owned payments association, Askeladden's core activity is representing member banks' interests in patent policy, matching this business association code.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Askeladden's patent-quality research and analysis work resembles a specialized professional service.
Its patent-policy advocacy involves substantial legal analysis, though it is not itself a law firm.

alternates.naics_title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities
alternates.justification: Its parent, The Clearing House, is a payments/clearinghouse company, but Askeladden itself does not process transactions.

naics.category_justification: Askeladden functions as the patent-policy advocacy arm of a bank industry association, representing member banks' collective interests.

naics.description: Amazon.com, Inc. is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: AMZN) multinational technology and e-commerce conglomerate headquartered in Seattle, Washington. Its business spans online and physical retail, cloud computing and AI infrastructure through Amazon Web Services, digital advertising, streaming media, and consumer devices. Amazon is one of the world's largest companies by revenue and a major commenter on federal AI and technology policy.
naics.justification: Under the 2022 NAICS revision, large general-merchandise online retailers such as Amazon are classified under Department Stores, and retail e-commerce remains Amazon's largest single revenue segment even though the company is highly diversified.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Amazon Web Services is a major, highly profitable segment providing cloud computing and AI infrastructure.
Some AWS professional-services offerings involve systems design and integration work for enterprise customers.
A general retail catch-all that could apply given Amazon's broad merchandise mix.

naics.category_justification: Amazon is a publicly traded, for-profit multinational corporation.

naics.description: Pindrop is an Atlanta, Georgia-based company that develops voice authentication, fraud detection, and deepfake/voice-clone detection software, primarily for call centers and financial institutions. Its platform analyzes voice and behavioral signals to verify caller identity and flag fraudulent or AI-generated voice interactions in real time. Pindrop is a privately held, venture-backed technology company.
naics.justification: Pindrop's core business is licensing a proprietary voice-security and authentication software platform, matching software publishing.

alternates.justification: Pindrop also integrates its platform into customers' call-center and security infrastructure.
The company's fraud-detection function is a form of security service, though delivered as software rather than physical/network security monitoring.

alternates.naics_title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities
alternates.justification: Pindrop's largest customer base is financial institutions, though it does not process transactions itself.

naics.category_justification: Pindrop is a privately held, for-profit voice-security software company.

naics.description: The High Tech Inventors Alliance (HTIA) is a nonprofit coalition formed in 2017 by major technology companies, including Amazon, Google, Intel, Microsoft, and Salesforce, to advocate for balanced patent policy. HTIA's members collectively hold hundreds of thousands of U.S. patents and advocate for improving patent examination quality, supporting inter partes review, and reforming patent litigation practices. It engages with the USPTO, courts, and Congress on patent-related policy issues.
naics.justification: HTIA's core activity is representing and advocating for its member technology companies' collective interests in patent policy, matching this business association code.

alternates.justification: HTIA's patent-policy work is legally focused, though it is not itself a law firm.
A weaker fit since HTIA's membership consists of companies rather than individual professionals.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Not a strong fit; included as a low-confidence catch-all.

naics.category_justification: HTIA is explicitly a coalition of major technology companies formed to advocate jointly on patent policy.

Without a verified match, no reliable description of its business activity can be given.
naics.justification: The name and docket (a USPTO patent RFI) suggest a possible intellectual-property law or consulting practice, but this could not be confirmed, so the code is a low-confidence guess.

Plausible if the entity is an IT/network services firm, matching one unverified "Neo IP" telecom company found in France.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)

naics.description: Americans for Prosperity Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit affiliated with the broader Americans for Prosperity network, engaged in public-policy education, litigation, and research promoting limited-government and free-market positions. It conducts legal advocacy (including open-records and regulatory litigation) and publishes policy analysis on issues such as technology regulation and government transparency. It is organizationally distinct from its sister entity Americans for Prosperity, a 501(c)(4) lobbying arm.
naics.justification: The Foundation's primary activity is public-interest policy research, education, and litigation advocacy rather than direct member representation, fitting the general social-advocacy category.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Much of its output is policy research and analysis, which this R&D code also captures.
A generic civic-organization fit, but less precise than the dedicated advocacy code.
The Foundation runs a significant litigation practice, but this is a program within a broader advocacy mission rather than a law-firm business model.

naics.category_justification: It is a 501(c)(3) educational/legal nonprofit pursuing a policy mission rather than representing a dues-paying membership base, distinguishing it from a trade association.

naics.description: Palisade Research is a nonprofit organization, based in Berkeley, California and founded in 2023, that conducts empirical research demonstrating dangerous or offensive capabilities in frontier AI systems, such as autonomous hacking, deception, and resistance to shutdown commands. Its work is aimed at informing policymakers and the public about existential and security risks from advanced AI. It was founded by cybersecurity researcher Jeffrey Ladish.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: Palisade's primary activity is empirical technical research on AI systems' capabilities and risks, which NAICS captures under this general engineering/physical-science R&D code since no dedicated computer-science R&D code exists.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Its work also feeds policy analysis and public communication, which leans toward social-science-oriented research.
Its research is conducted partly to advocate for AI safety policy, though its core output is technical demonstration rather than advocacy campaigning.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Considered but ruled out because Palisade is a research nonprofit, not a fee-for-service consultancy.

naics.category_justification: Palisade is a registered nonprofit conducting research in the public interest rather than a membership or for-profit body.

naics.description: ControlAI is an advocacy organization, founded in 2023 by Andrea Miotti, that campaigns for binding international regulation of advanced/superintelligent AI, briefing lawmakers in the UK, US, and EU and promoting its "Direct Institutional Plan" for AI safety. It engages in direct policy outreach rather than technical research, lobbying parliamentarians and submitting comments to government AI policy processes. It has expanded from UK-focused campaigning to the US, Canada, and Germany.
naics.justification: ControlAI's core activity is public and legislative advocacy for AI-safety regulation, which is the defining feature of this social-advocacy code.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Some of its output involves policy analysis, though its primary mode is direct advocacy/lobbying rather than research publication.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all considered but less precise than the dedicated advocacy code.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; ControlAI does not provide paid consulting services to clients.

naics.category_justification: ControlAI functions as a mission-driven advocacy nonprofit campaigning on AI safety policy rather than representing a dues-paying membership.

naics.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is a publicly traded American technology company that designs, manufactures, and sells enterprise servers, storage systems, networking equipment, and hybrid-cloud and high-performance computing solutions. It was spun off from Hewlett-Packard Company in 2015 to focus on enterprise IT infrastructure and services. HPE serves large businesses, governments, and data-center operators worldwide.
naics.justification: HPE's primary activity is designing and manufacturing servers and enterprise computing hardware, which matches this code even though it also sells software and services.

alternates.justification: HPE also derives significant revenue from IT systems integration and consulting services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: HPE's GreenLake cloud/as-a-service offerings resemble infrastructure-as-a-service, though hardware sales remain its core business.

alternates.naics_title: Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: Ruled out; HPE is a manufacturer and solutions provider, not primarily a wholesale distributor.

naics.category_justification: HPE is a publicly traded for-profit corporation commenting on its own commercial and regulatory interests.

naics.description: Encode Justice (also known as Encode) is a youth-led nonprofit advocacy organization focused on promoting safe and responsible artificial intelligence policy. It organizes students and young people to engage in public education, grassroots organizing, and advocacy campaigns aimed at AI safety and governance, and has submitted comments to U.S. federal AI policy proceedings. The organization has chapters and volunteers across multiple countries.
naics.justification: Encode Justice's core activity is public advocacy and grassroots organizing around AI safety policy, matching this social-advocacy code.

alternates.justification: Its youth-chapter, community-organizing structure also resembles a civic/social organization model.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: It occasionally publishes policy analysis, but advocacy/organizing is its dominant activity, not research production.
Ruled out; its public-education activities are advocacy-driven rather than a formal educational-services business.

naics.category_justification: Encode Justice is a mission-driven, volunteer-based advocacy nonprofit rather than a dues-paying trade or professional membership body.

naics.description: Convergence Analysis is a nonprofit international AI existential-risk strategy think tank, with contributors across the UK, US, Canada, and Portugal, that produces sociotechnical reports on AI scenarios and governance recommendations. It grew out of a research collaboration on existential risk strategy begun in 2017 and now conducts public-awareness efforts and convenes events such as its Threshold conference on the economic impacts of transformative AI. Its team spans AI governance, technical alignment, and hardware research.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: Convergence Analysis's core output is scenario and governance research on AI's societal and economic trajectory, which fits R&D in the social sciences even though some of its work touches technical AI alignment.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Some team members work on technical AI alignment and hardware research, which leans toward engineering-oriented R&D.
It also runs public-awareness campaigns, an advocacy-adjacent activity, though research production is its primary output.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic fallback considered but less precise than the dedicated R&D code.

naics.category_justification: Convergence Analysis is a nonprofit research think tank pursuing a public-interest mission rather than representing a dues-paying membership.

naics.description: METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) is a nonprofit research organization that develops methods to evaluate frontier AI models for dangerous autonomous capabilities, such as the ability to self-replicate or conduct sophisticated cyberattacks. It works directly with leading AI developers (including OpenAI and Anthropic) to run pre-deployment capability evaluations and has published widely cited research on AI capability trends. It emerged from earlier work at the AI safety group ARC Evals.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: METR's primary activity is technical research developing and running empirical AI-capability evaluations, which falls under this general engineering/physical-science R&D code in the absence of a dedicated computer-science R&D code.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: METR's evaluation work with AI labs resembles technical consulting, though it operates as a research nonprofit rather than a fee-based consultancy.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Its work informs AI governance and policy discussions, a social-science-adjacent application of its technical research.
Ruled out as secondary; METR's core output is technical evaluation research, not advocacy campaigning.

naics.category_justification: METR is a nonprofit research organization conducting technical AI-safety evaluation work in the public interest.

naics.description: Group 42 Holding Ltd, known as G42, is an Emirati artificial intelligence holding company headquartered in Abu Dhabi, UAE, founded in 2018, that develops AI systems, cloud computing infrastructure, and data platforms deployed across government, healthcare, and enterprise sectors. It is chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan and backed by Mubadala, Microsoft, and Silver Lake, among others. G42 has formed major partnerships, including a strategic investment from Microsoft in 2024.
naics.justification: The entity is legally structured and named as a holding company overseeing AI and technology subsidiaries, matching this code, though its operating subsidiaries are primarily engaged in AI computing infrastructure.

alternates.justification: Fits the company's formal holding-company structure as named.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: G42's actual operating activity is providing AI cloud computing and data infrastructure, which this code captures more functionally.
Some subsidiary work involves custom AI software development, though this is not the parent holding entity's primary described activity.

naics.category_justification: G42 is a for-profit corporate holding company commenting in its own commercial interest, notwithstanding partial state-linked investment ownership.

display_name: Center for AI Risk Management & Alignment

refs.raw_name: Center for AI Risk Management & Alignment

naics.resolved_name: Center for AI Risk Management & Alignment (CARMA), a project of Social & Environmental Entrepreneurs, Inc.
naics.description: The Center for AI Risk Management & Alignment (CARMA) is a research and policy think tank, operating as a project of the 501(c)(3) nonprofit Social & Environmental Entrepreneurs, Inc., dedicated to managing risks from advanced AI so that such systems remain controllable, aligned, and trustworthy. It brings together experts in AI, policy, infrastructure resilience, and international governance to conduct risk modeling and public-safety-preparedness work, including frameworks such as Probabilistic Risk Assessment for AI. CARMA integrates technical safety research with policy analysis on both acute and systemic AI risks.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: CARMA's core activity is interdisciplinary risk-management and governance research on AI, which spans policy and technical domains but leans toward social-science-oriented research and analysis.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Some of its work, such as technical risk modeling, is more engineering/technical in nature.
Its public-safety-preparedness advocacy work touches on social-advocacy activity, though research is its primary described output.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; CARMA is a research and policy nonprofit, not a fee-based management consultancy.

naics.category_justification: CARMA operates as a project of a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit pursuing public-interest AI risk research rather than representing a paying membership.

naics.description: CTIA – The Wireless Association is a U.S. trade association representing the wireless communications industry, including mobile network carriers, device manufacturers, and related technology companies. It advocates before Congress, the FCC, and other federal agencies on spectrum policy, wireless infrastructure, and technology regulation, and hosts industry events such as the former CTIA trade show. It represents member companies' collective interests rather than operating a wireless network itself.
naics.justification: CTIA's defining activity is representing wireless-industry member companies in policy advocacy, matching the trade/business-association code rather than any telecommunications-carrier or manufacturing code.
naics.category_justification: CTIA is a membership-based trade association representing wireless carriers and manufacturers' collective policy interests.

naics.description: AdvaMed (the Advanced Medical Technology Association) is a U.S. trade association representing medical device, diagnostics, and digital health technology companies. It advocates on regulatory, reimbursement, and market-access policy affecting the medical technology industry before Congress, FDA, CMS, and other federal agencies. Its membership spans large multinational device makers and smaller innovative medtech firms.
naics.justification: AdvaMed's core activity is representing medical-technology companies' collective policy and regulatory interests, matching the trade/business-association code.
naics.category_justification: AdvaMed is a membership-based trade association advocating for the medical technology industry's collective interests.

naics.description: Web research could not confidently identify an organization named "The Institute for New Frontiers"; searches surfaced similarly named but distinct entities (such as the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy and the CSIS Hess Center for New Frontiers) without confirming any of them as a match. naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities

naics.resolved_name: Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF), a Linux Foundation project
naics.description: The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) is a cross-industry initiative hosted by the Linux Foundation that develops standards, tools, and best practices to improve the security of open-source software supply chains. Its members include major technology companies, cloud providers, and software vendors that collaborate on projects addressing vulnerabilities and supply-chain risk in open-source code. OpenSSF also engages in public policy discussions on software and AI supply-chain security.
naics.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
naics.justification: OpenSSF is a nonprofit, cross-industry consortium coordinating shared open-source security standards and tooling, an activity that does not map cleanly onto a single business, professional, or R&D code, so this catch-all fits best.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)

Its member companies collaborate on shared industry interests, resembling a business/trade association structure.

naics.category_justification: OpenSSF is a multi-stakeholder, industry-member-driven coalition coordinating shared standards, matching the collective-representation focus of this category even though it is structured as a nonprofit foundation project.
