naics.description: The Open University (OU) is a distance-learning and research public university based in Milton Keynes, United Kingdom, established in 1969 to provide flexible, open-access higher education. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree programs primarily through distance and online learning, and conducts academic research across many fields, including technology and AI. It is one of the largest universities in the UK by student enrollment.
naics.justification: The Open University's primary activity is providing accredited degree programs, matching this code despite its distance-learning delivery model.
naics.category_justification: It is an accredited, degree-granting public university, notwithstanding its distinctive distance-learning format.

naics.description: The National Education Association (NEA) is the largest labor union and professional employee organization in the United States, representing public school teachers, education support professionals, and other education employees. It engages in collective bargaining support, lobbying, and advocacy on education policy, including the use of AI in classrooms. NEA is headquartered in Washington, D.C., with affiliates in every state.
naics.naics_title: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
naics.justification: NEA's primary activity is representing education employees' collective interests and engaging in labor advocacy, which is the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: NEA is a labor union representing the collective interests of its education-employee membership.

naics.resolved_name: Center for AI and Digital Policy
naics.description: The Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP) is a nonprofit research and advocacy organization based in Washington, D.C., that focuses on AI governance, human rights, and democratic values in AI policy. It publishes an annual global AI policy report, trains fellows in AI policy, and files comments and complaints with regulators including the FTC and NIST. CAIDP was founded by AI policy expert Merve Hickok and Marc Rotenberg.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: CAIDP's primary activity is producing AI-policy research, reports, and analysis, matching this R&D code, though its heavy regulatory-advocacy component also resembles social advocacy.

alternates.justification: CAIDP files formal regulatory complaints and advocates for specific AI governance policies, which is a significant advocacy function.
Its fellowship and training programs provide an educational function, though this is secondary to its research and advocacy.
It is not primarily a membership body for practitioners.

naics.category_justification: CAIDP is a nonprofit research and advocacy organization, not a membership trade body, university, or government entity.

naics.description: The Committee on Artificial Intelligence Applications to Environmental Science is a standing committee of the American Meteorological Society (AMS), a nonprofit professional and scientific society for atmospheric, oceanic, and hydrologic scientists. The committee promotes the development, evaluation, and application of AI and machine learning methods to weather, climate, and environmental science problems. It organizes conference sessions and educational activities within AMS on this topic.

naics.description: The Duke Clinical Research Institute (DCRI) is the academic clinical research organization of Duke University School of Medicine, based in Durham, North Carolina. DCRI collaborates with pharmaceutical companies, government agencies, and other academic medical centers.

naics.resolved_name: Christian Reformed Church in North America
naics.description: The Christian Reformed Church in North America (CRCNA) is a Protestant Reformed denomination with congregations across the United States and Canada, tracing its roots to Dutch Reformed immigrants in the 19th century. It coordinates worship, theological education, missions, and social ministries across its member congregations, and its leadership periodically issues public statements on ethical and social issues, including technology and AI. It is governed by synods composed of representatives from local congregations.

naics.justification: AFSCME's primary activity is representing and bargaining on behalf of its member workers, the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: AFSCME is a labor union, a membership body organized to represent workers' collective interests.

naics.description: DePaul University is a private Catholic research university in Chicago, Illinois, founded by the Vincentian order in 1898. It is one of the largest Catholic universities in the United States, offering undergraduate and graduate programs across colleges including business, law, and computing. It maintains multiple campuses in the Chicago area.
naics.justification: DePaul University's primary activity is degree-granting higher education.
naics.category_justification: It is an accredited, degree-granting private university.

naics.description: The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is a public university within the University of California system that focuses exclusively on graduate-level health sciences education, research, and patient care. It includes schools of medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and nursing, along with UCSF Health, its affiliated hospital system. UCSF is a leading center for biomedical research.
naics.justification: UCSF's primary activity is graduate and professional health-sciences education, matching this higher-education code even though it also operates a major hospital system.
naics.category_justification: UCSF is a public university within the University of California system.

naics.description: The University of California, Berkeley is a public research university and the flagship campus of the University of California system, founded in 1868. It offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate, graduate, and professional degree programs and is a leading center for research, including in artificial intelligence and computer science. It is located in Berkeley, California.
naics.justification: UC Berkeley's primary activity is degree-granting higher education and academic research.
naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting research university.

naics.description: Olaris, Inc. is a precision medicine company based in Framingham, Massachusetts, that combines metabolomics analysis with machine learning to develop diagnostic tests. Its myOLARIS platform analyzes patient metabolic signatures to support treatment selection in areas such as oncology and organ transplantation. The company has received investment from Labcorp and obtained a unique AMA procedural code for one of its diagnostic tests.
naics.justification: Olaris develops and runs diagnostic laboratory tests for clinical use, matching a medical laboratory classification, though it is also fundamentally an R&D-driven diagnostics company.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: Olaris is heavily focused on developing new metabolomic biomarker technology, which fits a biotechnology R&D classification well.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Its combination of chemistry (NMR-based metabolomics) and machine learning R&D also fits this broader life-sciences R&D code.
If Olaris is viewed as manufacturing a diagnostic test/reagent product rather than running a lab service, this code would apply instead.

naics.category_justification: Olaris is a venture- and corporate-backed, for-profit precision medicine diagnostics company.

naics.description: Columbia University is a private Ivy League research university in New York City, founded in 1754 as King's College. It offers undergraduate, graduate, and professional degrees across numerous schools, including law, business, medicine, and engineering. It is one of the oldest and most prominent higher-education institutions in the United States.
naics.justification: Columbia University's primary activity is degree-granting higher education.
naics.category_justification: It is an accredited, degree-granting private university.

naics.resolved_name: Stanford University's Digital Economy Lab (Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research)
naics.description: The Digital Economy Lab is a research initiative housed within the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR) at Stanford University. It studies the economic effects of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, on labor markets, productivity, and the broader economy. It is directed by Stanford faculty and produces academic and policy-oriented research.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: The lab's primary activity is conducting economics research on the impact of digital technologies, matching social-science R&D; it operates as a research unit of Stanford University.

alternates.justification: As a Stanford University unit, it could alternatively be classified under the parent institution's general higher-education code.
The candidate shortlist suggested this government economic-administration code, but the lab is a university research unit, not a government program administrator.

alternates.naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
alternates.justification: Some economic research involves survey methods, though this is not the lab's primary focus.

naics.category_justification: The Digital Economy Lab is a research unit within Stanford University's SIEPR, sharing the university's category.

naics.description: Dell Technologies is a multinational technology company headquartered in Round Rock, Texas, that designs, manufactures, and sells personal computers, servers, storage systems, and enterprise IT infrastructure. It also provides related IT services and solutions to businesses and consumers worldwide. The company is publicly traded and one of the largest computer hardware makers globally.
naics.justification: Dell's primary activity is designing and selling computer hardware (PCs, servers, storage), the defining activity of this manufacturing code, even though it also sells IT services.

alternates.justification: Dell also provides substantial IT infrastructure and systems design services alongside its hardware business.

alternates.naics_title: Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: A portion of Dell's model involves direct distribution/sale of hardware, resembling wholesale distribution.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Dell also offers cloud and hosted infrastructure services, a smaller but growing part of its business.

naics.category_justification: Dell Technologies is a publicly traded, for-profit multinational technology company.

naics.description: O'Reilly Media is a U.S. publishing and online learning company best known for its technical books on programming, technology, and business topics, often recognized by their animal-illustration covers. It also operates the O'Reilly online learning platform, offering courses, videos, and live training for technology professionals. The company was founded by Tim O'Reilly in 1978.
naics.justification: O'Reilly Media's historic and namesake primary activity is publishing technical books, matching this code, though it has increasingly shifted toward an online learning subscription platform.

alternates.justification: The O'Reilly online learning platform now delivers courses and training, which closely matches educational support services.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Its digital content platform could alternatively be classified as an online information service.
O'Reilly Media historically also organized technology conferences, a secondary line of business.

naics.category_justification: O'Reilly Media is a privately held, for-profit publishing and online education company.

naics.description: India is a sovereign nation in South Asia; the record's name refers to a comment submitted on behalf of the national government rather than a specific named ministry or agency. National governments participate in U.S. federal AI policy dockets through embassies, trade missions, or specific ministries such as those overseeing technology or commerce.
naics.justification: Without a named sub-agency, a general international-affairs/foreign-government code is used to represent India's national government commenting on U.S. policy, though the specific ministry is unknown.

alternates.justification: If the comment came from a general executive government office rather than a foreign-affairs body, this code would apply instead.
If the comment originated from a commerce or economic ministry, this would be a plausible alternative code.
If the comment reflected national-security concerns about AI, this would be a lower-likelihood alternative.

naics.category_justification: The record name is a sovereign nation, indicating a national government commenter, even though the specific ministry or office is unspecified.

naics.description: The North Dakota University System is the state government agency that governs North Dakota's eleven public colleges and universities, operating under the State Board of Higher Education. It sets policy, coordinates budgets, and oversees academic programs across the state's public higher-education institutions but does not itself grant degrees. It is headed by a Chancellor and is part of North Dakota's state government.
naics.justification: The System's primary activity is government administration and policy coordination across public higher-education institutions, rather than direct instruction, matching this public-administration code.

alternates.justification: Because the System encompasses degree-granting institutions collectively, a higher-education code is also a reasonable classification.
As a general state administrative body, this broader government-support code is a plausible alternative.

alternates.naics_title: Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing
alternates.justification: This candidate from the keyword-matched shortlist (matching on the word 'system') is not a plausible fit.

naics.category_justification: The North Dakota University System is a state government agency governing higher education, distinct from any single university it oversees.

normalized_name: metropolitan water district of southern california
display_name: Metropolitan Water District of Southern California

refs.raw_name: Metropolitan Water District of Southern California

naics.resolved_name: Metropolitan Water District of Southern California
naics.description: The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California (MWD) is a public agency and regional water wholesaler that supplies drinking water to nearly 19 million people across six counties in Southern California. It is governed by a board of directors representing its member public agencies and manages large-scale water infrastructure, including aqueducts and treatment facilities. MWD is one of the largest water suppliers in the United States.
naics.justification: MWD's primary activity is wholesale supply and distribution of treated water, the defining activity of this utilities code.

alternates.justification: MWD generates some hydroelectric power from its aqueduct system, a minor secondary activity.

alternates.naics_title: Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction
alternates.justification: MWD builds and maintains major aqueduct infrastructure, a supporting activity to its core water-supply mission.

alternates.naics_title: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities
alternates.justification: As a public agency, it could be viewed as a regional utility administrator rather than a direct operator, though it directly owns and runs the water system.

naics.category_justification: MWD is a public agency created by California state law and governed by representatives of its member public water agencies.

naics.description: Code.org is a U.S. nonprofit organization founded in 2013 that promotes computer science education in K-12 schools. It provides free curriculum, teacher training, and platforms such as the Hour of Code to expand access to computer science, particularly among underrepresented groups. It partners with school districts and policymakers to expand computer science education policy nationwide.
naics.justification: Code.org's primary activity is providing curriculum, training, and educational support resources to schools rather than directly granting degrees or operating as a school itself, matching educational support services.

alternates.justification: As a broad civic-minded nonprofit advocating for CS education policy, a civic organization code is a plausible alternative.
Code.org also engages in policy advocacy for computer science education, which could be its primary classified activity.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Code.org distributes some of its curriculum through online platforms, a weaker alternative to educational support services.

naics.category_justification: Code.org is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization focused on expanding computer science education access.

naics.description: The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) is a public research university in Enugu State, Nigeria, founded in 1960 as the first indigenous university in the country. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs across faculties including sciences, engineering, medicine, agriculture, and the social sciences. The university conducts research and community outreach across Nigeria and West Africa.
naics.justification: The organization is a degree-granting public university whose primary activity is higher education instruction and research, matching this code exactly.
naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting university in Nigeria.

naics.resolved_name: College of Healthcare Information Management Executives (CHIME)
naics.description: CHIME (the College of Healthcare Information Management Executives) is a U.S.-based professional association for chief information officers and other senior healthcare IT executives, with thousands of members worldwide. It provides education, professional development, networking, and advocacy on health information technology and policy, including AI in healthcare. CHIME regularly submits comments to federal agencies such as NIST and CMS on health IT and data policy.
naics.justification: CHIME's core activity is operating a membership-based professional association for healthcare IT executives, providing education and advocacy, which matches professional organizations.

alternates.justification: CHIME could be viewed as a broader social/civic membership body, though it is more specifically a professional association.
CHIME organizes conferences for its members, but this is secondary to its core professional-association mission.
CHIME offers professional development/certification programs, but this is not its primary activity.

naics.category_justification: CHIME is a membership association representing healthcare IT executives' collective professional interests.

normalized_name: juelsgaard intellectual property and innovation clinic
display_name: Juelsgaard Intellectual Property and Innovation Clinic

refs.raw_name: Juelsgaard Intellectual Property and Innovation Clinic

naics.resolved_name: Stanford Law School's Juelsgaard Intellectual Property and Innovation Clinic
naics.description: The Juelsgaard Intellectual Property and Innovation Clinic is a legal clinic within Stanford Law School's Mills Legal Clinic, established with support from alumnus Stephen Juelsgaard. Law students, under faculty supervision (led by Phillip Malone), represent nonprofits, startups, and individuals on intellectual property and technology policy matters, including AI regulation, online speech, and privacy. It engages in litigation, counseling, and policy advocacy on innovation-related law.
naics.justification: The clinic is an academic teaching unit of Stanford Law School staffed by students for course credit, so its primary activity is legal education, sharing the parent university's educational services code, though it also delivers legal services.

alternates.justification: The clinic directly represents clients in legal matters, which resembles a law office's core activity.
Some of its work is technology-policy advocacy rather than direct legal education or representation.
Some clinic activities resemble general legal services outside a standard law office.

naics.category_justification: It is an in-house clinical teaching program of Stanford Law School, part of the university itself rather than an independent organization.

naics.description: The University of Memphis is a public research university located in Memphis, Tennessee, offering undergraduate, graduate, and professional degree programs. It conducts research across a wide range of disciplines including engineering, business, health sciences, and education. The university engages in community and economic development activities in the Memphis region.
naics.justification: The organization is a public degree-granting university whose primary activity is higher education instruction and research.
naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting state university.

naics.description: AI & Partners is an Amsterdam-based professional services firm that helps companies comply with the EU AI Act and other AI governance regulations. It provides a software-based AI governance platform for inventorying and monitoring AI systems, along with regulatory compliance assessments and impact-assessment advisory services. The firm serves organizations across Europe navigating AI regulatory requirements.
naics.justification: The firm's primary activity is advising clients on AI regulatory compliance strategy and risk assessment, which is a specialized management consulting service, though it also sells a software platform.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Its advisory and governance-framework work could also be classified as general management consulting.
The firm also licenses a proprietary AI governance software platform, which could be its primary revenue driver.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: The specialized, hybrid nature of AI-regulatory advisory work does not cleanly fit a single professional-services code.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit consultancy/software vendor commenting in its own commercial capacity on AI regulation.

naics.description: The Beaufort-Jasper Water and Sewer Authority (BJWSA) is a public authority created by the South Carolina General Assembly in 1954 that provides water and wastewater services to Beaufort and Jasper counties in the South Carolina Lowcountry. It operates water treatment, distribution, and sewer collection/treatment infrastructure, including for several municipalities and military installations. BJWSA also runs one of the state's first sustainable water reclamation facilities.
naics.justification: The authority's primary activity is operating a public water supply system, though it also operates sewer/wastewater treatment, so a single water-focused code understates half its mission.

alternates.justification: BJWSA also operates significant wastewater/sewer treatment infrastructure, which could be considered co-primary with water supply.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Air and Water Resource and Solid Waste Management Programs
alternates.justification: As a public authority, its activities could alternatively be viewed as government program administration rather than direct utility operation.

alternates.naics_title: Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction
alternates.justification: The authority also builds water/sewer infrastructure, though construction is not its core ongoing activity.

naics.category_justification: It is a special-purpose public authority created by South Carolina state statute to provide water/sewer utility service, i.e., a local government body.

naics.description: 3M Innovative Properties Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of 3M Company that holds, manages, and licenses 3M's global intellectual property portfolio, including over 100,000 patents. It handles patent filing, prosecution, and licensing on behalf of its parent, 3M, a diversified industrial and consumer products manufacturer. The subsidiary is the named assignee on many of 3M's patent filings with the USPTO.
naics.naics_title: Lessors of Nonfinancial Intangible Assets (except Copyrighted Works)
naics.justification: The subsidiary's defining activity is holding and licensing intellectual property (patents) on behalf of its parent, which matches licensing/leasing of intangible assets.

alternates.justification: As a corporate IP-holding subsidiary, it could alternatively be classified as a holding company office.
Its patents cover parent 3M's diversified manufacturing businesses, which could inform classification if the subsidiary is viewed as inseparable from 3M's manufacturing operations.
The subsidiary's IP-counsel office handles patent prosecution work resembling legal services.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit corporate subsidiary of 3M Company managing intellectual property assets.

naics.description: The University of Tennessee at Chattanooga is a public university and part of the University of Tennessee System, offering undergraduate and graduate degree programs. It conducts teaching and research across colleges including business, engineering, health, and the arts and sciences. The university serves the Chattanooga region and broader state of Tennessee.
naics.justification: The organization is a public degree-granting university whose primary activity is higher education instruction and research.
naics.category_justification: It is a public university within the University of Tennessee System.

naics.resolved_name: City of Philadelphia's Philadelphia Water Department
naics.description: The Philadelphia Water Department (PWD) is a municipal government department that provides drinking water, wastewater collection and treatment, and stormwater management services for the City of Philadelphia. It operates water treatment plants, distribution systems, and sewer infrastructure serving over 1.5 million residents. PWD also engages in green stormwater infrastructure initiatives and environmental compliance programs.
naics.justification: The department's primary activity includes operating a public water supply system, though its wastewater/sewer treatment mission is equally central.

alternates.justification: PWD also operates major wastewater treatment plants, which could be considered co-primary with water supply.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Air and Water Resource and Solid Waste Management Programs
alternates.justification: As a city government department, its function could alternatively be classified as public program administration.

alternates.naics_title: Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction
alternates.justification: The department also builds and maintains water/sewer infrastructure, though this is not its sole ongoing activity.

naics.category_justification: It is a municipal government department of the City of Philadelphia.

naics.description: The Ohio State University is a large public land-grant research university headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, offering undergraduate, graduate, and professional degree programs. It conducts extensive research across engineering, medicine, agriculture, business, and the sciences. The university also operates a major academic medical center and extension services throughout Ohio.
naics.justification: The organization is a public land-grant university whose primary activity is higher education instruction and research.
naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting state university.

naics.description: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit organization founded in late 2023 that advocates for federal AI governance policy. It works with lawmakers, national security experts, and civil society groups to develop bipartisan legislation addressing AI risks such as scams, privacy harms, and AI-powered weapons, while preserving U.S. AI competitiveness. ARI does not accept funding from for-profit corporations or non-U.S. entities to preserve its independence.
naics.justification: ARI's primary activity is public-interest advocacy for AI policy and legislation, which fits a social advocacy organization rather than research, membership representation, or government administration.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: ARI also produces policy research and analysis to support its advocacy, which resembles social-science R&D.
It could be viewed more broadly as a civic organization engaging on public issues.
Its policy coalition-building work with industry and government stakeholders has some overlap with business-association activity, though it is not membership-based.

naics.category_justification: ARI is a mission-driven, non-membership nonprofit organization pursuing AI policy advocacy in the public interest, not itself a membership body representing dues-paying members.

naics.resolved_name: International Union, United Automobile, Aerospace and Agricultural Implement Workers of America (UAW)
naics.description: The International Union, United Automobile, Aerospace and Agricultural Implement Workers of America (UAW) is a major U.S. labor union representing workers in the automotive, aerospace, agricultural equipment, and other manufacturing industries. It negotiates collective bargaining agreements, represents workers in grievances, and advocates on workplace policy issues including automation and AI's effect on jobs. The UAW has submitted comments to federal agencies on technology and labor policy.
naics.naics_title: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
naics.justification: The organization's defining activity is representing unionized workers and negotiating labor agreements, which is the core activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: A labor union is a membership body representing workers' collective interests, matching this category.

naics.description: Waxman Strategies is a Washington, D.C.-based public affairs firm founded by former Congressman Henry Waxman that provides policy, lobbying, and communications services. The firm represents clients in areas such as health care, environment, and telecommunications/technology policy. It engages with federal agencies and Congress on behalf of paying clients on regulatory and legislative matters.
naics.justification: Lobbying and public-affairs firms of this kind are conventionally classified under public relations agencies, as the firm's core activity is managing clients' public policy image and government relations rather than legal representation.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The firm's strategic policy advisory work also resembles general management consulting.
Some of its communications strategy work overlaps with marketing consulting.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Lobbying/policy consulting is a hybrid professional service not cleanly captured by a single code.

naics.category_justification: Waxman Strategies is a for-profit consultancy; when it comments on dockets it is typically acting as a paid advisor for named or unnamed clients rather than expressing its own substantive stake.

naics.resolved_name: The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights
naics.description: The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights is a coalition of over 200 national organizations working to promote civil rights, voting rights, and social/economic justice in the United States. It advocates for federal policy on issues including algorithmic bias, AI, and technology's impact on marginalized communities. The coalition coordinates joint statements and comments from its member organizations on legislative and regulatory matters.
naics.justification: The coalition's core mission is advocating for civil and human rights, matching this code's focus on organizations promoting human rights causes.

alternates.justification: Its broader social/economic justice advocacy work could also fit general social advocacy.
As a broad coalition of civic groups, it could be viewed as a civic/social organization.
It functions somewhat like a coalition/association, though its members are advocacy groups rather than businesses.

naics.category_justification: It is explicitly a coalition of member civil-rights organizations that coordinates and represents their collective advocacy positions.

naics.description: S&P Global is a publicly traded American financial information and analytics company known for its credit ratings (S&P Global Ratings), market intelligence, commodity insights, and stock market indices (S&P Dow Jones Indices). It provides data, research, and benchmarks used by investors, governments, and businesses worldwide. The company has commented on federal AI policy given its use of AI in financial data analysis and ratings.
naics.justification: S&P Global's core business, credit ratings and financial analytics, is conventionally classified under miscellaneous financial investment activities rather than a single narrower financial code.

alternates.justification: Its ratings business shares similarities with credit-reporting activities, though S&P Global rates securities/issuers rather than consumer credit.
S&P Global Market Intelligence sells data/analytics platforms that resemble software/data publishing.

alternates.naics_title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities
alternates.justification: Some index/benchmark administration work has minor overlap with financial transaction processing, though this is not its core activity.

naics.category_justification: S&P Global is a publicly traded, for-profit financial information and analytics company.

naics.description: AArete is a Chicago-headquartered global management and technology consulting firm founded in 2008, specializing in strategic profitability improvement, digital transformation, and data-driven advisory services. It serves clients across healthcare, private equity, retail, financial services, the public sector, and higher education. The firm has been recognized by Forbes as one of the world's best management consulting firms.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: AArete's core business is providing management and strategy consulting services to organizations across industries, directly matching this code.

alternates.justification: Some of its specialized data/digital-transformation consulting could fall under this narrower consulting code.
Its digital transformation work includes technology implementation, which overlaps with custom software services.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Its broad advisory scope spans multiple professional service types.

naics.category_justification: AArete is a for-profit management consulting firm.

naics.resolved_name: Institute for Systems and Technologies of Information, Control and Communication (INSTICC)
naics.description: INSTICC (the Institute for Systems and Technologies of Information, Control and Communication) is a scientific, non-profit association headquartered in Setubal, Portugal. It organizes international scientific conferences and workshops in fields such as artificial intelligence, software technologies, and information systems, and disseminates related research. INSTICC operates conferences across multiple European countries and publishes proceedings from its events.
naics.justification: INSTICC's primary observable activity is organizing recurring international scientific conferences and workshops, matching convention/event organizing, even though it self-describes as a scientific association.

alternates.justification: As a scientific association serving a professional/research community, it could instead be classified as a professional organization.
Its non-profit association structure has some overlap with general civic/social organizations.
Its conferences serve an educational/professional-development function for researchers.

naics.category_justification: INSTICC describes itself as a scientific, non-profit association promoting research dissemination, rather than a government, university, or dues-based trade group.

display_name: United States Patent and Trademark Office

United States Patent and Trademark Office

naics.resolved_name: United States Patent and Trademark Office
naics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) is a federal agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce responsible for examining and granting patents and registering trademarks. It administers intellectual property law, advises the federal government on IP policy, and has engaged in AI policy matters including AI and inventorship and generative AI's effect on IP. USPTO also participates in international IP cooperation efforts.
naics.naics_title: Regulation, Licensing, and Inspection of Miscellaneous Commercial Sectors
naics.justification: USPTO's core function is examining and granting patents/trademarks, a regulatory/licensing activity over intellectual property matters, matching this public-administration code.

alternates.justification: USPTO could also be seen as administering broader federal economic/innovation programs.
Patent examination involves legal review akin to prosecution/counsel functions, though it is not litigation-focused.
USPTO staff include patent examiners with legal training, though the agency itself is not a law office.

naics.category_justification: USPTO is a federal government agency within the Department of Commerce.

naics.resolved_name: Bridgestone Corporation's Bridgestone Americas Holding Co.
naics.description: Bridgestone Americas Holding Co. is the U.S. holding company subsidiary of Bridgestone Corporation, the Japan-based multinational tire and rubber manufacturer. It oversees Bridgestone's North, Central, and South American operations, including tire manufacturing, retail, and related businesses. Bridgestone Americas has engaged with the USPTO on patent policy matters relevant to its manufacturing and technology innovations.
naics.justification: As the named entity is a regional holding company overseeing subsidiary operations rather than a manufacturing plant itself, it best matches the holding-company management code.

alternates.justification: The holding company's underlying business, and that of its parent Bridgestone, is tire manufacturing, which could be the more meaningful primary-activity code.

alternates.naics_title: Motor Vehicle Supplies and New Parts Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: Bridgestone Americas also distributes tires and parts through wholesale channels.
Ruled out because Bridgestone Americas Holding Co. is not a bank holding entity, though it shares the generic holding-company structure.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit corporate holding subsidiary of Bridgestone Corporation, a multinational manufacturer.

naics.description: Astris AI is a subsidiary launched by Lockheed Martin in December 2024 to enable secure AI adoption across the U.S. defense industrial base and other high-assurance industries. It provides end-to-end AI engineering and consulting services, including strategy, implementation, training, and generative AI/machine learning system development, with a focus on data control and defense-grade security. Astris AI partners with cloud and technology providers such as Dell, HPE, and Oracle.
naics.justification: Astris AI's primary offering is custom AI system engineering, development, and implementation services for clients, which matches custom computer programming/systems development.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Astris AI also provides AI strategy and governance consulting, which overlaps with management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: As part of Lockheed Martin's defense engineering portfolio, some of its work may be closer to applied engineering R&D.
Its systems engineering work for defense clients has overlap with engineering services.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit subsidiary of Lockheed Martin providing commercial AI engineering and consulting services.

naics.description: AMIA (the American Medical Informatics Association) is a U.S. non-profit professional association for biomedical and health informatics professionals, with over 6,400 members in more than 65 countries. It advances translational bioinformatics, clinical informatics, and public health informatics through education, research promotion, and policy advocacy, and serves as the official U.S. representative to the International Medical Informatics Association. AMIA regularly comments on federal health IT and AI policy.
naics.justification: AMIA's core activity is operating a membership-based professional association for informatics professionals, matching this code.

alternates.justification: It could broadly be viewed as a civic/social membership organization, though it is more specifically a professional body.
Some of its policy advocacy work overlaps with general social advocacy.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: Its research-promotion activities have minor overlap with professional/technical services, though membership association is the better fit.

naics.category_justification: AMIA is a membership-based professional association representing informatics professionals' collective interests.

naics.description: Danaher Corporation is a publicly traded American conglomerate headquartered in Washington, D.C., operating in life sciences, diagnostics, and biotechnology tools through subsidiaries such as Beckman Coulter, Cepheid, and Leica Microsystems. The company designs, manufactures, and sells scientific instruments, reagents, and diagnostic systems used in laboratories and healthcare worldwide. Danaher has engaged with the USPTO on patent policy matters affecting its manufacturing and diagnostics businesses.
naics.justification: Danaher's largest reporting segments center on manufacturing life-science and laboratory analytical instruments, though as a diversified holding company its true 'primary activity' spans several manufacturing and diagnostics lines.

alternates.justification: A large share of Danaher's revenue comes from diagnostics subsidiaries like Cepheid and Beckman Coulter, which manufacture in-vitro diagnostic products.

naics.description: The Land Trust Alliance is a Washington, D.C.-based national membership organization supporting roughly 950 local and regional land trusts across the United States. Founded in 1982, it provides policy advocacy, education, training, and standards-setting for the land conservation community, with a goal of conserving millions of additional acres by 2030. The Alliance receives both member support and government funding from agencies such as NOAA, the Federal Highway Administration, and the EPA.
naics.justification: The Alliance's core mission is land conservation policy, education, and standards for its member land trusts, matching this environment/conservation-focused code.

alternates.justification: As a broad national membership nonprofit, it could alternatively be classified as a general civic/social organization.

Some of its technical-assistance and standards work for land trusts resembles environmental consulting.

naics.category_justification: The Alliance is explicitly membership-based, supporting and representing the collective interests of its ~950 member land trusts, though it also carries out charitable conservation education.
