naics.resolved_name: United States Patent and Trademark Office's Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patents
naics.description: The Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patents is a leadership office within the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's Patents business unit, responsible for establishing patent examination policy, revising the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure, and training patent examiners on legal and procedural issues. It operates under the Commissioner for Patents within the federal USPTO. It has commented on federal patent-related rulemakings.
naics.naics_title: Regulation, Licensing, and Inspection of Miscellaneous Commercial Sectors
naics.justification: As a sub-office managing patent examination policy and standards, its activity is best captured by this general federal regulatory-administration code, since no NAICS code specifically covers patent-office administration.

alternates.justification: Patent examination involves legal review of applications, which this code could also plausibly capture.
As a component of a federal executive-branch agency, this general code is also a plausible fit.
Not a strong fit; included only as a low-confidence alternate.

naics.category_justification: This is a sub-unit of the USPTO, a federal government agency, and shares its parent's governmental category.

naics.description: The Digital Medicine Society (DiMe) is a nonprofit professional society advancing the field of digital medicine, including the development and validation of digital clinical measures, biosensors, and software-based health tools. It convenes researchers, clinicians, regulators, and industry to develop best practices and educational resources. It has commented on a federal AI-related rulemaking.
naics.justification: DiMe functions as a professional membership society advancing standards and knowledge-sharing in the digital medicine field, matching this code's core activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: DiMe also produces substantive technical research and validation frameworks, which this code could capture instead.
A weaker fit reflecting any funding or resource-distribution activities DiMe may perform.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: A weak fit; DiMe's focus is technical/clinical rather than social-science research.

naics.category_justification: DiMe is structured as a mission-driven nonprofit professional society rather than a university, government body, or for-profit company.

naics.description: Kennesaw State University is a public research university in Kennesaw, Georgia, part of the University System of Georgia. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs across a wide range of disciplines, including business, engineering, and computing, and is one of the largest universities in Georgia by enrollment. It has commented on a federal AI-related rulemaking.
naics.justification: The institution is a degree-granting public university, the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: It is an accredited, degree-granting public university, unambiguously matching this category.

naics.description: Verily Life Sciences is a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. (Google's parent company) focused on precision health, developing tools that combine hardware, software, and data science to improve health research and care delivery, including chronic-disease management platforms and clinical research technologies. It has commented on an FDA rulemaking related to AI in health care.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
naics.justification: Verily's core activity is developing and researching health-technology tools and data platforms for precision medicine, which most closely matches biotechnology-oriented R&D.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: A very close alternate given Verily's broad engineering-plus-life-sciences research scope.
Reflects the substantial health-data software platforms Verily develops and licenses.
A weak fit reflecting Verily's clinical research and diagnostics-adjacent activities.

naics.category_justification: Verily is a for-profit subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. operating commercially in the health-technology sector.

naics.resolved_name: Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association's Asset Management Group (SIFMA AMG)
naics.description: SIFMA AMG (the Asset Management Group of the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association) is a division of SIFMA, the leading U.S. trade association for the securities industry, representing the interests of the buy-side asset-management community, including mutual funds, hedge funds, and institutional investors. It advocates on regulatory and market-structure issues affecting asset managers. It has commented on federal AI-related rulemakings affecting financial services.
naics.justification: As a division of SIFMA representing the collective regulatory and policy interests of asset-management firms, its core activity matches a business association's defining function.

alternates.justification: A close alternate given its focus on representing a specific professional/financial community.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A plausible catch-all for a specialized sub-group within a larger association.
A weak fit; SIFMA AMG advocates for asset managers but does not itself manage investments.

naics.category_justification: SIFMA AMG is a sub-group of a trade association representing the shared interests of asset-management firms, sharing its parent's category.

naics.description: Web research did not identify a specific, verifiable organization named 'Healthcare Trust Institute.' No credible dedicated website, registry entry, or news coverage under this exact name was found; it may be a generic or informally used name for a smaller or now-defunct entity that could not be confirmed.
naics.justification: Given no confirmed identity, this is a low-confidence guess based on the literal name suggesting a health-focused nonprofit or trust-like entity, not a verified classification.

alternates.naics_title: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers
alternates.justification: Plausible if 'trust' refers to a health-benefits trust fund, but unconfirmed.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: A keyword-matched candidate with no supporting evidence.
Plausible given the literal use of 'Trust' in the name, but unconfirmed.

naics.category_justification: No specific organization matching this name could be confirmed through web research, despite the health- and trust-related wording of the name.

naics.description: PAPA Missions is a nonprofit medical missions organization, founded in 2003 by Dr. H. Kyle Sheets, that provides practical support—including volunteer physicians and donated medical supplies—to medical mission trips in underserved regions around the world. Its typical focus is global medical humanitarian aid rather than technology policy, so its connection to the recorded AI-related comment could not be independently confirmed.
naics.justification: The identified organization's core activity is coordinating volunteer medical missions and supply donations, matching a voluntary health organization, though its link to an AI-policy comment is unconfirmed and could indicate a different or misattributed entity.

alternates.justification: A plausible alternate reflecting its broader humanitarian-aid activities beyond strictly medical services.
Plausible if its role is understood primarily as channeling donated medical supplies.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all given the uncertainty about which organization actually submitted the comment.

naics.category_justification: The best-identified match is a nonprofit medical-missions charity, but given the unusual context (a medical humanitarian nonprofit commenting on an AI RFI) this identification carries real uncertainty.

naics.description: The Wireless Infrastructure Association (WIA) is a trade association representing companies that build, own, and operate wireless communications infrastructure, including tower companies, distributed antenna system providers, and small-cell deployers. It advocates before federal, state, and local policymakers on siting, permitting, and broadband-deployment policy. It has commented on a federal AI-related rulemaking.
naics.justification: WIA's core activity is representing the collective policy interests of wireless-infrastructure companies before regulators, the defining activity of a business association.

alternates.justification: A plausible alternate given WIA's technical standards and best-practices work.

alternates.naics_title: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: A keyword-matched candidate; WIA represents infrastructure operators, not equipment manufacturers itself.
A weak fit; WIA is an association, not a carrier itself.

naics.category_justification: WIA is a membership-based trade association representing wireless-infrastructure companies' collective policy interests.

naics.description: An entity named 'Responsible AI Lab' is associated with a joint AI policy comment credited to UC San Diego Health and UCSF Health, but no organization by this exact name could be independently verified through web research. It may refer to an internal AI ethics or governance initiative within one of these health systems rather than a freestanding organization. Public sources describe UCSD Health's and UCSF Health's broader responsible-AI programs but do not name a distinct 'Responsible AI Lab' unit.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: If this is a health-system AI research/ethics unit, its primary activity would likely be applied research and governance work on AI methods, but the entity could not be confirmed, so the code is a low-confidence placeholder.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: An AI ethics/governance lab could alternatively be characterized as an internal advisory function within a health system.
If the lab is administratively part of a university-affiliated academic medical center, the parent institution's education code could apply instead.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: If the lab operates as an independent nonprofit initiative, this catch-all nonprofit code could apply.

naics.category_justification: Web research could not confirm whether 'Responsible AI Lab' is a distinct organization or a program inside UC San Diego Health/UCSF Health, so the category cannot be confidently assigned.

naics.description: Synteract is a full-service contract research organization (CRO) that supports biopharmaceutical and medical device companies through clinical drug development, conducting Phase I-IV studies worldwide. Headquartered in Carlsbad, California, it built its reputation serving emerging biopharma in areas such as oncology, rare diseases, neuroscience, and dermatology. Synteract was acquired by Syneos Health in 2020 and now operates as part of that larger clinical research and commercialization company.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
naics.justification: Synteract's primary activity is conducting contracted clinical trial research and development services on behalf of biopharmaceutical sponsors, matching R&D services in biotechnology/life sciences rather than manufacturing or general consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: CRO work spans devices and non-biotech therapeutics too, so this broader life-sciences R&D code is a close alternative.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: CROs perform a mix of scientific, regulatory, and project-management services that could fall into this catch-all code.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Some CRO offerings resemble project-management consulting, though this is a weaker fit than the R&D codes.

naics.category_justification: Synteract is a for-profit CRO operating as a subsidiary of Syneos Health, commenting in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: The University of Pennsylvania is a private Ivy League research university located in Philadelphia, founded in 1740. It offers undergraduate, graduate, and professional education across schools including Wharton, Penn Engineering, and the Perelman School of Medicine. Penn is one of the largest private research universities in the United States and is active in biomedical, engineering, and AI-related research.
naics.justification: Penn's defining activity is degree-granting higher education and academic research, which is precisely what this code covers.
naics.category_justification: The University of Pennsylvania is an unambiguous private research university.

naics.description: Sanofi is a French multinational pharmaceutical and healthcare company headquartered in Paris, with major U.S. operations. It researches, develops, manufactures, and markets prescription medicines and vaccines across areas such as immunology, oncology, rare diseases, and diabetes. Sanofi is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies and engages with U.S. regulators including the FDA on drug development and AI-related policy.
naics.justification: Sanofi's core activity is developing and manufacturing pharmaceutical preparations, which is the defining activity of this code, even though it also manufactures vaccines and biologics.

alternates.justification: Sanofi is also a major vaccine and biologics manufacturer, a significant adjacent business line.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)
alternates.justification: Sanofi conducts extensive drug-discovery R&D that this code could alternatively capture.

alternates.naics_title: Drugs and Druggists' Sundries Merchant Wholesalers
alternates.justification: Not a strong fit; included as a low-ranked alternative given Sanofi's distribution operations.

naics.category_justification: Sanofi is a large, publicly traded for-profit pharmaceutical company commenting in its own commercial interest.

display_name: The Nancy T. Tippins Group, LLC.

refs.raw_name: The Nancy T. Tippins Group, LLC.

naics.resolved_name: The Nancy T. Tippins Group, LLC.
naics.description: The Nancy T. Tippins Group, LLC is a boutique industrial-organizational psychology consulting firm led by Dr. Nancy T. Tippins, a longtime leader in the Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology (SIOP). The firm advises employers on workforce planning, employee selection and assessment, and the legal defensibility of testing programs, including issues raised by AI-based hiring tools. It is a small, employer-side consultancy rather than a research institution or advocacy group.
naics.justification: The firm's core service is advising employers on personnel selection, assessment validity, and HR testing programs, which is the defining activity of human resources consulting.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: As a small, specialized psychology consultancy, some of its work could fall into this general professional-services catch-all.
The firm's SIOP-related work touches on training and standards development, a secondary possibility.
Dr. Tippins' deep ties to SIOP suggest an association-like activity, though the firm itself is a private consultancy, not a membership body.

naics.category_justification: This is a for-profit consulting LLC commenting in its own capacity on employment-testing policy, not a membership association or nonprofit.

naics.description: Thematix Partners LLC is a New York-based consultancy founded in 2011 specializing in business architecture, ontology development, and semantic technologies. It helps organizations model business systems and digitally transform operations, and has contributed to industry standards efforts such as the National Retail Federation's ARTS specifications. It is a small, privately held professional-services firm.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: Thematix's core offering is advising organizations on business architecture and operating-model design, closest to general management consulting, though its semantic-technology/ontology focus also overlaps with technical consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Business architecture consulting with a technical bent could alternatively be classified as scientific/technical consulting.
Ontology and semantic-technology work has a significant software-engineering component that could place it here instead.
A specialized management-consulting niche like business architecture could fall into this residual consulting code.

naics.category_justification: Thematix is a small, privately held LLC consultancy commenting on AI/technology standards in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: The Northern Kentucky Water District is a public water utility that provides drinking-water treatment and distribution services to residents and businesses across several counties in northern Kentucky. It is a government-chartered special district rather than a private company, funded through customer rates and overseen by a public board. Its core function is water-supply infrastructure and treatment, not water-related manufacturing or transportation.
naics.justification: The district's primary activity is operating public water treatment and distribution infrastructure, the defining activity of this utilities code.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Air and Water Resource and Solid Waste Management Programs
alternates.justification: As a government-created special district, its oversight role could alternatively be coded as public administration rather than utility operation.

alternates.naics_title: Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction
alternates.justification: The district also builds and maintains pipeline infrastructure, though construction is secondary to ongoing utility operation.

alternates.naics_title: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities
alternates.justification: A weaker alternative reflecting its status as a government-created utility body.

naics.category_justification: It is a special-purpose public water district, a local government utility authority, not a private business.

naics.description: UL is a global safety science and certification organization, originally founded in 1894 as Underwriters Laboratories, that tests and certifies products for compliance with safety standards. Since 2022 the UL enterprise has been organized into UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement (nonprofit) alongside UL Solutions (the for-profit testing, inspection, and certification business, now publicly traded). At the time of this 2019 comment, UL operated as a unified private safety-certification company serving manufacturers across many industries.
naics.justification: UL's core activity is testing and certifying products against safety standards, matching the defining activity of testing-laboratory services.

alternates.justification: Because UL also develops safety standards, it has some overlap with standards-setting professional organizations.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: UL's broad advisory and standards work could alternatively be captured under this catch-all professional-services code.
Not a strong fit; included as a low-ranked alternative since UL's labs use specialized testing instrumentation.

naics.category_justification: At the time of its 2019 NIST comment, UL operated as a private testing/certification company; confidence is moderated because parts of the modern UL enterprise are nonprofit.

naics.description: BNP Paribas is a French multinational universal bank headquartered in Paris, offering retail banking, corporate and institutional banking, and investment services worldwide, including a significant U.S. presence. It is one of the largest banks in Europe by assets and engages with U.S. financial regulators on topics including AI use in banking. Its business spans commercial banking, investment banking, and asset management.
naics.justification: BNP Paribas's largest and most defining line of business is deposit-taking commercial and retail banking, even though it also runs substantial investment-banking and asset-management operations.

alternates.justification: BNP Paribas's corporate and institutional banking arm is a major investment-banking business that could be the primary classification instead.
BNP Paribas also operates substantial asset-management and investment-advisory businesses.

alternates.naics_title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities
alternates.justification: Not a strong fit; included as a low-ranked alternative given the bank's large-scale transaction-processing operations.

naics.category_justification: BNP Paribas is a large, publicly traded for-profit bank commenting in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: 'Analytics Center of Excellence' is a generic name commonly used by large companies for an internal data-analytics unit, and web research could not identify a specific standalone organization by this exact name tied to the FDA AI/ML drug-development docket. The associated comment (FDA-2023-N-0743-0063) appears among submissions from life-sciences and pharmaceutical companies, suggesting this is likely an internal analytics team at a pharmaceutical or health-data company rather than an independent entity. No parent organization could be confirmed with confidence.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: An internal analytics center of excellence at a life-sciences company would likely support data science and R&D activities, but without confirming the parent company the code is a low-confidence guess.

alternates.justification: If the unit is primarily a data-engineering/software team, this code could fit instead.
Corporate 'centers of excellence' are often internal consulting-style units advising business units, which this code could capture.
This was the keyword-matched shortlist candidate but is a poor substantive fit for a data-analytics team.

naics.category_justification: The name is a generic internal-unit label with no identifiable parent organization confirmed through research, so no category can be responsibly assigned.

naics.description: The University of Wisconsin-Madison is a large public research university in Madison, Wisconsin, and the flagship campus of the University of Wisconsin System. It offers extensive undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs and is a major recipient of federal research funding, including in computer science and AI. It is one of the nation's top public research universities.
naics.justification: UW-Madison's defining activity is degree-granting higher education and academic research, which is precisely what this code covers.
naics.category_justification: UW-Madison is an unambiguous public research university.

naics.description: The U.S. Department of Labor is a federal cabinet-level agency responsible for administering federal labor laws covering wages, workplace safety, unemployment insurance, and workers' rights, including emerging issues around AI use in hiring and workplace monitoring. It oversees agencies such as OSHA, the Wage and Hour Division, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and reports to the President.
naics.naics_title: Administration of Human Resource Programs (except Education, Public Health, and Veterans' Affairs Programs)
naics.justification: DOL's core mission is administering federal programs and regulations related to labor, employment, and workers' rights, which fits the human-resource-programs administration code most closely among the available public-administration codes.

alternates.justification: As a broad cabinet department with many sub-functions, a general government-support code is a plausible alternative.
Some DOL functions (e.g., labor statistics, economic data) touch on general economic program administration.

alternates.naics_title: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
alternates.justification: This was a keyword-matched candidate, but DOL is a federal regulator, not a membership labor union.

naics.category_justification: This is a U.S. federal cabinet department, unambiguously a federal government body.

naics.resolved_name: Networking and Information Technology Research and Development (NITRD) Program
naics.description: NITRD is the U.S. government's primary interagency program for coordinating federally funded research and development in networking, computing, and information technology, operating under the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. Its roughly 20 member agencies collectively invest billions of dollars annually in IT R&D, and NITRD coordinates AI-related research priorities across the federal government, including hosting the 2025 AI Action Plan RFI responses. It does not itself perform research but coordinates policy and planning across agencies.
naics.justification: NAICS 927110 is the standard federal public-administration code commonly used for government science and technology research-coordination bodies, the closest available match for NITRD's role coordinating federal IT R&D even though its focus is IT rather than space specifically.

alternates.justification: As an interagency coordinating body without its own R&D operations, this general government-support code is a reasonable alternative.
NITRD's coordination function has some overlap with broad federal program administration.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: If treated as performing R&D directly rather than only coordinating it, this code would apply instead.

naics.category_justification: NITRD is a federal interagency program operating under the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy.

naics.description: Lucent Technologies was an American telecommunications equipment manufacturer spun off from AT&T in 1996, known for its Bell Labs research arm and networking hardware. It merged with the French company Alcatel in 2006 to form Alcatel-Lucent, which was later acquired by Nokia in 2016, so Lucent no longer exists as an independent company today. The name likely appears here in connection with a legacy Bell Labs-affiliated researcher's AI RFI comment rather than an active corporate filer.
naics.justification: Lucent's core historical business was designing and manufacturing telecommunications and networking equipment, matching this manufacturing code, though the company has since been absorbed into Nokia.

alternates.naics_title: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Lucent also made a broad range of wireless and network infrastructure equipment covered by this adjacent code.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Lucent's Bell Labs division was primarily an R&D operation, which could be the more relevant activity for this comment's context.
This was the keyword-matched shortlist candidate but is not a substantive fit for a telecom equipment maker.

naics.category_justification: Lucent was historically a for-profit telecom equipment manufacturer; confidence is moderated because the company has since been dissolved into Nokia and this comment may reflect a legacy researcher affiliation rather than an active corporate filing.

naics.resolved_name: First Things (Institute on Religion and Public Life)
naics.description: First Things is a monthly magazine and journal of religion, culture, and public policy published by the Institute on Religion and Public Life, a nonprofit organization based in New York City. Founded by Richard John Neuhaus in 1990, it publishes essays from a religiously informed, largely conservative perspective on topics including technology, ethics, and public policy. It is a nonprofit-published periodical rather than a commercial magazine.
naics.justification: First Things' core activity is publishing a periodical magazine/journal, which is precisely the defining activity of this code.

alternates.justification: Its publisher, the Institute on Religion and Public Life, also engages in public-policy commentary that could be viewed as advocacy rather than pure publishing.
Given its religious editorial focus, a religious-organization code is a plausible secondary classification.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A residual nonprofit code is a weak but possible alternative.

naics.category_justification: First Things is published by the Institute on Religion and Public Life, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, rather than being a commercial media company.

naics.description: Koninklijke Philips N.V., commonly known as Philips, is a Dutch multinational conglomerate headquartered in Amsterdam that today focuses primarily on health technology, including diagnostic imaging, patient monitoring, and connected-care devices. Historically Philips also manufactured consumer electronics and lighting, but it divested those businesses to concentrate on health technology. Philips engages with U.S. patent and technology policy bodies as a major medical-device manufacturer.
naics.justification: Philips' current core business is designing and manufacturing medical imaging and patient-monitoring devices, matching this electromedical-equipment manufacturing code.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Philips conducts substantial R&D that could alternatively be the primary classified activity.

alternates.naics_title: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Philips retains some connected/wireless health-device technology that overlaps with this code.

alternates.naics_title: Electric Lamp Bulb and Other Lighting Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Reflects Philips' historic lighting business, since divested, included as a lower-ranked legacy alternative.

naics.category_justification: Philips is a publicly traded, for-profit multinational corporation commenting on patent/AI policy in its own commercial interest.

naics.description: The Spectator is a weekly British magazine of politics, culture, and current affairs, first published in 1828, making it one of the oldest continuously published magazines in the world. It is a privately owned, for-profit publication, historically associated with the Telegraph Media Group family and more recently owned by Sir Paul Marshall's Old Queen Street Ventures. The magazine publishes commentary and opinion, including occasional pieces touching on technology and AI policy.
naics.justification: The Spectator's core activity is publishing a weekly print and digital magazine, which is the defining activity of this periodical-publishing code.

alternates.justification: The Spectator functions much like an opinion/news publication, close to a newspaper in format and content.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: The magazine's substantial digital/online publishing operation could alternatively fall under general information services.
Not a strong fit; included as a low-ranked alternative given the outlet's political commentary focus.

naics.category_justification: The Spectator is a privately owned, for-profit magazine publisher, not a nonprofit or advocacy organization.

naics.resolved_name: Lockheed Martin AI Center (Lockheed Martin Corporation)
naics.description: The Lockheed Martin AI Center is an internal artificial intelligence hub within Lockheed Martin Corporation, a major U.S. aerospace, defense, and security company. The center develops and applies AI and machine learning technologies to national-security and defense systems, and Lockheed Martin submitted formal comments under this name to the 2025 federal AI Action Plan RFI. As a unit of Lockheed Martin, it shares the parent company's aerospace/defense manufacturing focus.
naics.justification: Lockheed Martin's overall primary business and official NAICS classification is aircraft manufacturing, and the AI Center is treated here as sharing its parent company's primary industry per standard sub-unit classification practice.

alternates.naics_title: Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Lockheed Martin's Space and Missiles segment is a major business line that this code equally captures.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The AI Center itself performs applied software and AI R&D rather than manufacturing directly, which could argue for an R&D services code.
A weak fit since Lockheed Martin is a private contractor rather than a government body, but included given its national-security-focused work.

naics.category_justification: Lockheed Martin AI Center is an internal unit of Lockheed Martin Corporation, a publicly traded for-profit defense contractor.

naics.description: Chattanooga State Community College is a public two-year community college in Chattanooga, Tennessee, part of the Tennessee Board of Regents system. It offers associate degrees and workforce/technical certificate programs, and a faculty or staff member submitted AI policy comments referencing the institution as part of Tennessee's broader engagement with federal AI initiatives. It is a public junior/community college rather than a four-year university.
naics.justification: As a two-year community college awarding associate degrees, its core educational activity is precisely captured by the Junior Colleges code rather than the four-year Colleges/Universities code.

alternates.justification: Some data sources classify community colleges under the broader higher-education code instead of the specific junior-college code.
Ancillary educational-support functions could be a minor secondary activity, though not the primary one.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Urban Planning and Community and Rural Development
alternates.justification: This was a keyword-matched candidate but is not a substantive fit for a community college.

naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting community college, matching the university/higher-education category as defined.

naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: If iForAI is a nonprofit advocacy or membership initiative, this catch-all nonprofit code would apply instead.
If iForAI is a professional/industry association for AI practitioners, this code would fit.

naics.description: Applied Intuition is a Mountain View, California-based software company that provides simulation, testing, and validation tools for autonomous vehicles and other AI-driven robotics systems. Founded in 2017, it is a well-funded private technology company serving automotive OEMs, defense, and other autonomy-focused customers. It has submitted comments on federal AI policy given its role building safety-critical AI/autonomy software.

naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is representing and advocating for its member news and magazine publishers on policy matters, which is the defining activity of a business association.

alternates.justification: It could be seen as a professional membership body for the journalism/publishing industry, though it functions more as an industry trade group than a professional credentialing body.

alternates.naics_title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks and Content Providers
alternates.justification: Considered because the members it represents are media content providers, but the Alliance itself does not produce or distribute content.
Ruled out because the Alliance does not buy media placements on behalf of clients.

naics.category_justification: It is a membership-based association representing the collective interests of news and magazine publishers.

naics.description: Deutsche Bank AG is a German multinational investment bank and financial services company headquartered in Frankfurt, Germany, with major operations in the United States. It provides commercial and investment banking, asset management, and wealth management services to corporate, institutional, and private clients worldwide. It is one of the largest banks in Europe and a significant player in global capital markets.
naics.justification: Deutsche Bank's primary activity is commercial and retail banking services, though it also has a substantial investment banking arm.

alternates.justification: Deutsche Bank has a very large investment banking and securities trading division, which could be considered its primary revenue driver in some years.
Ruled out; Deutsche Bank is a for-profit bank, not a member-owned credit union.
Ruled out; asset management is only one part of its diversified banking business.

naics.category_justification: Deutsche Bank is a for-profit, publicly traded commercial and investment bank commenting on its own behalf.

naics.description: AT&T Inc. is a major American multinational telecommunications company headquartered in Dallas, Texas. It provides wireless and wired voice, data, and broadband internet services to consumers and businesses across the United States. It is one of the largest telecommunications carriers in the world and regularly comments on federal technology and intellectual property policy.
naics.justification: AT&T's largest and primary revenue segment is wireless mobile telecommunications service, though it also operates substantial wired network infrastructure.

alternates.justification: AT&T also operates extensive wired broadband and legacy telephone networks, making this a close second choice.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; data services are a minor part of AT&T's business compared to telecommunications carriage.
Ruled out; AT&T divested its media/entertainment holdings and is not primarily a broadcaster.

naics.category_justification: AT&T is a publicly traded, for-profit telecommunications corporation commenting in its own capacity.

naics.description: Digital Content Next (DCN) is a nonprofit trade association representing high-quality digital content and media companies that maintain direct relationships with consumers and advertisers. It conducts research, hosts events, and engages with policymakers on issues such as digital advertising, privacy, antitrust, and AI's impact on content and journalism. It is based in New York City and was formerly known as the Online Publishers Association.
naics.justification: DCN's core activity is representing and advocating for its member digital media and publishing companies, the defining activity of a business/trade association.

alternates.naics_title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks and Content Providers
alternates.justification: Its candidate shortlist suggested this because DCN's members are content and media providers, but DCN itself does not directly distribute media content.
Considered because it serves an industry professional community, though it functions as a trade association rather than a credentialing professional body.

alternates.naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
alternates.justification: Ruled out; research is a member service, not DCN's primary activity.

naics.category_justification: DCN is explicitly described as a trade association representing digital media company members' collective interests.

normalized_name: division of science technology and innovation
display_name: Division of Science, Technology and Innovation

refs.raw_name: Division of Science, Technology and Innovation

naics.resolved_name: Division of Science, Technology and Innovation (state economic development agency)
naics.description: The Division of Science, Technology and Innovation is a name used by multiple U.S. state government offices (such as New York's Empire State Development NYSTAR division and North Carolina's Office of Science, Technology & Innovation) that administer programs supporting research, technology commercialization, and economic development. The specific state agency behind this comment could not be confirmed from available information. These divisions typically fund and coordinate science and technology initiatives to spur state economic growth.
naics.justification: State science and technology divisions primarily administer economic development and innovation-support programs, which matches this public administration code, though the exact state agency is unconfirmed.

alternates.justification: Some such divisions are housed within education or research agencies, but the name suggests an economic-development rather than education focus.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Considered if the division itself conducts R&D rather than administering programs, but government divisions with this name are typically administrative, not research-performing.
Ruled out; no evidence ties this division specifically to space research.

naics.category_justification: The name and structure match a state-level government agency division, though the specific state could not be confirmed.

normalized_name: us department of education office of educational technology
display_name: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION OFFICE OF EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGY

refs.raw_name: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION OFFICE OF EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGY

naics.resolved_name: U.S. Department of Education Office of Educational Technology
naics.description: The Office of Educational Technology is a federal office within the U.S. Department of Education that develops national policy and provides leadership on the use of technology, including AI, in K-12 and higher education. It produces guidance documents, such as reports on AI in teaching and learning, and supports states and districts in effective technology adoption. It operates under the federal Department of Education.
naics.justification: The office's primary activity is administering federal education technology policy and programs, directly matching this public administration code for education program administration.
naics.category_justification: This is a federal executive branch office within the U.S. Department of Education.

naics.resolved_name: U.S. General Services Administration, Federal Acquisition Service
naics.description: The Federal Acquisition Service (FAS) is a division of the U.S. General Services Administration that provides federal agencies with contracting vehicles, procurement of products and services, and technology solutions. It manages government-wide acquisition programs including IT, telecommunications, and professional services contracts. It is a component of the federal government's central procurement agency.
naics.justification: FAS's primary activity is administering federal procurement and acquisition programs on behalf of the government, which is best captured by this general economic/administrative program code as there is no NAICS code specific to procurement administration.

alternates.justification: Considered because FAS provides acquisition and administrative support services, but this private-sector code doesn't fit a government agency.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Human Resource Programs (except Education, Public Health, and Veterans' Affairs Programs)
alternates.justification: Considered because FAS administers a broad range of government-wide support programs, though its focus is procurement, not human resource programs specifically.

alternates.naics_title: Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities
alternates.justification: Ruled out; FAS's function is procurement, not justice or public order.

naics.category_justification: FAS is a component agency of the U.S. General Services Administration, a federal government body.

naics.description: The Contra Costa Water District is a public agency that provides drinking water treatment and delivery services to residents and businesses in Contra Costa County, California. It manages water supply infrastructure, including the Los Vaqueros Reservoir, and is governed by an elected board of directors. It operates as a special district under California state law.
naics.justification: The district's primary activity is the supply, treatment, and distribution of drinking water, which is the defining activity of this utilities code.

alternates.naics_title: Administration of Air and Water Resource and Solid Waste Management Programs
alternates.justification: As a public agency, its regulatory/administrative functions could also fit government program administration, though it directly operates the utility rather than merely regulating it.

alternates.naics_title: Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction
alternates.justification: Ruled out; construction is not the district's ongoing primary activity, only incidental to infrastructure maintenance.
Ruled out; unrelated to the district's water supply mission.

naics.category_justification: It is a special-purpose local government water district operating under California state law.

naics.description: GE Software Research refers to the software and analytics research arm of General Electric's corporate research organization, GE Global Research. It develops software, industrial AI, and data analytics technologies to support GE's industrial businesses such as aviation, power, and healthcare. It operates as part of General Electric, a diversified American multinational conglomerate.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: The unit's primary activity is conducting corporate research and development in software and engineering technology for GE's industrial businesses.

alternates.justification: If the unit primarily develops and licenses proprietary software products rather than performing R&D services, this code would apply instead.
Considered because the group writes custom software, but its stated mission is research rather than programming services for clients.

alternates.naics_title: Aircraft Engine and Engine Parts Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Ruled out; while GE's parent business includes aviation manufacturing, this specific research unit's activity is software, not manufacturing.

naics.category_justification: It is a corporate research division of General Electric, a for-profit industrial conglomerate.

naics.description: Symantec Corporation was an American cybersecurity software company known for products such as Norton antivirus and enterprise security solutions. Its enterprise security business was acquired by Broadcom in 2019, while its consumer business became NortonLifeLock (now Gen Digital). Historically, Symantec developed and sold software for endpoint protection, data security, and threat intelligence.
naics.justification: Symantec's primary activity was developing and licensing packaged cybersecurity and antivirus software, matching this code for software publishing.

alternates.justification: Considered given Symantec's security industry focus, but this code applies to physical/electronic security systems services, not software.
Considered because Symantec also provided enterprise implementation services, but its core business was packaged software licensing.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; Symantec was primarily a software vendor, not a hosting or data-processing infrastructure provider.

naics.category_justification: Symantec was a for-profit, publicly traded software corporation commenting in its own business capacity.

naics.description: SLB, formerly known as Schlumberger, is a multinational technology and oilfield services company that provides equipment, software, and services for the energy industry, including seismic surveying, drilling, well completion, and reservoir management. Headquartered with principal offices in Houston, Paris, London, and The Hague, it is one of the largest oilfield services companies in the world. The company rebranded from Schlumberger to SLB in 2022 to reflect a broader focus on energy technology.
naics.naics_title: Support Activities for Oil and Gas Operations
naics.justification: SLB's primary business is providing technical services and equipment support to oil and gas well operators, matching this support-activities code rather than direct extraction.

alternates.justification: SLB performs some drilling services directly, making this a plausible secondary code.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Considered because SLB also provides consulting and software services, but this is secondary to its core oilfield services work.

alternates.naics_title: Oil and Gas Field Machinery and Equipment Manufacturing
alternates.justification: SLB also manufactures oilfield equipment, though this is not its primary revenue source.

naics.category_justification: SLB is a for-profit, publicly traded multinational energy technology and services corporation.

naics.resolved_name: Ratio Christi and Colson Fellows (joint submission)
naics.description: Ratio Christi is a Christian apologetics organization that supports university student and faculty chapters in defending the historical, philosophical, and scientific basis of Christian faith. The Colson Fellows Program, run by the Colson Center, is a ten-month Christian worldview training program for adult professionals. Both are faith-based educational and advocacy organizations that jointly submitted a public comment on AI policy reflecting Christian worldview perspectives.
naics.justification: Both organizations are faith-based ministries whose primary activity is religious education, apologetics training, and worldview formation, matching the religious organizations code.

alternates.justification: Considered because both groups provide structured training and fellowship programs, which resembles educational support services, though their mission is explicitly religious rather than secular education.
Considered given their engagement in public policy commentary, though advocacy is secondary to their core religious/educational mission.
Ruled out; their activities are more specifically religious/educational than general civic/social in nature.

naics.category_justification: Both are mission-driven, faith-based nonprofit organizations engaged in religious education rather than a membership trade body or government entity.

naics.description: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) is a federal research and development laboratory located in Livermore, California, managed for the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Security, LLC. It conducts research in national security, nuclear weapons stewardship, high-performance computing, and advanced science including AI applications. LLNL is one of the U.S. Department of Energy's national laboratories.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: LLNL's primary activity is conducting scientific and engineering research and development under contract for the Department of Energy, matching this R&D code.

alternates.justification: LLNL's work has a strong national security and nuclear weapons mission, making this a plausible alternate given its DOE/NNSA affiliation.
Considered because it is a federally funded research facility similar to those under this code's public administration analog, though LLNL's focus is broader than space research.
Ruled out; testing services are a minor part compared to LLNL's broad research mission.

naics.category_justification: LLNL is operated by a nonprofit-affiliated management contractor (Lawrence Livermore National Security, LLC) under a DOE contract, functioning as a federally funded research and development center rather than a direct government agency.

naics.resolved_name: Stanford University's Institute for Human-Centered AI and Digital Economy Lab
naics.description: The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) is a research institute at Stanford University focused on studying and advancing AI's impact on humanity, spanning research, education, and policy. The Stanford Digital Economy Lab is a research lab within HAI that studies AI's economic impacts. Both are academic research units of Stanford University.
naics.justification: Both entities are research institutes housed within Stanford University, whose primary activity is higher education and university-affiliated research.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Considered because these institutes primarily perform research rather than teaching, which could be seen as standalone R&D activity, though they remain organizationally part of the university.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Considered given HAI's technical AI research focus, but its work spans social science and policy as much as technical research.
Ruled out; these are research institutes, not grantmaking bodies.

naics.category_justification: Both are research units of Stanford University, a private research university, sharing the university's category.

naics.description: "School of Information" is a common name for graduate schools of information science at several U.S. universities (such as UC Berkeley, University of Michigan, and University of Texas). Web research could not confirm which specific university's School of Information submitted this comment, given the ambiguous associated record identifiers. These schools generally offer graduate education and conduct research in information science, data, and technology policy.
naics.justification: The name plainly denotes an academic school of information within a university, matching this code, though the specific parent institution could not be verified.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Considered due to keyword overlap with 'information,' but this code does not fit an academic school.

naics.description: The Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) is the national trade association for the U.S. solar and solar-plus-storage industry. It represents solar manufacturers, installers, and developers, advocating for policies that support solar energy growth and publishing industry research and market data. SEIA is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
naics.justification: SEIA's primary activity is representing and advocating for the collective interests of solar energy companies, the defining activity of a business/trade association.

alternates.justification: Considered because it serves a professional/technical industry community, but it functions as a broad industry trade group rather than a credentialing professional body.
Ruled out; SEIA is an association representing generators and installers, not itself a power generation operator.

alternates.naics_title: Marketing Research and Public Opinion Polling
alternates.justification: Ruled out; market research is a member service SEIA provides, not its core defining activity.

naics.category_justification: SEIA is explicitly a national trade association representing the solar industry's member companies.

naics.description: Coworker.org is a nonprofit organization, fiscally sponsored by the New Venture Fund, that provides workers with online tools, training, and campaign support to organize with coworkers and advocate for workplace changes. It supports worker-led campaigns on issues such as scheduling, wages, and workplace policies, notably including efforts at large retail and service employers. It positions itself as a modern alternative and complement to traditional union organizing.
naics.justification: Coworker.org's primary activity is advocacy and organizing support for workers' rights, matching this social advocacy organization code rather than a labor union with formal collective bargaining authority.

alternates.naics_title: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
alternates.justification: It functions similarly to a labor organizing body, though it is not itself a certified labor union engaged in collective bargaining.
Considered as a general civic organization category, but its specific worker-advocacy focus is better captured by the social advocacy code.
Ruled out; it does not provide consulting services to employers.

naics.category_justification: It is a mission-driven 501(c)(3)-sponsored nonprofit providing worker organizing tools and support rather than functioning as a formal union or trade group.

naics.description: Benedictine College is a private, Catholic, Benedictine liberal arts college located in Atchison, Kansas. It offers undergraduate and graduate degree programs across a range of disciplines and is affiliated with the Catholic Benedictine monastic tradition. The college was formed through the merger of St. Benedict's College and Mount St. Scholastica College.
naics.justification: Benedictine College is a four-year degree-granting college, directly matching this code for colleges and universities.
naics.category_justification: It is an accredited, degree-granting four-year college.

naics.description: Snorkel AI is a venture-backed technology company that develops software for programmatic data labeling and AI model development, originating from research at Stanford University. Its platform helps enterprises build and fine-tune machine learning and AI models more efficiently by reducing the need for manual data annotation. The company is headquartered in Redwood City, California.
naics.justification: Snorkel AI's primary activity is developing and licensing proprietary AI data-labeling and model-development software, matching this software publishing code.

alternates.justification: Considered because it also provides implementation services, but its core business model is a licensed software platform, not custom programming.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services

naics.category_justification: Snorkel AI is a for-profit, venture-backed technology company commenting in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: The Minnesota Catholic Conference is the public policy voice of the Catholic bishops of Minnesota, representing the state's Catholic dioceses on legislative and regulatory matters. It advocates on issues including life, family, education, and social justice consistent with Catholic teaching. It is based in St. Paul, Minnesota.
naics.justification: The Conference's primary activity is representing the Catholic Church's official positions and advocacy on public policy, matching the religious organizations code.

alternates.justification: Considered given its policy advocacy focus, though its identity and mission are explicitly religious rather than secular advocacy.
Considered because it engages heavily in legislative advocacy, but it operates as a religious body rather than a partisan political organization.
Ruled out; it does not represent business interests.

naics.category_justification: It functions as the collective public policy advocacy arm representing the state's Catholic dioceses, similar to a membership-based advocacy coalition, though it is also fundamentally a religious body.

naics.description: IBM Research is the corporate research division of International Business Machines Corporation, conducting fundamental and applied research across computing, AI, and technology domains. The Security group within IBM Research focuses on cybersecurity, cryptography, and AI security research. It operates as part of IBM, a multinational information technology company.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: The unit's primary activity is conducting corporate scientific and technical research and development in security and computing for IBM, matching this R&D code.

alternates.justification: Considered because IBM's broader business includes publishing security software products derived from this research.
Considered given IBM's large systems integration and consulting business, though this specific unit is research-focused.
Ruled out; this code applies to physical security systems installation, not cybersecurity research.

naics.category_justification: It is a research division of IBM, a for-profit multinational technology corporation.

naics.description: The American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonprofit behavioral and social science research organization headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. It conducts research and provides technical assistance in areas such as education, health, workforce development, and international development, often under contracts with government agencies and foundations. AIR is one of the largest nonprofit social science research organizations in the United States.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: AIR's primary activity is conducting behavioral and social science research and evaluation, directly matching this code.

alternates.justification: Considered because AIR provides significant technical assistance and evaluation services to education agencies, though its work spans well beyond education into health and workforce research.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Ruled out; AIR's research is predominantly behavioral and social science rather than physical or engineering science.
Ruled out; AIR is a nonprofit contractor performing research, not a government agency administering programs.

naics.category_justification: AIR is a nonprofit research organization conducting mission-driven social science research and technical assistance.

naics.description: H2O.ai is a venture-backed technology company that develops open-source and enterprise software platforms for machine learning and generative AI, including its H2O and H2O LLM Studio products. The company is headquartered in Mountain View, California, and serves enterprise customers building and deploying AI models. It has been an active commenter on federal AI policy.
naics.justification: H2O.ai's primary activity is developing and licensing machine learning and AI software platforms, matching this software publishing code.

alternates.justification: Considered given its enterprise services and support offerings, though its core products are licensed software platforms.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Considered due to its heavy investment in AI research, though it commercializes this research as software products.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Ruled out; H2O.ai is primarily a software vendor rather than an infrastructure/hosting provider.

naics.category_justification: H2O.ai is a for-profit, venture-backed AI software company commenting in its own commercial capacity.

naics.description: Exponential Blueprint Consulting LLC is a small consulting firm founded by Doug Hohulin, a former Motorola and Nokia executive, focused on advising organizations on emerging and exponential technologies including AI, in areas such as healthcare, autonomous vehicles, education, and energy policy. The firm's founder has co-authored books on future technology trends. It appears to operate as a small independent management consultancy.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: The firm's primary activity is providing general strategic and management consulting on technology trends and policy to organizations across industries.

alternates.justification: Considered as a close alternative since the firm's advisory work spans multiple specialized topics rather than fitting neatly into administrative/general management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Considered given the firm's technology and scientific-trend focus, which could fall under technical consulting rather than general management consulting.
Considered because the founder is also an author, but this is secondary to the firm's consulting activity.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit, independently owned consulting LLC commenting on its own behalf, though it may act in an advisory capacity representing views on behalf of unnamed clients on some topics.

naics.description: Daedalus Futures is a consulting firm focused on strategy and advisory services for transformational and responsible AI, helping organizations navigate AI regulatory and governance complexity. Limited independent information is available about the firm's size, ownership, or client base beyond its own website. It appears to operate as a boutique AI policy and strategy consultancy.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: The firm's stated primary activity is providing strategic and policy advisory consulting services related to AI governance, matching general management consulting.

alternates.justification: A close alternative given the specialized nature of AI governance consulting, which may not fit neatly into general management consulting.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Considered given the technical/AI-specific nature of its consulting work.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Ruled out; the firm markets itself as a consultancy, not a research institution.

naics.category_justification: It presents itself as a for-profit consulting firm, though details on its size and structure are limited, and it may advise clients rather than act on its own behalf on some matters.

naics.description: Monash University is a public research university headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, with additional campuses internationally. It offers a broad range of undergraduate and graduate degree programs and conducts extensive research across disciplines including AI and data science. It is one of Australia's largest and most research-intensive universities.
naics.justification: Monash University's primary activity is degree-granting higher education and university research, directly matching this code.
naics.category_justification: Monash University is an accredited, degree-granting public research university.

naics.description: People For the American Way is a progressive nonprofit advocacy organization based in Washington, D.C., that works to promote democratic values, civil rights, and civil liberties, and to counter what it views as threats from the political and religious right. It engages in public education, grassroots organizing, and policy advocacy on issues including voting rights, judicial nominations, and technology policy. It was founded in 1981 by television producer Norman Lear.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is public policy advocacy and civic education on democracy and civil rights issues, matching this social advocacy code.

alternates.justification: Considered given its civil rights focus, though its mission is broader civic/democracy advocacy rather than exclusively human rights work.
Considered given its engagement in political and legislative issues, but it is a nonpartisan 501(c)(3)/(c)(4) advocacy nonprofit rather than a partisan political organization.
Ruled out; its focused policy advocacy mission is more specific than general civic/social activity.

naics.category_justification: It is a mission-driven nonprofit advocacy organization rather than a membership trade body, government entity, or university.

naics.resolved_name: Office of the West Virginia Attorney General

The Attorney General is an elected constitutional officer of the state. The office regularly participates in multistate policy comments, including on technology and AI issues.
naics.naics_title: Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities
naics.justification: The Attorney General's office's primary activity is legal enforcement and public order functions on behalf of the state government, matching this public administration code.

alternates.justification: Ruled out; not applicable, this is a state government office, not a tribal government.

naics.description: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) is a Japanese multinational financial holding company headquartered in Tokyo, formed in 2005 through the merger of Mitsubishi Tokyo Financial Group and UFJ Holdings. It provides commercial banking, trust banking, securities, credit card, and asset management services through subsidiaries including MUFG Bank and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities. MUFG is one of the largest financial groups in the world, with major operations in the United States.
naics.justification: MUFG's core business, through its principal subsidiary MUFG Bank, is commercial banking, though the parent group also spans trust, securities, and asset management activities.

alternates.justification: MUFG's large securities subsidiary, Mitsubishi UFJ Securities, provides substantial investment banking services, making this a close alternate.
As a financial holding company parent, this code could apply to the top-level corporate entity rather than its operating banking subsidiaries.
Ruled out; asset management is a smaller part of the diversified group's overall business.

naics.category_justification: MUFG is a for-profit, publicly traded multinational financial holding company.

naics.description: AI ALT Lab is an organization that describes itself as working to provide independent assessment and verification of AI tools, and to build participatory forms of AI literacy and citizenship by connecting affected communities with AI developers. It offers training, resources, and frameworks to help translate ethical AI principles into practice. Limited independent verification of its organizational structure or funding was available beyond its own website.
naics.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
naics.justification: The organization's described activity is providing independent technical assessment, training, and advisory services related to AI ethics and trustworthiness, which loosely fits scientific and technical consulting.

alternates.justification: Its stated mission of building AI literacy and connecting affected communities with developers has a strong advocacy and public-education character, making this a strong alternate.
Considered given its emphasis on training and education resources on AI, which fits educational support activities.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Ruled out as lower likelihood; the organization emphasizes assessment and education over conducting original technical research.

naics.category_justification: While the organization has a public website describing its mission, independent verification of its legal structure (nonprofit, business, or other) could not be confirmed.

naics.resolved_name: Carnegie Mellon University School of Computer Science
naics.description: The School of Computer Science is an academic college within Carnegie Mellon University, widely regarded as one of the top computer science schools in the world. It offers undergraduate and graduate degree programs and conducts extensive research in computer science, robotics, machine learning, and human-computer interaction. It is a major hub for AI-related research within Carnegie Mellon University.
