It works with state and federal policymakers to promote grid modernization to relieve transmission congestion, partly in response to rising electricity demand from AI data centers. Its members include grid technology vendors such as Smart Wires, LineVision, and Ampacimon.
naics.justification: The coalition's primary activity is representing member grid-technology companies and advocating collectively for policy favorable to their shared industry interests, matching a business association.

alternates.justification: Its work is largely policy advocacy, which overlaps with general social/policy advocacy organizations.
Could be seen as a professional grouping, though its members are companies rather than individual professionals.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all if it does not fit cleanly as a business association.

naics.category_justification: It is a coalition of companies representing their shared commercial interest in grid-enhancing technology policy.

naics.description: New Saint Andrews College is a small private classical Christian college located in Moscow, Idaho, founded in 1994. It offers an integrated liberal arts curriculum grounded in classical and Christian texts, awarding associate's, bachelor's, and master's degrees rather than conventional undergraduate majors. The college is accredited by the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities.
naics.justification: The organization is a degree-granting college offering bachelor's and master's degrees, which is the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: It is an accredited degree-granting college.

naics.description: The Association of American Universities (AAU) is a membership organization of leading public and private research universities in the United States and Canada. It advocates for federal policies supporting research funding, higher education, and innovation on behalf of its member institutions. AAU produces policy analysis and public statements on issues affecting research universities.
naics.justification: AAU's primary activity is representing the collective interests of member research universities in federal policy, matching a membership association of institutions.

alternates.justification: Could be viewed as a professional/institutional association rather than a strict business association.
AAU itself does not grant degrees, so this fits its members rather than AAU.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: Generic catch-all if not classified as a business association.

naics.category_justification: AAU is a membership body representing the collective interests of research universities.

naics.description: Luminary Strategies, LLC is a boutique advisory firm founded by Arushi Sharma Frank that sits at the intersection of AI, energy markets, and capital deployment. It advises hedge funds, private equity sponsors, and portfolio-company executives on power infrastructure and AI-era energy investment strategy. The firm has also submitted public comments on federal energy and AI policy, including on grid capacity for AI data centers.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: The firm's primary activity is strategic advisory consulting for clients on energy and AI capital decisions, which is best captured by general management consulting.

alternates.justification: Its specialized energy/AI strategy advisory work could also fall under this closely related consulting code.
Some of its work advising investors on capital deployment resembles investment advisory services.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all given the firm's cross-disciplinary advisory nature.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit consulting/advisory firm commenting in its own business capacity.

naics.description: The Computing Research Association (CRA) is a nonprofit professional association representing academic departments, industrial laboratories, and professional societies in computing research across North America. It advocates for federal funding of computing research and produces reports on workforce and research trends in computer science. CRA membership spans universities, government labs, and industry research organizations.
naics.justification: CRA's core activity is representing and coordinating the professional/research interests of computing researchers and their institutions, matching a professional organization.

alternates.justification: Its membership includes industry labs, giving it some business-association character.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: CRA produces some research reports itself, though this is not its primary activity.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: Generic catch-all if not classified as a professional organization.

naics.category_justification: CRA is a membership association representing the collective interests of computing research institutions and researchers.

naics.description: Saint Luke's Anglican Church is the name shared by multiple independent Anglican parishes across the United States that follow traditional Anglican worship using the Book of Common Prayer. Web research could not confirm which specific parish submitted the comment, as several congregations share this name. Each such parish is a local house of worship serving its congregation.
naics.justification: The name clearly identifies a church congregation, whose primary activity is religious worship and ministry, though the specific parish could not be confirmed.

alternates.justification: Unlikely, but possible if the comment reflects an advocacy-focused ministry rather than a congregation.
A distant alternative if the entity functions more as a community/social group than a place of worship.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: Generic catch-all given inability to confirm the specific parish.

naics.category_justification: It is a religious congregation, a mission-driven organization rather than a membership trade body, government, or university.

naics.description: The County of Los Angeles is the local government of Los Angeles County, California, the most populous county in the United States. It provides a broad range of public services including public health, social services, law enforcement, and infrastructure to residents across its incorporated and unincorporated areas. The county government is led by an elected Board of Supervisors.
naics.justification: As a general-purpose county government providing a broad mix of public services rather than one single administrative function, it best fits the catch-all general government support code.

alternates.justification: The Board of Supervisors functions as the county's executive body.
The Board of Supervisors combines executive and legislative functions for the county.
The county also operates legal/prosecutorial offices, though this is only one of many functions.

naics.category_justification: It is a county-level (local) government body.

naics.description: Pearson Plc is a British multinational company providing educational content, assessments, qualifications, and digital learning services worldwide. Its business spans higher education and workforce skills training, English-language learning, and testing/assessment services, alongside a legacy publishing business in textbooks and educational materials. Pearson is a for-profit, publicly traded company headquartered in London.
naics.justification: Pearson's modern primary activity is providing assessments, digital learning platforms, and educational support services rather than solely publishing physical books.

alternates.justification: Pearson has a long legacy as a textbook and educational book publisher.
A significant part of its business is testing and qualification services.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: Its digital learning platforms could be seen as an information service.

naics.category_justification: Pearson is a for-profit, publicly traded company commenting on policy affecting its own business.

naics.description: Prudential Financial, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American financial services company providing life insurance, annuities, retirement plan administration, and asset management. It is one of the largest life insurance providers in the United States. The company is publicly traded and headquartered in Newark, New Jersey.
naics.justification: Prudential's core, historic business is underwriting life insurance policies, matching this code, though it also has substantial asset management and annuity operations.

alternates.justification: Prudential also engages in reinsurance activity, though it is not its primary line.
Prudential also distributes financial products, though it primarily underwrites rather than brokers.
Its asset management and retirement businesses could partially fit this code.

naics.category_justification: Prudential is a for-profit, publicly traded financial services corporation.

naics.description: Simon Fraser University is a public research university based in British Columbia, Canada, offering undergraduate and graduate degrees across many disciplines. alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Metagov's research-collective activity fits a social science R&D code.
Metagov could be viewed as a research network/professional collective rather than a university.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)

naics.category_justification: Simon Fraser University, a degree-granting institution, is the primary named entity, though the joint filing with a non-university research collective lowers certainty.

naics.description: ProductBio is a small San Francisco-based company that has built a large ESG (environmental, social, governance) database and uses AI-enabled data science to support supply-chain sustainability decisions for purchasing, manufacturing, and merchandising. It provides software and data services helping organizations align purchasing decisions with sustainability targets. Web research found limited additional detail on the company beyond this description.
naics.justification: ProductBio's primary offering is a proprietary software/data platform for sustainability decision-making, best captured by software publishing, though its data-service character introduces ambiguity.

alternates.justification: It may primarily deliver custom software/data solutions to clients rather than a packaged software product.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Its ESG database and data science services resemble a data processing service.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: A generic catch-all if its business is more advisory/consulting than software-based.

naics.category_justification: ProductBio is described as a for-profit company selling data and software services.

naics.description: The University of South Florida is a public research university based in Tampa, Florida, with additional campuses in St. Petersburg and Sarasota-Manatee. It offers undergraduate, graduate, and professional degree programs and conducts extensive federally funded research, including in cybersecurity through its affiliated Cyber Florida center. USF is a member of the State University System of Florida.
naics.justification: USF is a degree-granting public research university, the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting research university.

naics.description: Feeding America is a nationwide network of more than 200 member food banks that works to fight hunger in the United States. It sources, distributes, and coordinates donated food and grocery products to local food banks and pantries. The organization is a nonprofit charity headquartered in Chicago, Illinois.
naics.justification: Feeding America's primary activity is coordinating the collection and distribution of food to people in need, which is the defining activity of this code.

alternates.justification: It operates large-scale food warehousing and logistics as part of its distribution network.
It also channels donated resources similar to a grantmaking charity, though it is not primarily a foundation.
A generic social-services alternative given its broader anti-hunger mission.

naics.category_justification: Feeding America is a charitable nonprofit organization delivering hunger-relief services.

AHIMA is a membership-based nonprofit organization headquartered in Chicago.

Its members include a range of fintech firms and financial services technology providers.
naics.justification: The association's primary activity is representing member fintech companies' collective policy interests, the defining activity of this code.

naics.description: The MIT Shaping the Future of Work Initiative is a research program housed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology that studies how technology, including AI and automation, affects jobs, wages, and the labor market. It produces academic research and policy recommendations on labor market and technology issues. It operates as part of MIT's Sloan School of Management and broader research community.
naics.justification: As a research initiative housed within MIT, its NAICS code follows its parent university's primary activity of higher education and research.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The initiative's specific activity is labor-economics research, which could be classified as social science R&D if considered independently of MIT.

naics.description: Mayo Clinic Platform is a digital health and data initiative operated by Mayo Clinic, a nonprofit academic medical center. It develops AI-enabled tools, data-sharing infrastructure, and validation frameworks intended to support diagnostics and healthcare delivery in partnership with technology and data companies. It leverages Mayo Clinic's clinical data and expertise to advance health AI applications.
naics.justification: As a platform operated within Mayo Clinic, its NAICS code follows the parent hospital system's primary activity, even though the platform itself focuses on data and AI infrastructure.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Considered on its own, the platform's activity of hosting and processing health data resembles a computing infrastructure/data service.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: Mayo Clinic also operates extensive physician practices, a plausible alternate parent activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: The platform's AI validation work has an R&D character.

naics.description: The Danish Medicines Agency (Laegemiddelstyrelsen) is the Danish national government authority responsible for regulating and approving medicines and medical devices in Denmark. It oversees drug safety, clinical trials, and pharmaceutical licensing under the Danish Ministry of the Interior and Health. It is the Danish counterpart to agencies like the U.S. FDA.
naics.naics_title: Regulation, Licensing, and Inspection of Miscellaneous Commercial Sectors
naics.justification: The agency's primary activity is regulating and licensing pharmaceutical products for commercial distribution, matching this general regulatory code.

alternates.justification: Its work could also be viewed as administering national public health/drug-safety programs.
A more generic government economic-administration code.
Generic catch-all if neither regulatory nor public-health administration code fits precisely.

naics.category_justification: It is a national (Danish) government regulatory agency.

naics.resolved_name: Family Research Council's Center for Religious Liberty
naics.description: The Center for Religious Liberty is a program of the Family Research Council (FRC), a Washington, D.C.-based conservative Christian public policy and advocacy organization. The Center focuses on defending religious freedom domestically and internationally, including analyzing the effects of emerging technologies like AI on religious expression. It is led within FRC by a director focused on international religious freedom policy.
naics.justification: As a program of FRC, its NAICS code follows the parent organization's primary activity of public-policy advocacy on social and religious issues.

alternates.justification: Its focus on religious liberty gives it some character of a religious organization rather than a secular advocacy group.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: Generic catch-all alternative.
FRC engages in policy advocacy that borders on political activity, though it is not formally a political organization.

naics.category_justification: FRC is a mission-driven public-policy advocacy nonprofit, and this center is one of its internal programs.

naics.resolved_name: State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company
naics.description: State Farm is a large American insurance and financial services group best known for automobile, homeowners, and other property and casualty insurance, alongside life insurance and banking products. naics.naics_title: Direct Property and Casualty Insurance Carriers

naics.description: The Future Society and ForHumanity are two independent nonprofit organizations focused on AI governance and safety that jointly submitted comments to a federal AI policy docket. The Future Society is an international nonprofit that researches and advocates for responsible AI governance frameworks. ForHumanity is a nonprofit that develops independent audit criteria and certification schemes for assessing AI system risk.
naics.justification: Both organizations' primary activity is AI governance research and advocacy, best captured by a social advocacy organization code, though their joint filing introduces some ambiguity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: Both organizations also conduct policy and technical research on AI governance.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)

naics.category_justification: Both organizations are mission-driven nonprofits focused on AI governance research and advocacy rather than representing a dues-paying membership base.

naics.description: Aarhus University is a public research university in Aarhus, Denmark, one of the largest and most prominent universities in the country. It offers undergraduate and graduate degree programs across a wide range of disciplines and conducts extensive research, including in cryptography and computer science. It is a member of several international research consortia.
naics.justification: Aarhus University is a degree-granting public research university, the defining activity of this code.
naics.category_justification: It is a public, degree-granting research university.

naics.resolved_name: United States Copyright Office (Library of Congress)

It provides policy advice to Congress on domestic and international copyright issues and maintains public records of copyright registrations. It is led by the Register of Copyrights.
naics.justification: As a federal administrative office performing registration and policy-advisory functions rather than a more narrowly defined government activity, the general government support code is the best fit.

alternates.justification: Copyright administration relates to protecting intellectual property, an economic program function.

alternates.justification: Its name suggests carrier activity, but TIA itself is an association, not an operating carrier.

alternates.justification: TIA also develops technical standards, which could alternatively be framed under this residual professional-services code.
A closely related membership-association alternate, less specific than the business-associations code for an industry trade group.

naics.category_justification: TIA is a membership-based trade association representing the collective interests of telecommunications industry companies.

naics.description: EleutherAI is a nonprofit AI research institute originally formed as a grassroots collective in 2020 to conduct open, transparent research on large language models and other AI systems. It has released widely used open-source models and datasets (such as GPT-Neo/GPT-J and the Pile) and now operates as a nonprofit research organization funded by grants and donations. Its mission emphasizes open-source, interpretable, and accountable AI research rather than commercial product sales.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
naics.justification: EleutherAI's primary activity is conducting and publishing AI research, which is best captured by this general scientific-R&D code since NAICS has no dedicated computer-science-research code.

alternates.justification: Its work centers on building and releasing software/models, which could alternatively be framed under a software-development code.
A weak alternate if EleutherAI's role is understood primarily as a grant-funded organization rather than an active research producer.

alternates.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
alternates.justification: A less likely alternate given EleutherAI's outputs (models, datasets, papers) are not primarily an information-service product.

naics.category_justification: EleutherAI operates as a nonprofit research institute funded by grants, focused on open scientific research rather than a membership or commercial mission.

naics.description: Them Before Us is a nonprofit advocacy organization, founded in 2018 by Katy Faust, that promotes a child-centered view of marriage, family policy, and reproductive technology, arguing for children's right to be raised by their biological mother and father. It publishes books, policy scorecards, and commentary on issues such as surrogacy, donor conception, and no-fault divorce, and submitted comments on a federal AI action plan RFI framing family-policy concerns around AI. It operates as a mission-driven nonprofit advocacy group rather than a membership trade body or government entity.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is advocating for a specific family-policy and children's-rights position through publications and public commentary, matching this social-advocacy code.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
alternates.justification: The organization also produces policy research/scorecards, which could be framed as social-science R&D.
A general catch-all civic-organization code, less specific than the social-advocacy code chosen.
The organization publishes books as part of its advocacy, but publishing is not its defining primary activity.

naics.category_justification: Them Before Us is a mission-driven nonprofit advocacy organization rather than a membership trade association or government body.

naics.description: Rush University Medical Center is a large academic medical center in Chicago, Illinois, encompassing a hospital, Rush University (offering nursing, medical, and health-science degrees), and affiliated research programs. It provides comprehensive inpatient and outpatient clinical care while also training health professionals and conducting biomedical research. It operates as a nonprofit academic hospital system.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is operating a full-service acute-care hospital, matching this hospital code, even though it also includes a degree-granting university component.

alternates.justification: Rush University, its degree-granting arm, is a substantial and named part of the institution, making this a strong alternate primary activity.
Rush operates significant clinical and research laboratories, a secondary but less defining activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Rush conducts substantial biomedical research, though patient care remains its primary defining activity.

naics.category_justification: Rush operates as a nonprofit academic medical center; its hospital-delivery mission is treated as primary even though it also has a university component.

naics.description: cébé IT & Knowledge Management LLC is a small consulting firm founded in 2009 by Claude Baudoin, based in San Rafael, California, providing management and IT consulting services in areas such as IT strategy, enterprise architecture, cloud computing, and knowledge management. It also offers related training courses and workshops for business and technical audiences. It operates as a small, for-profit sole-owner-led consulting practice.
naics.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
naics.justification: The firm's primary activity is providing IT strategy, enterprise architecture, and management consulting services, matching this consulting code.

alternates.justification: Its IT strategy and enterprise-architecture consulting overlaps significantly with computer systems design services.
The firm also offers courses and workshops, a secondary but notable line of business.
A residual management-consulting code that could apply to its knowledge-management-specific advisory work.

naics.category_justification: It is a for-profit, privately owned consulting LLC.

naics.description: Michigan Medicine is the academic medical center of the University of Michigan, comprising hospitals, health centers, and the University of Michigan Medical School. It provides clinical patient care while also training medical students and residents and conducting biomedical research. It operates as part of a large public research university's health system.
naics.justification: As the academic medical center of a public research university, its overarching parent activity is degree-granting higher education, matching this code even though it also delivers extensive hospital care.

alternates.justification: Michigan Medicine's day-to-day primary activity is operating hospitals and clinics providing patient care, a strong alternate primary-activity code.
It operates substantial clinical and research laboratories, a secondary activity.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Michigan Medicine conducts substantial biomedical research, though patient care and education remain more defining.

naics.category_justification: Michigan Medicine is the health system of the University of Michigan, a public university, though its hospital operations also support a nonprofit/hospital framing.

naics.resolved_name: Medical Imaging & Technology Alliance (a division of the National Electrical Manufacturers Association)
naics.description: The Medical Imaging & Technology Alliance (MITA) is a trade association, operating as a division of the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA), representing manufacturers of medical imaging equipment, radiopharmaceuticals, and related diagnostic technologies. It advocates on regulatory, reimbursement, and AI-related standards issues affecting the medical imaging industry and has submitted comments on NIST's AI Risk Management Framework. It is a membership-based trade association rather than a manufacturer itself.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is representing and advocating for medical imaging equipment manufacturers' collective interests, matching the business-association code.

alternates.justification: MITA's member companies manufacture imaging/irradiation equipment, though MITA itself does not manufacture anything.
A similarly member-related manufacturing code, ruled out since MITA is an association rather than a manufacturer.
A closely related alternate membership-association code, less specific than the business-associations code for an industry trade group.

naics.category_justification: MITA is a membership trade association representing medical imaging technology manufacturers, and is explicitly organized as a division of NEMA.

naics.description: "EFCA" is an acronym shared by multiple distinct organizations (such as the Evangelical Free Church of America, various engineering/consulting federations, and other groups), and web research could not confidently determine which specific entity filed this AI-related comment given only the bare acronym. Without further identifying context, the specific organization cannot be verified.
naics.justification: Without confirming which "EFCA" filed the comment, a low-confidence general-advocacy code is offered as a placeholder rather than a confirmed classification.

alternates.justification: One prominent organization using this acronym (Evangelical Free Church of America) is a religious denomination, a plausible but unconfirmed alternate.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Some engineering/consulting federations also use this acronym, a plausible but unconfirmed alternate.
A low-confidence fallback given the complete ambiguity of the acronym.

naics.category_justification: The bare acronym "EFCA" matches multiple unrelated organizations, and web research could not confirm which one filed this comment.

naics.description: Substack is a for-profit online platform that enables independent writers and podcasters to publish newsletters and audio/video content and monetize it through paid subscriptions. It provides publishing tools, payment processing, and audience-building features to its creators while taking a percentage of subscription revenue. It is a private technology company rather than a media outlet with its own editorial staff.
naics.naics_title: Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services
naics.justification: Substack's primary activity is operating an online content-hosting and distribution platform for independent publishers, which is best captured by this general information-services code.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: Substack's core function is hosting and serving content for its creators, closely matching web-hosting/computing-infrastructure services.
Substack facilitates newsletter (periodical-like) publishing, though it is the platform rather than the publisher of the content itself.
A less likely alternate if Substack were characterized primarily by its software development activity rather than the platform service it provides.

naics.category_justification: Substack is a privately held, for-profit technology company.

naics.description: The American Academy of Dermatology is the largest professional membership association of dermatologists in the United States, representing physicians who diagnose and treat skin, hair, and nail conditions. It develops clinical practice guidelines, provides continuing medical education, and advocates on health policy issues affecting dermatologic care, including AI-related regulatory comments. It is a membership-based professional association rather than a direct healthcare provider.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is representing and advocating for dermatologist members and setting practice guidelines, matching the professional-organizations code.

alternates.justification: Its health-policy advocacy overlaps with general social advocacy organizations.

alternates.naics_title: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
alternates.justification: Ruled out; the Academy itself does not provide direct patient care.
A less precise catch-all membership code, ruled out in favor of the more specific professional-organizations code.

naics.category_justification: It is a membership-based professional association representing dermatologists' collective interests.

naics.description: LatentView Analytics is a publicly traded, India-founded (with major U.S. presence) data analytics and consulting company that provides data engineering, business analytics, and AI-driven consulting services to enterprise clients, including many Fortune 500 companies, across sectors such as technology, financial services, retail, and healthcare. Founded in 2006 by Venkat Viswanathan and Pramod Jandhyala, it has grown into an international analytics consultancy. It is a for-profit professional services company.
naics.justification: LatentView's core activity is building custom data analytics, data engineering, and AI solutions for clients, closely matching custom software/programming services.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: LatentView also provides broader business and management consulting services alongside its technical analytics work.
Its data-engineering and systems-integration work overlaps substantially with computer systems design services.

alternates.naics_title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
alternates.justification: A less likely alternate if its activity were characterized as data processing/hosting rather than consulting and custom development.

naics.category_justification: LatentView Analytics is a publicly traded, for-profit consulting and technology services company.

naics.resolved_name: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program Management Office (General Services Administration)
naics.description: The FedRAMP Program Management Office is the U.S. federal government office, housed within the General Services Administration, that administers the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program, a standardized approach to security assessment and authorization for cloud products used by federal agencies. It develops and enforces cloud-security authorization requirements for cloud service providers seeking to sell to the federal government. It is a federal government office rather than a private company or nonprofit.
naics.justification: The FedRAMP PMO's primary activity is administering a federal regulatory/certification program governing cloud service providers, matching this government-administration code.

alternates.justification: A general government-support code that could apply if the office is framed as internal federal administrative support rather than economic-program regulation.

alternates.naics_title: Regulation, Licensing, and Inspection of Miscellaneous Commercial Sectors
alternates.justification: An alternate regulatory-administration code given FedRAMP's role in certifying/licensing cloud providers for government use.
FedRAMP's work concerns cloud/IT security assessment, but the PMO itself performs regulatory administration rather than delivering IT services.

naics.category_justification: The FedRAMP PMO is a federal government office within GSA.

naics.description: The AI Policy Network is a bipartisan advocacy organization, registered as a 501(c)(4) and led by Executive Director Daniel Colson, that engages Congress, federal officials, and the media to promote AI policy focused on national security, economic competitiveness, and technological leadership. It employs staff with backgrounds in Congress, the Pentagon's AI policy office, and major technology companies, and is a registered federal lobbying entity. It is a mission-driven advocacy organization rather than a membership trade body or company.
naics.justification: The organization's primary activity is advocacy and lobbying on AI policy issues before Congress and federal agencies, matching this social-advocacy code.

alternates.justification: Its close engagement with the technology industry on AI policy gives it some characteristics of an industry-coordinating association.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
alternates.justification: A residual professional-services code that could apply to its policy-research and advisory outputs.

alternates.naics_title: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
alternates.justification: A general catch-all nonprofit code, less specific than the social-advocacy code chosen.

naics.category_justification: As a 501(c)(4) social-welfare advocacy organization rather than a membership body representing an industry or professional group, it best fits the nonprofit category, though its policy-coalition-like advocacy role also makes trade/coalition organization plausible.

naics.description: Mattiq is a Chicago-based, venture-backed startup founded in 2020 that spun out of Northwestern University research to combine high-throughput nanomaterial synthesis with AI/machine learning for rapid materials discovery. Its work focuses on sustainable chemicals, fuels, and nanomaterials, including catalysts aimed at decarbonizing hard-to-abate industries. The company submitted a public comment supporting the America's AI Action Plan to OSTP/NIST.
naics.justification: Mattiq's core activity is R&D combining AI-driven materials discovery with nanomaterial synthesis ("megalibraries") to develop new catalysts and materials, which is the defining activity of the nanotechnology R&D code rather than general physical-science R&D (which explicitly excludes nanotechnology) or manufacturing, since the company is still at the discovery/platform stage.

alternates.naics_title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
alternates.justification: Mattiq's R&D spans broader physical/chemical science, but this code explicitly excludes nanotechnology, which is central to Mattiq's stated approach.

alternates.naics_title: All Other Basic Organic Chemical Manufacturing
alternates.justification: Mattiq's eventual goal is commercial chemicals/materials production, but current public information describes it as a discovery-stage R&D and platform company, not a manufacturer.

alternates.naics_title: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
alternates.justification: The company could be seen as providing technical/scientific consulting via its AI-materials platform, but this undersells its direct R&D activity.

naics.category_justification: Mattiq is a private, venture-funded for-profit startup commenting on AI policy in its own capacity as a company.

naics.resolved_name: Future of Privacy Forum's Israel Tech Policy Institute
naics.description: The Israel Tech Policy Institute (ITPI) is a Tel Aviv-based policy think tank founded in 2018 that convenes multi-stakeholder workshops and produces research on technology policy topics including AI/ML, privacy, digital health, cybersecurity, and smart mobility. It is the Israeli affiliate office of the U.S.-based nonprofit Future of Privacy Forum, operating under the branding "FPF - Israel Tech Policy Institute." It states that it does not engage in lobbying in Israel or abroad, focusing instead on research and convening.
naics.naics_title: Research and Development in the Social Sciences and Humanities
naics.justification: ITPI's primary activity is producing policy research and convening multi-stakeholder discussions on technology and privacy issues, which fits social-science-oriented R&D/policy research better than an advocacy-specific code, though think tanks often straddle multiple NAICS categories.

alternates.justification: If ITPI's convening and public-facing policy output is viewed primarily as advocacy rather than research output, this social advocacy code would apply instead.
ITPI is not a membership-based professional association, making this a weaker fit despite some overlap in policy-convening activity.

alternates.naics_title: Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
alternates.justification: Unlikely fit; ITPI's output is research/advocacy rather than management consulting, but included as a distant alternate given policy-advisory overlap.

naics.category_justification: ITPI is the Israeli office of the Future of Privacy Forum, a nonprofit think tank, and functions as a mission-driven research and convening body rather than a membership/advocacy trade group or government entity.

naics.description: The University at Buffalo (UB) is a public research university and the largest campus in the State University of New York (SUNY) system, offering undergraduate and graduate degree programs and conducting research across many fields including AI.
naics.justification: UB is a public research university, exactly matching this education-services code.
naics.category_justification: The University at Buffalo is a public state university.

naics.description: The Greater New York Hospital Association (GNYHA) is a nonprofit trade association representing over 150 hospitals and health systems in the New York metropolitan area and beyond, advocating on healthcare policy and regulatory issues, including AI use in healthcare.
naics.justification: GNYHA's core activity is representing and advocating for its membership of hospitals and health systems, matching this professional/membership-association code.

alternates.justification: GNYHA's healthcare-sector focus overlaps with this voluntary-health-organization code.
GNYHA engages in substantial policy advocacy on behalf of members, overlapping with this code.
Not applicable; GNYHA is a membership association, not a hospital operator itself.

naics.category_justification: GNYHA is a membership-based hospital trade association.

naics.description: The Open Source Initiative (OSI) is a nonprofit organization that maintains and stewards the Open Source Definition, reviews and approves open source software licenses, and advocates for open source principles, including in the context of open-source AI models.
naics.justification: OSI's core activity is standards-stewardship and advocacy for open source software principles, closest to this social-advocacy code given no NAICS code specific to software-licensing standards bodies.

alternates.justification: OSI functions partly as a professional/community standards body for the open source software community.
Weak fit; OSI stewards licensing standards rather than building software for clients.
Weak fit; too generic relative to the more specific social-advocacy code.

naics.category_justification: OSI is a mission-driven nonprofit standards and advocacy organization.
